title: 145 Constitution of Tribunal—general rule
zh: 第145條 法庭組成－一般規則
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies:
(1) 本條適用：
(a) in relation to a proceeding for review of a decision in the Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area; and
(a) 與情報和安全管轄範圍內的決定審查程序有關；和
(b) instead of section 39 (general rules for constitution of Tribunal).
(b) 代替第 39 條（法庭組成的一般規則）。
Note: Section 39 continues to apply in relation to incidental and ancillary proceedings, such those dealing with costs and extensions of time.
註：第 39 條繼續適用於附帶和附屬程序，例如涉及費用和延長時間的程序。
Constitution of Tribunal—general rule
法庭組成－一般規則
(2) The Tribunal must be constituted for the purposes of the proceeding by:
(2) 為了訴訟目的，仲裁庭必須由下列人員組成：
(a) the President; or
(a) 主席；或
(b) a Deputy President; or
(b) 一位副主席；或
(c) 3 members, at least one of whom is the President or a Deputy President.
(c) 3 名成員，其中至少一名為主席或副主席。
Note: For constitution of the Tribunal, see Division 4 of Part 4 (constitution of Tribunal for a proceeding), and for reconstitution of the Tribunal, see Subdivision D of that Division.
註：有關法庭的組成，請參閱第 4 部分第 4 分部（訴訟程序的法庭組成），有關法庭的重組，請參閱該分部的 D 分部。
Presiding member
主持委員
(3) If the Tribunal is constituted for the purposes of the proceeding by 3 members, the presiding member must be:
(3) 如果仲裁庭由 3 名成員組成，則首席成員必須是：
(a) if the President is one of the members—the President; or
(a) 若主席是成員之一－主席；或
(b) if the President is not one of the members but one or more Judges are—the most senior (or only) Judge; or
(b) 若主席不是成員之一，而是一名或多名法官－最資深（或唯一）的法官；或
(c) if paragraphs (a) and (b) do not apply—a Deputy President.
(c) 如 (a) 及 (b) 款不適用－一名副主席。
Avoiding conflicts of interest—members who were agency heads
避免利益衝突－擔任機構負責人的成員
(4) However, none of the members can be a person who is, or was, the head of an agency within the national intelligence community if:
(4) 但是，在下列情況下，任何成員都不能擔任或曾經擔任國家情報界機構的負責人：
(a) in any case—the agency is a party to the proceeding; or
(a) 在任何情況下－該機構是訴訟的一方；或者
(b) if the review relates to an exempt security record decision—the document or record concerned originated with, or was received from, the agency.
(b) 如果審查涉及豁免安全記錄決定－相關文件或記錄源自該機構或從該機構收到。
Avoiding conflicts of interest—members who were certain Ministers
避免利益衝突－擔任某些部長的成員
(5) In addition, none of the members can be a person who was:
(5) 另外，任何成員都不能是下列人員：
(a) in any case—the Treasurer; or
(a) 在任何情況下－財務主管；或
(b) the Minister responsible for an agency within the national intelligence community if:
(b) 負責國家情報界機構的部長，如果：
(i) the agency is a party to the proceeding; or
(i) 該機構是訴訟的一方；或
(ii) if the review relates to an exempt security record decision—the document or record concerned originated with, or was received from, the agency.
(ii) 如果審查涉及豁免安全記錄決定－相關文件或記錄源自該機構或從該機構收到。

title: 147 Parties to proceedings
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies:
(1) 本條適用：
(a) in relation to a proceeding for review of an intelligence and security decision; and
(a) 與情報和安全決定審查程序有關；和
(b) instead of the following provisions:
(b) 代替下列規定：
(i) unless the decision is an exempt security record decision—section 22 (parties to proceeding for review);
(i) 除非該決定是豁免安全記錄決定－第 22 條（審查程序的各方）；
(ii) section 60 (decision ‑ makers may elect not to participate in kind of proceeding or Tribunal case event);
(ii) 第 60 條（決策者可以選擇不參與某種訴訟或法庭案件活動）；
(iii) section 61 (decision ‑ maker who elects not to participate may be a non ‑ participating party to proceeding or Tribunal case event);
(iii) 第 61 條（選擇不參與的決策者可能是訴訟程序或法庭案件活動的非參與者）；
(iv) section 65 (certain parties may seek to withdraw from being a party);
(iv) 第 65 條（某些當事人可以尋求退出當事人身分）；
(v) section 83 (Tribunal may remove party from proceeding if party fails to appear or does not comply).
(v) 第 83 條（如果當事人未出庭或不遵守規定，仲裁庭可以將當事人從訴訟程序中剔除）。
Parties to proceedings
訴訟當事人
(2) The parties to a proceeding for review of a decision mentioned in column 1 of an item in the following table are the persons mentioned in column 2 of the item.
(2)下表中第1欄所指決定複核程序的當事人為該欄第2欄所指人員。

訴訟當事人
項目 |第 1 欄決定 |第 2 欄 訴訟當事人
1 |犯罪情報評估|申請人澳洲犯罪委員會首席執行官
2 |海外收購及收購決策|申請人 財務主管

title: 148 Certain hearings must be held in private
zh: 148 某些聽證會必須非公開舉行
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies in relation to a proceeding that relates to an intelligence and security decision, other than an exempt security record decision.
(1) 本節適用於與情報和安全決定相關的訴訟，但豁免安全記錄決定除外。
(2) This section applies subject to:
(2) 本條適用於：
(a) section 149 (persons entitled to be present at hearings); and
(a) 第 149 條（有權出席聽證會的人員）；和
(b) section 158 (security certificates—responsible Minister).
(b) 第 158 條（安全證明書－責任部長）。
Hearings to be held in private
聽證會非公開舉行
(3) The hearing of the proceeding must be held in private.
(3) 訴訟聽證必須非公開進行。
(4) The Tribunal may, by order, give directions in relation to the persons who may be present at the hearing.
(4) 仲裁庭可以透過命令，就可能出席聽證會的人員發出指示。

title: 149 Persons entitled to be present at hearings
zh: 第149章 有權出席聽證會的人
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies:
(1) 本條適用：
(a) in relation to a proceeding for review of an intelligence and security decision; and
(a) 與情報和安全決定審查程序有關；和
(b) subject to section 158 (security certificates—responsible Minister).
(b) 遵守第 158 條（安全證書－責任部長）。
Persons entitled to be present
有權出席的人士
(2) The applicant, and the applicant’s representative, are entitled to be present at the hearing of the proceeding when the Tribunal hears submissions made, or evidence adduced by:
(2) 申請人及其代表有權在仲裁庭聽取以下人員提出的意見或提出的證據時出席訴訟聽證會：
(a) the agency head (or representative); or
(a) 機構負責人（或代表）；或
(b) a relevant body.
(b) 相關機構。
(3) The following are entitled to be present at the hearing of the proceeding when the Tribunal hears submissions made, or evidence adduced by the applicant (or representative):
(3) 當仲裁庭聽取申請人（或代表）提出的意見或提出的證據時，以下人員有權出席訴訟聽證會：
(a) the agency head (or representative);
(a) 機構負責人（或代表）；
(b) a relevant body.
(b) 相關機構。

title: 150 Relevant bodies may adduce evidence and make submissions
zh: 第150章 相關機構可以舉證並提出意見
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies in relation to a proceeding for review of an intelligence and security decision.
(1) 本節適用於情報和安全決定審查程序。
Relevant bodies may adduce evidence and make submissions
有關機構可舉證並提出意見
(2) A relevant body:
（二）相關機構：
(a) is entitled to adduce evidence and make submissions in the proceeding; and
(a) 有權在訴訟程序中舉證並提出意見；和
(b) for the purposes of the following sections, is taken to be a party to the proceeding:
(b) 就以下各節而言，被視為訴訟的一方：
(i) section 56 (parties and their representatives to assist Tribunal);
(i) 第 56 條（協助仲裁庭的當事人及其代表）；
(ii) section 66 (representation before Tribunal);
(ii) 第 66 條（出庭代表）；
(iii) section 79 (Tribunal may give directions in relation to procedure for a proceeding);
(iii) 第 79 條（仲裁庭可就訴訟程序發出指示）；
(iv) section 151 (order of evidence and submissions);
(iv) 第 151 條（證據順序和提交資料）；
(v) section 152 (opportunity for further evidence and submissions).
(v) 第 152 條（提供進一步證據和意見的機會）。

title: 151 Order of evidence and submissions
zh: 第151條 證據和陳詞的順序
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies in relation to a proceeding for review of an intelligence and security decision.
(1) 本節適用於情報和安全決定審查程序。
Order of presentation
演示順序
(2) Unless it determines otherwise, the Tribunal must hear initial evidence and submissions from the parties to the proceeding in the following order:
(2) 除非另有決定，仲裁庭必須依下列順序聽取訴訟各方的初步證據和陳述：
(a) first—evidence adduced and submissions made by the agency head;
(a) 首先－機構負責人提出的證據和意見；
(b) second—evidence adduced and submissions made by relevant bodies;
(b) 第二－有關機構提出的證據和提交的意見；
(c) third—evidence adduced and submissions made by the applicant.
(c) 第三－申請人提出的證據和陳述。

title: 152 Opportunity for further evidence and submissions
zh: 152 提供進一步證據和意見的機會
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies in relation to a proceeding for review of an intelligence and security decision.
(1) 本節適用於情報和安全決定審查程序。
Further evidence and submissions
進一步的證據和意見
(2) The Tribunal must give a party to the proceeding an opportunity to adduce further evidence and make further submissions in relation to the further evidence if:
(2) 在下列情況下，仲裁庭必須給予訴訟一方提供進一步證據並就進一步證據提出進一步意見的機會：
(a) the party presents the party’s case to the Tribunal; and
(a) 當事人向仲裁庭陳述當事人的案件；和
(b) after that case is presented, another party adduces evidence; and
(b) 案情陳述後，另一方當事人提出證據；和
(c) the Tribunal considers that, because of evidence adduced by the other party, the first ‑ mentioned party should be further heard.
(c) 仲裁庭認為，由於另一方提出了證據，應進一步聽取首先提到的一方的意見。
(3) To avoid doubt, the Tribunal must not give the applicant particulars of evidence or a submission in contravention of another provision of this Act that prohibits or restricts the disclosure of those particulars.
(3) 為避免疑義，仲裁庭不得向申請人提供證據詳情或提交的資料，以違反本法禁止或限制披露這些詳情的其他條款。

title: 153 Tribunal may invite person to give evidence
zh: 第153條 審裁處可邀請某人提供證據
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies in relation to a proceeding in the Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area.
(1) 本節適用於情報和安全管轄範圍內的訴訟。
Tribunal may invite person to give evidence
審裁處可邀請某人提供證據
(2) The Tribunal may, on its own initiative and at any stage of the proceeding, invite a person to give evidence.
(2) 仲裁庭可在訴訟程序的任何階段主動邀請某人提供證據。

title: 154 Certain processes not available
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies in relation to an intelligence and security decision, other than an exempt security record decision.
(1) 本節適用於情報和安全決定，但豁免安全記錄決定除外。
Dispute resolution
爭議解決
(2) Subdivision C of Division 6 of Part 4 (dispute resolution processes) does not apply in relation to a proceeding for review of the decision.
(2) 第 4 部分第 6 節 C 分節（爭議解決程序）不適用於決定複審程序。

title: 155 Guidance and appeals panel
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies in relation to an intelligence and security decision.
(1) 本節適用於情報和安全決定。
Guidance and appeals panel
指導和上訴小組
(2) Part 5 (guidance and appeals panel) does not apply in relation to:
(2) 第 5 部分（指導與上訴小組）不適用於：
(a) an application for review of the decision; or
(a) 覆核決定的申請；或
(b) a decision of the Tribunal on review of the decision.
(b) 仲裁庭對該決定進行審查的決定。

title: Division 4 — Disclosure of information
zh: 第 4 分部 — 資訊揭露
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area

title: 156 Duty of Tribunal in relation to security and law enforcement information
zh: 156 仲裁庭在安全和執法資訊方面的職責
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies in relation to a proceeding in the Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area.
(1) 本節適用於情報和安全管轄範圍內的訴訟。
Duty to protect security and law enforcement information
保護安全和執法資訊的義務
(2) It is the duty of the Tribunal, even though there may be no relevant certificate under this or any other Act, to ensure, so far as possible, that information is not communicated or made available to a person if that communication or availability would prejudice:
(2) 即使根據本法或任何其他法案可能沒有相關證書，仲裁庭也有責任盡可能確保資訊不會被傳達或提供給任何人，如果資訊的傳達或可用性會損害：
(a) the security, defence or international relations of the Commonwealth; or
(a) 英聯邦的安全、國防或國際關係；或
(b) law enforcement or intelligence interests.
(b) 執法或情報利益。

title: 157 Restricting publication or disclosure of information
zh: 157 限制資訊的發布或揭露
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies:
(1) 本條適用：
(a) in relation to a proceeding in the Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area; and
(a) 與情報和安全管轄範圍內的訴訟有關；和
(b) in addition to:
(b) 另外：
(i) section 70 (Tribunal may restrict publication or disclosure of information); and
(i) 第 70 條（仲裁庭可以限制資訊的發布或揭露）；和
(ii) section 71 (requirements for Tribunal orders about hearings, publication and disclosure).
(ii) 第 71 條（法庭關於聽證會、公佈和披露的命令的要求）。
Orders restricting publication or disclosure of information
限制發布或揭露資訊的命令
(2) In considering whether to make an order under section 70 restricting publication or other disclosure of information, the Tribunal must:
(2) 在考慮是否根據第 70 條下達命令限制公開或以其他方式披露資訊時，仲裁庭必須：
(a) in any case—have regard to the necessity of avoiding the disclosure of national security information; and
(a) 在任何情況下－考慮避免揭露國家安全資訊的必要性；和
(b) if the proceeding is for review of an intelligence and security decision—give particular weight to any submission made by, or on behalf of, the agency head.
(b) 如果程序是為了審查情報和安全決定－特別重視由機構負責人或代表機構負責人提出的任何意見。
Orders restricting publication or disclosure of findings
限制公佈或揭露調查結果的命令
(3) The Tribunal may, by order, give directions prohibiting or restricting the publication or other disclosure of the whole or any part of its findings in the proceeding.
(3) 仲裁庭可以透過命令發出指示，禁止或限制公佈或以其他方式揭露其訴訟結果的全部或任何部分。
Note: Breach of a non ‑ publication or non ‑ disclosure order is an offence (see section 119).
註：違反不公開或不揭露命令屬於犯罪行為（參閱第 119 條）。

title: 158 Security certificates—responsible Minister
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies in relation to a proceeding for review of an intelligence and security decision, other than an exempt security record decision.
(1) 本節適用於審查情報和安全決定的程序，但豁免安全記錄決定除外。
(2) This section applies in relation to evidence to be adduced or a submission to be made by or on behalf of any of the following:
(2) 本條適用於以下任何人或其代表提出的證據或提交的資料：
(a) the agency head;
(a) 機構負責人；
(b) a relevant body;
(b) 相關機構；
(c) an officer or employee of the agency head’s agency;
(c) 機構領導機構的官員或員工；
(d) an officer or employee of a relevant body;
(d) 相關機構的官員或僱員；
(e) a person connected with the agency or a relevant body.
(e) 與該機構或相關機構有關的人員。
Security certificates by responsible Ministers
負責部長的安全證書
(3) The responsible Minister may certify, in writing, that disclosing the evidence or making the submission would be contrary to the public interest because it would prejudice:
(3) 負責部長可以書面證明披露證據或提交意見將違反公共利益，因為它會損害：
(a) in any case—the security, defence or international relations of the Commonwealth; or
(a) 在任何情況下－英聯邦的安全、國防或國際關係；或
(b) in the case of a criminal intelligence assessment decision—law enforcement or intelligence interests.
(b) 在刑事情報評估決定的情況下－執法或情報利益。
(4) If the responsible Minister so certifies, when the evidence is adduced or the submission is made:
(4) 若負責部長如此證明，則在提出證據或提出意見時：
(a) the applicant must not be present; and
(a) 申請人不得在場；和
(b) the applicant’s representative must not be present except with the consent of the responsible Minister.
(b) 除非得到負責部長的同意，否則申請人的代表不得出席。
(5) A certificate under this section is not a legislative instrument.
(5) 本條規定的證書不是立法文書。
Delegation—security clearance decisions and security clearance suitability assessments
授權－安全審查決定和安全審查適用性評估
(6) The ASIO Minister may, in writing, delegate the ASIO Minister’s power under subsection (3) in relation to a security clearance decision or a security clearance suitability assessment to:
(6) ASIO 部長可以書面形式將第 (3) 款規定的 ASIO 部長有關安全許可決定或安全許可適宜性評估的權力委託給：
(a) the Director ‑ General of Security; or
(a) 安全局長；或
(b) an ASIO employee (within the meaning of the ASIO Act), or an ASIO affiliate (within the meaning of that Act), who holds, or is acting in, a position in ASIO that is equivalent to or higher than a position occupied by an SES employee.
(b) 在 ASIO 中擔任或正在擔任與 SES 員工同等或更高職位的 ASIO 員工（根據 ASIO 法案的含義）或 ASIO 附屬機構（根據該法案的含義）。
(7) In exercising a power under the delegation, the delegate must comply with any written directions of the ASIO Minister.
(7) 在行使授權下的權力時，代表必須遵守 ASIO 部長的任何書面指示。
Offence
進攻
(8) An applicant’s representative commits an offence if:
(8) 申請人代表犯有下列行為：
(a) a certificate is given under subsection (3) in relation to evidence or a submission; and
(a) 根據第 (3) 款提供與證據或提交資料有關的證書；和
(b) the representative is present when the evidence is adduced or the submission is made; and
(b) 舉證或提出陳述時，代表在場；和
(c) the representative discloses the evidence, or any information that was part of the submission, to the applicant or to any other person.
(c) 代表向申請人或任何其他人揭露證據或提交資料中的任何資訊。
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years.
刑罰：監禁2年。

title: 159 Sensitive information certificates—Director ‑ General of Security
zh: 159 敏感資訊證書－安全總監
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies in relation to a proceeding for review of:
(1) 本條適用於下列事項的審查程序：
(a) a security clearance decision; or
(a) 安全審查決定；或
(b) a security clearance suitability assessment.
(b) 安全許可適宜性評估。
Sensitive information certificates
敏感資訊證書
(2) The Director ‑ General of Security or a person authorised by the Director ‑ General under this section may certify, in writing, that, in the opinion of the Director ‑ General or authorised person, disclosure of information (the sensitive information ) contained in a document given to the Tribunal by the Director ‑ General in relation to a proceeding:
(2) 安全局長或局長根據本條授權的人可以書面證明，根據局長或授權人員的意見，局長向法庭提供的與訴訟有關的文件中包含的資訊（敏感資訊）的披露：
(a) would be contrary to the public interest for one or more of the following reasons:
(a) 因以下一個或多個原因而違反公共利益：
(i) the disclosure would prejudice the security, defence or international relations of the Commonwealth;
(i) 揭露會損害英聯邦的安全、國防或國際關係；
(ii) the disclosure would reveal information that has been disclosed to the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation in confidence;
(ii) 該披露將洩露已秘密向澳洲安全情報組織披露的資訊；
(iii) any other reason that could form the basis for a claim by the Crown in right of the Commonwealth in a judicial proceeding that the sensitive information or the matter contained in the document should not be disclosed; or
(iii) 可能構成英國政府在司法程序中主張不應披露敏感資訊或文件中所含事項的依據的任何其他原因；或
(b) could reveal the methodology underlying a psychological assessment of the person who applied for the decision or assessment.
(b) 可以揭示對申請決定或評估的人進行心理評估的方法。
(3) A certificate under subsection (2) is not a legislative instrument.
(3) 第 (2) 款規定的證書不是立法文件。
Effect of certificate
證書效力
(4) If a certificate is given under subsection (2), the Tribunal must do all things necessary to ensure that the sensitive information is not disclosed to the applicant or any person other than:
(4) 若依第 (2) 款提供證書，仲裁庭必須採取一切必要措施，確保敏感資訊不會洩漏給申請人或除以下人員以外的任何人：
(a) the Director ‑ General of Security or the Director ‑ General’s representative; or
(a) 安全局長或局長代表；或
(b) a member in the course of the performance of the member’s duties; or
(b) 會員在履行其職責過程中；或
(c) the Principal Registrar in the course of the performance of the Principal Registrar’s duties; or
(c) 首席書記官在履行首席書記官職責期間；或
(d) a staff member in the course of the performance of the staff member’s duties.
(d) 工作人員在履行其職責過程中。
(5) However, subsection (4) does not apply in relation to disclosure to the applicant or a person representing the applicant to the extent that the information:
(5) 但是，第 (4) 款不適用於向申請人或代表申請人的人員揭露以下資訊：
(a) has already been lawfully disclosed to the applicant; or
(a) 已合法地向申請人揭露；或
(b) is disclosed to the applicant with the consent of the Director ‑ General of Security.
(b) 經安全總監同意後向申請人揭露。
Authorisations
授權
(6) The Director ‑ General of Security may, in writing, authorise a person for the purposes of this section if the person is an ASIO employee (within the meaning of the ASIO Act), or an ASIO affiliate (within the meaning of that Act), who holds, or is acting in, a position in ASIO that is equivalent to or higher than a position occupied by an SES employee.
(6) 如果某人是 ASIO 僱員（在 ASIO 法案的含義內）或 ASIO 附屬機構（在該法案的含義內），且在 ASIO 中擔任或正在擔任的職位相當於或高於 SES 僱員的職位，則安全總監可以出於本節的目的以書面形式授權該人。

title: 160 Protecting identities of persons giving evidence
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies in relation to a proceeding in the Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area.
(1) 本節適用於情報和安全管轄範圍內的訴訟。
Protecting identities
保護身分
(2) The Tribunal must do all things necessary to ensure that the identity of a person is not revealed if:
(2) 在下列情況下，仲裁庭必須採取一切必要措施確保個人身分不會外洩：
(a) the person gives, or is to give, evidence on behalf of an agency within the national intelligence community; and
(a) 該人代表國家情報界的某個機構提供或將提供證據；和
(b) the head of the agency requests that the identity of the person is not revealed.
(b) 該機構負責人要求不透露該人的身分。

title: 161 Public interest certificates—responsible Minister
zh: 161 公共利益證明書－責任部長
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies:
(1) 本條適用：
(a) in relation to a proceeding for review of an intelligence and security decision, other than an exempt security record decision; and
(a) 與審查情報和安全決定的程序有關，但豁免安全記錄決定除外；和
(b) instead of the following provisions:
(b) 代替下列規定：
(i) section 91 (disclosure of information—public interest certificate);
(i) 第 91 條（資訊揭露－公共利益證明）；
(ii) section 92 (Attorney ‑ General may intervene for public interest reasons);
(ii) 第 92 條（總檢察長可以出於公共利益原因進行幹預）；
(iii) section 112 (notice of decision and statement of reasons—other proceedings) to the extent that it would apply in relation anything done under this section.
(iii) 第 112 條（決定通知和理由說明－其他程序），只要它適用於根據本條所做的任何事情。
Public interest certificate
公益證明
(2) The responsible Minister may certify, in writing, that the disclosure of specified information, or the content of a specified document, in the proceeding would be contrary to the public interest for one or more of the following reasons:
(2) 負責部長可以書面證明，由於以下一個或多個原因，在訴訟程序中披露特定資訊或特定文件的內容將違背公共利益：
(a) the disclosure would prejudice the security, defence or international relations of the Commonwealth;
(a) 揭露會損害英聯邦的安全、國防或國際關係；
(b) the disclosure would involve the disclosure of deliberations or decisions of the Cabinet or of a Committee of the Cabinet;
(b) 揭露涉及內閣或內閣委員會的審議或決定的揭露；
(c) if the proceeding is for review of a criminal intelligence assessment—the disclosure would prejudice law enforcement or intelligence interests;
(c) 如果程序是為了審查刑事情報評估－披露將損害執法或情報利益；
(d) any other reason that could form the basis for a claim by the Crown in right of the Commonwealth in a judicial proceeding that the information or the matter contained in the document should not be disclosed.
(d) 可能構成英國政府在司法程序中主張不應披露文件中包含的資訊或事項的依據的任何其他原因。
(3) A certificate under subsection (2) is not a legislative instrument.
(3) 第 (2) 款規定的證書不是立法文件。
Effect of certificate
證書效力
(4) If a certificate is given under subsection (2) in relation to information or a document, a person is not excused from disclosing the information, or giving the document, to the Tribunal for the purposes of the proceeding if the person is required by or under this Act to do so.
(4) 如果根據第 (2) 款提供了與資訊或文件有關的證明，則該人不得因本法要求或根據本法要求向法庭披露該資訊或向法庭提供該文件以進行訴訟。
(5) However, the Tribunal must do all things necessary to ensure that:
(5) 然而，仲裁庭必須採取一切必要措施以確保：
(a) subject to subsection (6), the information or document is not disclosed or given to any person other than:
(a) 依第 (6) 款，資訊或文件不得揭露或提供給下列任何人：
(i) a member in the course of the performance of the member’s duties; or
(i) 會員在執行會員職務的過程中；或
(ii) the Principal Registrar in the course of the performance of the Principal Registrar’s duties; or
(ii) 首席書記官長在履行首席書記官長職責期間；或
(iii) a staff member in the course of the performance of the staff member’s duties; and
(iii) 工作人員在履行其職責過程中；和
(b) in the case of a document given to the Tribunal by an agency head—the document is returned, to the agency from which it came, as soon as practicable after the Tribunal has finished considering the document.
(b) 對於由機構負責人向仲裁庭提供的文件－在仲裁庭完成該文件的審議後，在切實可行的範圍內盡快將該文件退還給其來源機構。
Tribunal may allow disclosure in limited cases
仲裁庭可以在有限的情況下允許披露
(6) The Tribunal may decide to make the information or document available to any or all of the parties to the proceeding if the certificate does not specify the reason set out in paragraph (2)(a), (b) or (c).
(6) 如果證書沒有具體說明第 (2)(a)、(b) 或 (c) 款中規定的原因，仲裁庭可以決定向訴訟的任何或所有當事人提供該資訊或文件。
(7) In deciding whether to make the information or document available, the Tribunal must:
(7) 在決定是否提供資訊或文件時，仲裁庭必須：
(a) take into account as a primary consideration the principle that it is desirable, in the interest of ensuring the effective performance of the Tribunal’s functions, for the parties to the proceeding to be made aware of all relevant matters; and
(a) 作為首要考慮因素，為了確保法庭有效履行職能，程序各方最好了解所有相關事項；和
(b) have regard to any reason specified in the certificate.
(b) 考慮證書中所指的任何原因。
Responsible Minister is party to proceeding
負責部長是訴訟當事人
(8) The responsible Minister is a party to the proceeding if:
(8) 在下列情況下，負責部長是訴訟的一方：
(a) the certificate does not specify a reason set out in paragraph (2)(a), (b) or (c); and
(a) 證書未說明第 (2)(a)、(b) 或 (c) 款所規定的原因；和
(b) the responsible Minister would not otherwise be a party to the proceeding.
(b) 負責部長否則不會成為訴訟的一方。
Notice of public interest decisions
公共利益決定的通知
(9) If the Tribunal decides to make the information or document available under subsection (6), the Tribunal must, as soon as practicable, give each party to the proceeding reasons for the decision.
(9) 若仲裁庭決定依第 (6) 款提供資訊或文件，則仲裁庭必須在切實可行的情況下盡快向各方提供該決定的訴訟理由。
Exclusion of other laws
其他法律的排除
(10) This section excludes the operation of any other law that relates to the public interest and would otherwise apply in relation to the disclosure of information, or of the content of documents, in a proceeding in the Tribunal.
(10) 本節排除與公共利益有關的任何其他法律的實施，以及在法庭訴訟中適用於資訊揭露或文件內容的其他法律。
Delegation—security clearance decisions and security clearance suitability assessments
授權－安全審查決定和安全審查適用性評估
(11) The ASIO Minister may, in writing, delegate the ASIO Minister’s power under subsection (2) in relation to a security clearance decision or a security clearance suitability assessment to:
(11) ASIO 部長可以書面形式將第 (2) 款規定的 ASIO 部長有關安全許可決定或安全許可適宜性評估的權力委託給：
(a) the Director ‑ General of Security; or
(a) 安全局長；或
(b) an ASIO employee (within the meaning of the ASIO Act), or an ASIO affiliate (within the meaning of that Act), who holds, or is acting in, a position in ASIO that is equivalent to or higher than a position occupied by an SES employee.
(b) 在 ASIO 中擔任或正在擔任與 SES 員工同等或更高職位的 ASIO 員工（根據 ASIO 法案的含義）或 ASIO 附屬機構（根據該法案的含義）。
(12) In exercising a power under the delegation, the delegate must comply with any written directions of the ASIO Minister.
(12) 在行使授權下的權力時，代表必須遵守 ASIO 部長的任何書面指示。

證書效力
(2) The certificate does not excuse a person from disclosing information, or giving a document, to the Tribunal for the purposes of the proceeding if the person is required by or under this Act to do so.
(2) 如果本法要求或根據本法要求，該證書不能免除某人出於訴訟目的向法庭披露資訊或提供文件的責任。
(3) However, the Tribunal must do all things necessary to ensure that:
(3) 然而，仲裁庭必須採取一切必要措施以確保：
(a) the information or document is not disclosed or given to any person other than:
(a) 該資訊或文件不會揭露或提供給以下任何人：
(i) a member in the course of the performance of the member’s duties; or
(i) 會員在執行會員職務的過程中；或
(ii) the Principal Registrar in the course of the performance of the Principal Registrar’s duties; or
(ii) 首席書記官長在履行首席書記官長職責期間；或
(iii) a staff member in the course of the performance of the staff member’s duties; and
(iii) 工作人員在履行其職責過程中；和
(b) in the case of a document given to the Tribunal by an agency head—the document is returned, to the agency from which it came, as soon as practicable after the Tribunal has finished considering the document.
(b) 對於由機構負責人向仲裁庭提供的文件－在仲裁庭完成該文件的審議後，在切實可行的範圍內盡快將該文件退還給其來源機構。

text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies:
(1) 本條適用：
(a) in relation to the review of a security clearance decision; and
(a) 與安全審查決定的審查有關；和
(b) instead of the following provisions:
(b) 代替下列規定：
(i) section 105 (Tribunal decision on review of reviewable decision);
(i) 第 105 條（法庭對審查可審查決定的決定）；
(ii) section 112 (notice of decision and statement of reasons—other proceedings).
(ii) 第 112 條（決定通知和理由說明－其他程序）。
Possible decisions
可能的決定
(2) The Tribunal must make a decision:
(2) 仲裁庭必須做出決定：
(a) affirming the security clearance decision; or
(a) 確認安全審查決定；或
(b) setting aside the security clearance decision and remitting the matter to the decision ‑ maker for reconsideration in accordance with any orders or recommendations of the Tribunal.
(b) 根據法庭的任何命令或建議，擱置安全審查決定並將此事轉交決策者重新考慮。
When Tribunal’s decision on review comes into operation
仲裁庭的複審決定何時生效
(3) However, section 107 (when Tribunal’s decision on review comes into operation) applies as if the Tribunal’s decision on the review were made under section 105.
(3) 然而，第 107 條（當仲裁庭關於複審的決定生效時）適用，如同仲裁庭關於複審的決定是根據第 105 條作出的。

title: 166 Making and recording findings
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
Subdivision B — Recording and communicating decisions
text:
(1) The Tribunal:
(1) 仲裁庭：
(a) must make and record its findings in relation to the decision; and
(a) 必須做出並記錄與該決定相關的調查結果；和
(b) in relation to those findings—may state the opinion of the Tribunal as to the correctness of, or justification for, any opinion, advice or information contained in the decision.
(b) 就這些調查結果而言－可以陳述仲裁庭對決定中所含任何意見、建議或資訊的正確性或合理性的意見。
(2) The Tribunal must not make findings in relation to the decision that would have the effect of superseding any information that is (or is taken to be) part of the decision unless those findings state that, in the Tribunal’s opinion, the information:
(2) 仲裁庭不得就該決定做出具有取代作為（或被視為）決定一部分的任何資訊的效果的調查結果，除非這些調查結果表明，仲裁庭認為該資訊：
(a) is incorrect; or
(a) 不正確；或
(b) is incorrectly represented; or
(b) 陳述不正確；或
(c) could not reasonably be relevant to the requirements of security; or
(c) 與安全要求不合理有關；或者
(d) could not reasonably be relevant for the purposes of having regard to whether there is intelligence or information that suggests that the person:
(d) 就考慮是否有情報或資訊顯示該人：
(i) may commit a serious and organised crime; or
(i) 可能實施嚴重的、有組織的犯罪；或
(ii) may assist another person to commit a serious and organised crime.
(ii) 可能協助他人實施嚴重的組織犯罪。

title: 167 Communicating decisions
path: Part 6 — Proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area
Subdivision B — Recording and communicating decisions
text:
Written notice of decisions and findings
決定和調查結果的書面通知
(1) The Tribunal must give written notice of its decision on the review, and copies of its findings made under section 166, to:
(1) 仲裁庭必須將其審查決定以及根據第 166 條作出的調查結果的副本書面通知：
(a) the applicant; and
(a) 申請人；和
(b) the agency head; and
(b) 機構負責人；和
(c) the responsible Minister.
(c) 負責部長。
(2) The notice must include notice of the right of the party to appeal to the Federal Court under Division 2 of Part 7.
(2) 該通知必須包括當事人根據第 7 部分第 2 分部向聯邦法院上訴的權利的通知。
(3) The agency head must give the notice and findings to each relevant body.
(3) 機構負責人必須向各相關機構發出通知及調查結果。
Oral notice of decisions and findings
決定和調查結果的口頭通知
(4) The Tribunal may give its decision and findings orally before giving them in writing.
(4) 仲裁庭可以在書面形式作出決定和調查結果之前以口頭形式作出決定和調查結果。
Directions about disclosure
有關披露的指示
(5) The Tribunal may, by order, direct that the whole or a particular part of its findings, so far as they relate to a matter that has not already been disclosed to the applicant, is not to be given to the applicant or a relevant body.
(5) 仲裁庭可以透過命令指示，其調查結果的全部或特定部分，只要其涉及尚未向申請人披露的事項，不得向申請人或相關機構提供。
Time for giving written notice and findings
發出書面通知和調查結果的時間
(6) The written notice and findings must be given by the time specified in the practice directions. If the practice directions do not specify a time, the written notice and findings must be given within 28 days after the day the Tribunal’s decision is made.
(6) 書面通知和調查結果必須在實務指示中規定的時間內發出。如果實務指示未指定時間，則必須在仲裁庭做出決定之日後 28 天內發出書面通知和調查結果。
Effect of failure to comply
不遵守規定的影響
(7) A failure to comply with this section does not affect the validity of the Tribunal’s decision.
(7) 不遵守本條並不影響仲裁庭裁決的效力。
Effect of non ‑ disclosure provisions
不公開條款的影響
(8) To avoid doubt, this section is subject to other provisions of this Part that prohibit or restrict the disclosure of information or documents.
(8) 為避免疑義，本節須遵守本部分禁止或限制揭露資訊或文件的其他規定。

title: 170 Simplified outline of this Part
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
text:
A party to a proceeding in the Tribunal may appeal to the Federal Court, on a question of law, from the decision of the Tribunal in the proceeding. A decision that a person’s interests are not affected by a reviewable decision may also be appealed. Timeframes apply to making appeals, but may be extended. An appeal does not affect the operation of a Tribunal decision unless the Court orders otherwise.
法庭訴訟的一方可以就法律問題對法庭在訴訟中的裁決向聯邦法院提出上訴。如果某人的利益不受可審查決定的影響，也可以提出上訴。提出上訴有一定的期限，但可能會延長。除非法院另有命令，否則上訴不會影響仲裁庭裁決的執行。
This Part contains the standard provisions for how the Court operates when dealing with an appeal. Other legislation can include provisions that apply in addition to, or instead of, these provisions.
本部分包含法院處理上訴時如何運作的標準規定。其他立法可以包括除這些規定之外或代替這些規定而適用的規定。
The Federal Court may transfer some kinds of appeal to the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2).
聯邦法院可以將某些類型的上訴移交給澳洲聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院（第 2 庭）。
There are provisions facilitating remittal of matters to the Tribunal to be decided again.
有一些規定有助於將事項移交法庭重新決定。
In some circumstances, the Tribunal may refer a question of law to the Federal Court.
在某些情況下，法庭可以將法律問題提交給聯邦法院。
There are requirements (including some non ‑ disclosure obligations) relating to sending documents between the Tribunal and the courts.
對於仲裁庭和法院之間發送文件有一些要求（包括一些保密義務）。

title: 171 Part applies whether Tribunal’s power is conferred by Commonwealth, State or Territory law
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
text:
(1) This Part applies in relation to a proceeding before the Tribunal under power conferred on it by or under:
(1) 本部分適用於仲裁庭依據下列所賦予的權力所進行的訴訟：
(a) an Act or an instrument made under an Act; or
(a) 法案或依法案製定的文書；或
(b) a law of a State, the Australian Capital Territory or the Northern Territory.
(b) 州、澳洲首都領地或北領地的法律。
(2) This Part has effect in relation to a proceeding before the Tribunal under power conferred on it by or under a law of a State, the Australian Capital Territory or the Northern Territory as if a reference in this Part to a provision of this Act that is not in this Part were a reference to that provision as applying as a law of the State or Territory.
(2) 本部分對於根據州、澳洲首都領地或北領地法律授予的權力向法庭提起的訴訟具有效力，如同本部分中提及本法中未包含在本部分中的規定時，即提及該規定作為州或領地的法律適用。

title: 172 Party may appeal

path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
Division 2 — Appeals on questions of law
Subdivision A — Appeals on questions of law
text:
(1) A party to a proceeding in the Tribunal may appeal to the Federal Court, on a question of law, from the decision of the Tribunal in the proceeding.
(1) 仲裁庭訴訟的一方可以就法律問題向聯邦法院上訴，對仲裁庭在訴訟中的決定提出上訴。
Note 1: A party to a proceeding for review of a decision of the Child Support Registrar, or second review that relates to the decision, may in some instances appeal instead to the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2) (see section 99 of the Child Support (Registration and Collection) Act 1988 and section 131E of this Act).
註 1：在某些情況下，對子女扶養登記官的決定進行複審或與該決定相關的第二次複審的訴訟的一方可以向澳大利亞聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院（第 2 庭）提出上訴（參見 1988 年《子女撫養費（登記和收取）法》第 99 條和本法第 131E 條）。
Note 2: For when a party to a proceeding for review of a decision under the Migration Act 1958 can make an application to the Federal Court or the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2), see sections 476 and 476A of the Migration Act 1958 ).
註2：根據《1958年移民法》決定複核訴訟的一方何時可以向聯邦法院或澳大利亞聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院（第2分庭）提出申請，請參閱《1958年移民法》第476和476A條）。
(2) To avoid doubt, subsection (1) does not apply in relation to a decision under section 128 (President decides whether to refer Tribunal decision to guidance and appeals panel).
(2) 為避免疑問，第 (1) 款不適用於第 128 條的決定（庭長決定是否將仲裁庭的決定提交給指導和上訴小組）。
Note: A decision under section 128 is not a decision of the Tribunal.
註：第 128 條的決定並非仲裁庭的決定。

一個人可以就法庭的決定向聯邦法院提出上訴，認為該人的利益不受可審查決定的影響。

title: 174 Time and manner for making appeals
zh: 第174條 上訴的時間和方式
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
Division 2 — Appeals on questions of law
Subdivision A — Appeals on questions of law
text:
(1) The appeal must be made:
(1) 上訴必須提出：
(a) if either of the following applies—no later than 28 days after the Tribunal gives the party or person its statement of reasons for the decision:
(a) 若下列任一情況適用－不遲於仲裁庭向當事人或個人提供該決定的理由陳述後 28 天：
(i) the Tribunal is required to give a statement of reasons for the decision;
(i) 仲裁庭需要說明作出該決定的理由；
(ii) the party or person has a right to request a statement of reasons for the decision and exercises the right; or
(ii) 當事人或個人有權要求陳述該決定的理由並行使該權利；或
(b) if the party or person has a right to request a statement of reasons for the decision and does not exercise the right—no later than 28 days after the last day on which the party or person could have requested a statement of reasons for the decision; or
(b) 若當事人或個人有權要求對決定的理由進行陳述，但沒有行使該權利－不晚於當事人或個人可以要求對決定的理由進行陳述的最後一天后的 28 天；或者
(c) in any other case—no later than 28 days after the party or person is given the decision.
(c) 在任何其他情況下－不遲於當事人或個人收到決定後 28 天。
(2) However, the Federal Court may extend the period within which the appeal must be made.
(2) 但是，聯邦法院可以延長必須提出上訴的期限。
(2A) For the purposes of counting the 28 days mentioned in paragraphs (1)(a), (b) and (c), do not take into account any day in the period starting on 24 December in a year and ending on 14 January in the next year.
(2A) 在計算第(1)(a)、(b)及(c)段所述的28天時，不考慮從當年12月24日開始至下一年1月14日結束期間的任何一天。
(3) If a person applies to refer the decision to the guidance and appeals panel, for the purposes of counting the 28 days mentioned in paragraph (1)(a), (b) or (c), do not take into account any day in the period between the day the application is made and the day the President refers the decision or refuses the application.
(3) 如果某人申請將決定提交給指導和上訴小組，則為了計算第 (1)(a)、(b) 或 (c) 款中提到的 28 天，不要考慮提出申請之日與總統提交決定或拒絕申請之日之間的任何一天。
(4) The appeal must be made in the manner prescribed by the Rules of Court made under the Federal Court of Australia Act 1976 .
(4) 上訴必須依照《1976 年澳洲聯邦法院法》所製定的《法院規則》所規定的方式提出。

title: 175 Constitution of Federal Court
zh: 第175章 聯邦法院憲法
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court

text:
(1) The appeal must be heard by a Full Court if the decision is given by:
(1) 若裁決由下列人員作出，則上訴必須由合議庭審理：
(a) a member who is a Judge; or
(a) 一名擔任法官的成員；或
(b) the Tribunal constituted for the purposes of a proceeding by a member who is, or members at least one of whom is, a Judge.
(b) 為訴訟目的而由一名法官或至少一名法官組成的法庭。
(2) The appeal may be heard by a Full Court if:
(2) 在下列情況下，上訴可由合議庭審理：
(a) subsection (1) does not apply; and
(a) 第 (1) 款不適用；和
(b) the decision is given by:
(b) 決定由下列人員作出：
(i) a member who is a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President; or
(i) 擔任非司法副主席的成員；或
(ii) the Tribunal constituted for the purposes of a proceeding by a member who is, or members at least one of whom is, a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President; or
(ii) 為訴訟目的而由一名或至少一名非司法副院長的成員組成的法庭；或
(iii) the Tribunal constituted for the purposes of a proceeding by the guidance and appeals panel; and
(iii) 指導和上訴小組為訴訟目的而組成的法庭；和
(c) the Chief Justice of the Court, following consultation with the President, thinks it appropriate.
(c) 法院首席大法官在與院長協商後認為適當。

path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court

text:
(1) If an appeal is made under Subdivision A, the Federal Court:
(1) 如果根據 A 分部提出上訴，聯邦法院：
(a) has jurisdiction to hear and determine the appeal; and
(a) 擁有審理和裁決上訴的管轄權；和
(b) must hear and determine the appeal; and
(b) 必須審理上訴並做出裁決；和
(c) may make any order it considers appropriate because of its decision.
(c) 可以根據其決定發布其認為適當的任何命令。
(2) Without limiting the orders it may make, the Federal Court may:
(2) 在不限制其可能發出的命令的情況下，聯邦法院可以：
(a) affirm or set aside a decision of the Tribunal; or
(a) 確認或撤銷仲裁庭的裁決；或
(b) remit a matter to be decided again by the Tribunal, either with or without the taking of further evidence, in accordance with the directions of the Court.
(b) 根據法院的指示，將事項交由仲裁庭重新決定，無論是否採取進一步證據。

title: 177 Court may make findings of fact
zh: 第177條 法院可以對事實作出認定
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
Division 2 — Appeals on questions of law
Subdivision B — Jurisdiction and powers of Federal Court
text:
(1) In hearing the appeal, the Federal Court may make findings of fact if:
(1) 在審理上訴時，聯邦法院可以在下列情況下作出事實認定：
(a) the findings of fact are not inconsistent with findings of fact made by the Tribunal (other than findings made by the Tribunal as the result of an error of law); and
(a) 事實認定與仲裁庭所作的事實認定不不一致（仲裁庭因法律錯誤而作出的認定除外）；和
(b) it appears to the Court that it is convenient to do so.
(b) 法院認為這樣做是方便的。
(2) In deciding whether it is convenient, the Court must have regard to:
(2) 在決定是否方便時，法院必須考慮：
(a) the extent (if any) to which it is necessary to make findings of fact; and
(a) 需要作出事實調查的程度（如有）；和
(b) the means by which those facts might be established; and
(b) 確定這些事實的方式；和
(c) the quick and efficient resolution of the whole of the matter; and
(c) 快速有效地解決整個問題；和
(d) the relative expense and delay (if any) to the parties if the Court, rather than the Tribunal, makes the findings of fact; and
(d) 若由法院而非仲裁庭作出事實認定，則雙方的相對費用和延誤（如有）；和
(e) whether any of the parties considers that it is appropriate for the Court, rather than the Tribunal, to make the findings of fact; and
(e) 是否有任何一方認為由法院而非仲裁庭作出事實認定是適當的；和
(f) any other matters that the Court considers relevant.
(f) 法院認為相關的任何其他事項。
(3) For the purposes of this section, the Court may:
(3) 就本條而言，法院可以：
(a) have regard to the evidence given in the proceeding in the Tribunal; and
(a) 考慮法庭程序中提供的證據；和
(b) receive further evidence.
(b) 取得進一步的證據。

title: 178 Operation and implementation of Tribunal’s decision
zh: 178 仲裁庭裁決的運作和執行
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
Division 2 — Appeals on questions of law
Subdivision B — Jurisdiction and powers of Federal Court
text:
General rule—operation or implementation not affected
一般規則－操作或實施不受影響
(1) An appeal to the Federal Court from a decision of the Tribunal does not affect the operation of the decision or prevent the taking of action to implement the decision.
(1) 對法庭裁決向聯邦法院提出上訴不影響該裁決的實施或阻止採取行動執行該裁決。
Exception—Court may stay operation or implementation
例外－法院可以中止運作或實施
(2) However, for the purpose of ensuring the effectiveness of the hearing and determination of the appeal, the Court or a Judge of the Court may make an order staying or otherwise affecting the operation or implementation of either or both of the following:
(2) 但是，為了確保上訴審理和裁決的有效性，法院或法院法官可以下令中止或以其他方式影響以下一項或兩項的運作或實施：
(a) the decision of the Tribunal, or a part of that decision;
(a) 仲裁庭的決定或該決定的一部分；
(b) the reviewable decision to which the decision of the Tribunal relates, or a part of that reviewable decision.
(b) 仲裁庭裁決所涉及的可覆核決定，或該可覆核決定的一部分。
(3) The order is subject to any conditions specified in the order.
(3) 該訂單須遵守訂單中指定的任何條件。
(4) The order remains in force until the decision on the appeal is given.
(4) 該命令在上訴作出決定之前一直有效。
(5) Despite subsection (4), if:
(5) 儘管有第(4)款的規定，如果：
(a) the order states that it applies for a period; and
(a) 該命令聲明其適用期限；和
(b) the period ends before the decision on the appeal is given;
(b) 該期限在提出上訴決定前結束；
the order has effect until the end of the period.
該命令的有效期限至該期限結束為止。
(6) The order may be varied or revoked by the Court or a Judge of the Court.
(6) 法院或法院法官可以更改或撤銷該命令。

title: Division 3 — Transfer of appeals to Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2)
zh: 第 3 分部 — 將上訴移交給澳洲聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院（第 2 部分）
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
Division 3 — Transfer of appeals to Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2)

title: 179 Transfer of appeals
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
Division 3 — Transfer of appeals to Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2)
text:
General rule—Federal Court may transfer appeal
一般規則－聯邦法院可以轉移上訴
(1) If an appeal under Subdivision A of Division 2 is pending in the Federal Court, the Federal Court may, by order, transfer the appeal to the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2).
(1) 如果根據第 2 分部 A 分部提出的上訴正在聯邦法院審理，則聯邦法院可根據命令將上訴移交澳大利亞聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院（第 2 分部）。
(2) The Federal Court may do so:
(2) 聯邦法院可以這樣做：
(a) on the application of a party to the appeal; or
(a) 根據上訴一方的申請；或
(b) on its own initiative.
(b) 自行主動。
Matters to which Federal Court must have regard
聯邦法院必須考慮的事項
(3) In deciding whether to transfer the appeal, the Federal Court must have regard to the following:
(3) 在決定是否轉移上訴時，聯邦法院必須考慮以下因素：
(a) any Rules of Court made for the purposes of section 181;
(a) 為第 181 條之目的而製定的任何法院規則；
(b) whether proceedings in respect of an associated matter are pending in the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2);
(b) 澳洲聯邦巡迴法院和家事法院（第 2 庭）是否正在審理有關相關事項的訴訟；
(c) whether the resources of the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2) are sufficient to hear and determine the appeal;
(c) 澳洲聯邦巡迴法院和家事法院（第 2 庭）的資源是否足以審理和裁決上訴；
(d) the interests of the administration of justice.
(d) 司法利益。
Jurisdiction and powers of Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2)
澳洲聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院的管轄權和權力（第 2 部）
(4) If the Federal Court transfers the appeal, Subdivision B of Division 2 (jurisdiction and powers of Federal Court) applies in relation to the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2) in the same way as it applies in relation to the Federal Court.
(4) 如果聯邦法院轉移上訴，第 2 分部 B 分部（聯邦法院的管轄權和權力）適用於澳洲聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院（第 2 分部），其適用方式與適用於聯邦法院的方式相同。
Exception—certain appeals must not be transferred
例外－某些上訴不得轉移
(5) However, the Federal Court must not transfer the appeal if it:
(5) 但是，如果出現以下情況，聯邦法院不得轉移上訴：
(a) relates to a decision given by the Tribunal constituted by a member who is, or by members at least one of whom is, a Judge or a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President; or
(a) 涉及由一名法官或非司法副院長組成的法庭作出的裁決，或由至少一名法官或非司法副院長組成的法庭作出的裁決；或者
(b) is of a kind prescribed by the rules.
(b) 屬於規則規定的類型。

title: 180 No appeal from decision to transfer
zh: 180 不可對轉學決定提出上訴
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
Division 3 — Transfer of appeals to Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2)
text:
No appeal lies in relation to a decision of the Federal Court to transfer an appeal under this Division.
聯邦法院依本分庭移交上訴的決定不存在上訴。

title: 181 Federal Court Rules
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
Division 3 — Transfer of appeals to Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2)
text:
(1) Rules of Court made under the Federal Court of Australia Act 1976 may make provision in relation to the transfer of appeals under this Division.
(1) 根據《1976 年澳洲聯邦法院法》制定的《法院規則》可以就本分部下上訴的轉移做出規定。
(2) In particular, the Rules of Court may set out factors that are to be taken into account in deciding whether to transfer an appeal.
(2) 特別是，《法院規則》可以規定在決定是否轉移上訴時應考慮的因素。
(3) Before Rules of Court are made for the purposes of this section, the Federal Court must consult the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2).
(3) 在為本節目的製定法院規則之前，聯邦法院必須諮詢澳洲聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院（第 2 部門）。

title: Division 4 — Matters remitted to Tribunal
zh: 第 4 分部 — 移交給仲裁庭的事項
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court

title: 182 When this Division applies
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
text:
This Division applies if:
本部分適用於以下情況：
(a) an appeal is made to the Federal Court from a decision of the Tribunal; and
(a) 針對法庭的裁決向聯邦法院提出上訴；和
(b) either:
(b) 任一：
(i) the Federal Court remits the matter to the Tribunal to be decided again; or
(i) 聯邦法院將此事移交法庭重新裁決；或
(ii) if the Federal Court transfers the appeal to the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2)—that court remits the matter to the Tribunal to be decided again.
(ii) 如果聯邦法院將上訴移交給澳洲聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院（第 2 庭）－該法院將案件移交法庭再次裁決。

title: 183 Constitution of Tribunal
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
text:
(1) The Tribunal does not need to be constituted for the review by the person or persons who made the decision.
(1) 不需要成立仲裁庭來接受做出決定的人的審查。
(2) To avoid doubt, constituting the Tribunal for the review is not a reconstitution for the purposes of Subdivision D of Division 4 of Part 4 (reconstitution).
(2) 為避免疑義，組成仲裁庭進行複審並非第 4 部分第 4 分 D 分部（重組）目的的重組。

title: 184 Tribunal may rely on previous proceedings
zh: 第184條 仲裁庭可以依賴先前的訴訟程序
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
text:
The Tribunal may have regard to:
仲裁庭可能會考慮：
(a) any record of the proceeding in the Tribunal prior to the appeal (including a record of any evidence taken in the proceeding); and
(a) 上訴先前仲裁庭訴訟程序的任何記錄（包括訴訟程序中取得的任何證據的記錄）；和
(b) any document or thing relating to the proceeding given to the Tribunal prior to the appeal;
(b) 在上訴之前向法庭提交的任何與訴訟程序有關的文件或物品；
unless doing so would be inconsistent with the directions of the court.
除非這樣做與法院的指示不一致。

title: Division 5 — Referring questions of law
zh: 第 5 分部 — —移交法律問題
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court

title: 185 Referring questions of law
zh: 第185章 轉介法律問題
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
text:
(1) The Tribunal may, with the agreement of the President, refer a question of law arising in a proceeding in the Tribunal to the Federal Court for decision.
(1) 經庭長同意，法庭可將法庭程序中出現的法律問題提交聯邦法院裁決。
(2) The Tribunal may do so:
(2) 仲裁庭可以這樣做：
(a) at the request of a party to the proceeding; or
(a) 應訴訟一方的請求；或
(b) on its own initiative.
(b) 自行主動。
(3) The Federal Court has jurisdiction to hear and determine a question of law referred to it under this section.
(3) 聯邦法院有權審理並裁決依本條提交的法律問題。
(4) If, after consulting the President, the Chief Justice of the Court considers it appropriate, that jurisdiction is to be exercised by the Court constituted as a Full Court.
(4) 若法院首席大法官在諮詢院長後認為適當，則由合議庭組成的法院行使管轄權。
(5) If a question of law arising in any proceeding has been referred to the Federal Court under this section, the Tribunal must not, in that proceeding:
(5) 如果任何訴訟中產生的法律問題已根據本條提交給聯邦法院，則仲裁庭不得在該訴訟中：
(a) give a decision to which the question is relevant while the reference is pending; or
(a) 在提交案件待決期間作出與該問題相關的決定；或
(b) proceed in a manner, or make a decision, that is inconsistent with the opinion of the Court on the question.
(b) 以與法院對該問題的意見不一致的方式行事或作出決定。

title: Division 6 — Sending and disclosing documents
zh: 第 6 分部 — 發送和揭露文件
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court

title: 186 When this Division applies
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
text:
This Division applies if:
本部分適用於以下情況：
(a) a party to a proceeding in the Tribunal appeals to the Federal Court from a decision of the Tribunal (see sections 172 and 173); or
(a) 仲裁庭訴訟的一方就仲裁庭的裁決向聯邦法院提出上訴（見第 172 和 173 條）；或者
(b) the Tribunal refers a question of law arising in a proceeding to the Federal Court (see section 185).
(b) 法庭將訴訟中產生的法律問題提交聯邦法院（見第 185 條）。

title: 187 Sending documents
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
text:
(1) The Tribunal must send to the Federal Court all documents that:
(1) 仲裁庭必須向聯邦法院發送以下所有文件：
(a) were before the Tribunal in connection with the proceeding; and
(a) 就該訴訟程序向仲裁庭提起訴訟；和
(b) are relevant to the appeal or reference.
(b) 與上訴或參考相關。
(2) If the Federal Court transfers an appeal to the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2):
(2) 如果聯邦法院將上訴轉移至澳洲聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院（第 2 庭）：
(a) the Federal Court must send the documents concerned to the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2); and
(a) 聯邦法院必須將有關文件發送至澳大利亞聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院（第 2 分庭）；和
(b) sections 189 (disclosure contrary to public interest) and 190 (disclosure of security clearance documents) apply in relation to that court in the same way as they apply in relation to the Federal Court.
(b) 第 189 條（違反公共利益的揭露）和第 190 條（安全審查文件的揭露）適用於該法院，其適用方式與適用於聯邦法院的方式相同。
(3) To avoid doubt, paragraph (2)(a) has effect despite:
(3) 為避免疑問，第 (2)(a) 款仍然有效，儘管：
(a) section 91 (disclosure of information—public interest certificate); and
(a) 第 91 條（資訊揭露－公共利益證明）；和
(b) any provision of Part 6 (proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area); or
(b) 第 6 節的任何規定（情報和安全管轄範圍內的訴訟）；或
(c) a certificate made under a provision mentioned in column 2 of the table in subsection 162(1) (non ‑ disclosure certificates under other Acts); or
(c) 根據第 162(1) 小節表格第 2 欄提及的規定所製作的證書（根據其他法案的非揭露證書）；或
(d) section 272 (public interest certificate in relation to statement of reasons).
(d) 第 272 條（與理由說明相關的公共利益證明）。

title: 188 Returning documents
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
text:
(1) At the conclusion of the proceeding before the Federal Court in relation to the appeal or reference, the Court must return to the Tribunal the documents sent to the Court under this Division.
(1) 在聯邦法院有關上訴或轉介的訴訟程序結束時，法院必須將根據本分庭發送給法院的文件退還給法庭。
(2) However, if the Federal Court sends the documents to the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2), the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2) must return the documents to the Tribunal at the conclusion of the proceeding before the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2) in relation to the appeal or reference.
(2) 但是，如果聯邦法院將文件發送至澳大利亞聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院（第 2 部），則澳大利亞聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院（第 2 部）必須在澳大利亞聯邦巡迴法院和家庭法院（第 2 部）就上訴或轉介進行的訴訟結束時將文件返還給法庭。

title: 189 Disclosure contrary to public interest
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies if:
(1) 本節適用於：
(a) a document is sent to the Federal Court under this Division; and
(a) 根據本分庭向聯邦法院發送一份文件；和
(b) a certificate in force under one of the following provisions certifies that disclosure of a matter contained in the document would be contrary to the public interest:
(b) 依據下列規定之一有效的證書證明揭露文件中所含事項將違反公共利益：
(i) subsection 91(1) or (2) (disclosure of information—public interest certificate);
(i) 第 91(1) 或 (2) 款（資訊揭露－公共利益證明）；
(ii) subsection 161(2) (public interest certificates—responsible Minister);
(ii) 第 161(2) 款（公共利益證明－責任部長）；
(iii) a provision mentioned in column 2 of the table in subsection 162(1) (non ‑ disclosure certificates under other Acts);
(iii) 第 162(1) 小節表格第 2 欄所提及的規定（其他法案下的保密證明）；
(iv) subsection 272(1) (public interest certificate in relation to statement of reasons).
(iv) 第 272(1) 款（與理由說明相關的公共利益證明）。
General rule
一般規則
(2) The Federal Court must do all things necessary to ensure that the matter is not disclosed to any person other than a member of the court as constituted for the purposes of the appeal or reference.
(2) 聯邦法院必須採取一切必要措施，確保此事不會透露給除為上訴或轉介目的而組成的法院成員以外的任何人。
Exception
例外
(3) However, the Federal Court must permit the parties to the proceeding in the Tribunal to inspect the part of the document that contains the matter if:
(3) 但是，在下列情況下，聯邦法院必須允許仲裁庭訴訟各方檢查包含該事項的文件部分：
(a) the document is covered by a certificate mentioned in paragraph (b); and
(a) 該文件附有(b)段所述的證書；和
(b) a reason specified in the certificate in relation to the matter is not a reason mentioned in:
(b) 證書中所指明的與該事項相關的原因不是以下內容所提及的原因：
(i) for a certificate in force under subsection 91(1)—paragraph 91(1)(a) or (b); or
(i) 依據第 91(1) 款有效的證明書－第 91(1)(a) 或 (b) 段；或者
(ii) for a certificate in force under subsection 91(2)—paragraph 91(2)(a); or
(ii) 依據第 91(2) 款有效的證明書－第 91(2)(a) 段；或
(iii) for a certificate in force under subsection 161(2)—paragraph 161(2)(a), (b) or (c); or
(iii) 依據第 161(2) 款有效的證明書－第 161(2)(a)、(b) 或 (c) 段；或
(iv) for a certificate in force under subsection 272(1)—paragraph 272(1)(a) or (b); and
(iv) 對於根據第 272(1) 款有效的證書－第 272(1)(a) 或 (b) 段；和
(c) a question for decision by the Court is whether the matter should be disclosed to some or all of the parties to the proceeding in the Tribunal; and
(c) 需要法院決定的問題是該事項是否應向仲裁庭訴訟的部分或全部當事人披露；和
(d) the Court decides that the matter should be so disclosed.
(d) 法院決定應如此披露此事。

title: 190 Disclosure of security clearance documents
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies if a document sent to the Federal Court under this Division:
(1) 若依本節向聯邦法院發送的文件符合以下條件，則本節適用：
(a) is a copy of a standard (or part of a standard) mentioned in subsection 143(1); or
(a) 是第 143(1) 款中提到的標準（或標準的一部分）的副本；或
(b) contains sensitive information as mentioned in subsection 159(2).
(b) 包含第 159(2) 款所提及的敏感資訊。
General rule
一般規則
(2) The Federal Court must do all things necessary to ensure that the copy of the standard (or part) and any information contained in it, or the sensitive information, is not disclosed to any person other than:
(2) 聯邦法院必須採取一切必要措施，確保標準（或部分）的副本及其中包含的任何資訊或敏感資訊不會透露給以下任何人：
(a) a member of the court as constituted for the purposes of the proceeding; or
(a) 為訴訟目的而組成的法院成員；或
(b) the Director ‑ General of Security or the Director ‑ General’s representative.
(b) 安全局長或局長代表。
Exception
例外
(3) However, subsection (2) does not apply in relation to a disclosure to the person who was the applicant, or a person representing the person who was the applicant, in the proceeding in the Tribunal to the extent that the information:
(3) 但是，第 (2) 款不適用於在法庭程序中向申請人或代表申請人的人披露的資訊：
(a) has already been lawfully disclosed to the person; or
(a) 已合法地向該人揭露；或
(b) is disclosed to the person with the consent of the Director ‑ General of Security.
(b) 經安全總監同意後向相關人員揭露。

title: 191 Disclosure to officers of the court
path: Part 7 — Appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court
text:
Nothing in this Division prevents the disclosure of a document, information or a matter contained in a document to an officer of a court who is performing duties as such an officer.
本節的任何規定均不阻止向履行職責的法院官員披露文件、資訊或文件中包含的事項。

title: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
zh: 第 8 部 — 審裁處成員及職員
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal

title: Division 1 — Preliminary
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal

title: 192 Simplified outline of this Part
zh: 第192節 本部分的簡化概要
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
The Tribunal has different jurisdictional areas. Lists may be established as sub ‑ areas within jurisdictional areas. The President, or some Non ‑ Judicial Deputy Presidents, may lead a jurisdictional area. A Deputy President or senior member may lead a list. Members may be assigned to one or more jurisdictional areas.
法庭有不同的管轄範圍。清單可以建立為管轄區域內的子區域。總統或一些非司法副總統可以領導一個管轄區域。副主席或高級成員可以領導一份名單。成員可能會被指派到一個或多個管轄區域。
Members of the Tribunal have different functions and obligations. Generally, before a person is appointed as a member (other than a Judicial Deputy President) the Minister must be satisfied that the person was assessed as suitable for the appointment through a merit ‑ based assessment process.
法庭成員有不同的職能和義務。一般來說，在某人被任命為成員（司法副院長除外）之前，部長必須確信該人透過基於績效的評估程序被評估為適合任命。
The President must determine a code of conduct and performance standard for non ‑ judicial members. The President may investigate some conduct of non ‑ judicial members, and must notify the Minister if the President reasonably believes there are grounds for termination of a non ‑ judicial member.
總統必須確定非司法成員的行為準則和績效標準。總統可以調查非司法成員的某些行為，如果總統合理地認為有理由解僱非司法成員，則必須通知部長。
One of the President’s functions is to inform relevant Ministers, relevant Commonwealth entities and the Council of identified systemic issues. Jurisdictional area leaders are to inform the President of systemic issues identified in relation to their jurisdictional areas.
總統的職責之一是向相關部長、相關英聯邦實體和理事會通報已發現的系統性問題。轄區領導人應向總統通報與其轄區相關的系統性議題。
The President is responsible for managing the administrative affairs of the Tribunal.
庭長負責管理法庭的行政事務。
The Principal Registrar’s functions include:
首席書記官長的職能包括：
(a) assisting the President in managing the administrative affairs of the Tribunal; and
(a) 協助庭長管理法庭的行政事務；和
(b) providing the corporate and registry services of the Tribunal.
(b) 提供法庭的公司和登記服務。
There are provisions related to the terms and conditions on which members and the Principal Registrar hold office.
有與會員和首席註冊官任職的條款和條件相關的規定。
The Tribunal Advisory Committee is established. The Committee consists of the President, the Principal Registrar, the jurisdictional area leaders and other nominated members.
法庭諮詢委員會成立。委員會由主席、首席書記官長、轄區領導人和其他提名成員組成。
The staff of the Tribunal must be persons engaged under the Public Service Act 1999 . Staff members may be appointed as registrars.
法庭工作人員必須是根據《1999 年公共服務法》聘用的人員。工作人員可被任命為登記員。

title: Division 2 — Members of Tribunal
zh: 第 2 分部 — 仲裁庭成員
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal

title: Subdivision A — Members and functions
zh: A 分部 — 成員與職能
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal

title: 193 Functions of President
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal

path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal

title: 195 Functions of senior and general members
zh: 195 高級會員和普通會員的功能
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
Senior members
高級會員
(1) A senior member has the following functions:
（一）高級會員具有下列職權：
(a) to participate as a member of the Tribunal, particularly in proceedings involving more complex matters;
(a) 作為法庭成員參與，特別是涉及更複雜事項的訴訟程序；
(b) to assist each jurisdictional area leader of each jurisdictional area to which the senior member has been assigned in the performance of the jurisdictional area leader’s functions;
(b) 協助高級會員所在轄區的各轄區領導者履行轄區領導的職責；
(c) to promote best practice in decision ‑ making by the Tribunal;
(c) 推廣法庭決策的最佳做法；
(d) any other functions conferred on a senior member by this Act or another Act;
(d) 本法或其他法賦予高級會員的任何其他職能；
(e) to do anything incidental or conducive to the performance of any of the above functions.
(e) 做任何附帶或有利於履行任何上述職能的事情。
General members
一般會員
(2) A general member has the following functions:
（二）普通會員具有下列職權：
(a) to participate as a member of the Tribunal;
(a) 以仲裁庭成員身分出席；
(b) any other functions conferred on a general member by this Act or another Act;
(b) 本法或其他法賦予一般會員的任何其他職能；
(c) to do anything incidental or conducive to the performance of any of the above functions.
(c) 做任何附帶或有利於履行任何上述職能的事情。

title: Subdivision B — Jurisdictional areas and lists
zh: B 分區 — 管轄區域和列表
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Jurisdictional areas and lists

title: 196 Jurisdictional areas and lists
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Jurisdictional areas and lists
text:
(1) The following jurisdictional areas of the Tribunal are established:
(1) 法庭的管轄範圍如下：
(a) General;
(a) 一般規定；
(b) Intelligence and Security;
(b) 情報和安全；
(c) Migration;
(c) 移徙；
(d) National Disability Insurance Scheme;
(d) 全國殘障保險計劃；
(e) Protection;
(e) 保護；
(f) Social Security;
(f) 社會保障；
(g) Taxation and Business;
(g) 稅務和商業；
(h) Veterans’ and Workers’ Compensation.
(h) 退伍軍人和工人賠償。
(2) The President:
(2) 主席：
(a) may establish one or more lists as subareas within a jurisdictional area; and
(a) 可建立一個或多個清單作為管轄區域內的分區；和
(b) may abolish any such list.
(b) 任何此類清單都可以廢除。
(3) Before establishing or abolishing a list, the President must consult the Tribunal Advisory Committee.
(3) 在建立或廢除名單之前，庭長必須諮詢仲裁庭諮詢委員會。
(4) The Tribunal’s powers in relation to a proceeding are to be exercised in the jurisdictional area or list that the President directs.
(4) 仲裁庭與訴訟有關的權力應在庭長指示的管轄區域或名單內行使。
(5) If a direction is made in writing, the direction is not a legislative instrument.
(5) 若指示以書面形式作出，則該指示並非立法文書。

title: 197 Jurisdictional area leaders
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Jurisdictional areas and lists
text:
Assignment of jurisdictional area leaders
轄區領導分配
(1) The Minister may, in consultation with the President, assign either or both of the following to be a leader of one or more jurisdictional areas:
(1) 部長可與總統協商，指派下列人員之一或兩者擔任一個或多個管轄區域的領導人：
(a) the President;
(a) 主席；
(b) a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President appointed on a salaried basis.
(b) 一名按薪任命的非司法副院長。
(2) The Minister may, on the recommendation of the President, vary or revoke an assignment under subsection (1).
(2) 部長可依總統的建議，更改或撤銷第 (1) 款的指派。
(3) The President must not make a recommendation to the Minister to vary or revoke an assignment under subsection (1) unless:
(3) 總統不得依第 (1) 款向部長提出變更或撤銷指派的建議，除非：
(a) the assignment has been in effect for more than 6 months; and
(a) 轉讓已生效超過 6 個月；和
(b) the President is satisfied that the variation or revocation would meet the operational needs of the Tribunal.
(b) 庭長確信變更或撤銷將符合法庭的運作需求。
(4) If an assignment under subsection (1) is made in writing, the assignment is not a legislative instrument.
(4) 如果第 (1) 款規定的轉讓以書面形式作出，則該轉讓不是立法文書。
Functions of jurisdictional area leaders
轄區領導職責
(5) A jurisdictional area leader has the following functions:
（五）轄區領導履行下列職責：
(a) to provide intellectual leadership to members assigned to the jurisdictional area, including by promoting best practice in decision ‑ making by those members;
(a) 為分配到管轄區域的成員提供智力領導，包括推廣這些成員決策的最佳做法；
(b) to assist the President to ensure that the Tribunal operates efficiently and effectively and continually pursues the objective in section 9 across all jurisdictional areas;
(b) 協助庭長確保法庭有效率且有效地運作，並在所有管轄範圍內持續實現第 9 條的目標；
(c) to oversee, and respond to issues and trends in, the caseload strategy of the jurisdictional area in consultation with the President;
(c) 與總統協商，監督並應對管轄區域的案件量策略中的問題和趨勢；
(d) to assist the President to manage the performance and conduct of members assigned to the jurisdictional area;
(d) 協助主席管理轄區成員的表現和行為；
(e) to provide training, education and professional development opportunities to members assigned to the jurisdictional area;
(e) 向分配到管轄區域的成員提供培訓、教育和專業發展機會；
(f) to identify systemic issues related to the making of reviewable decisions arising in the caseload of the jurisdictional area and to inform the President of those issues.
(f) 找出管轄範圍內案件中出現的與作出可審查決定有關的系統性問題，並將這些問題通知總統。
Acting jurisdictional area leaders
代理轄區領導
(6) The Minister may, in consultation with the President, assign a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President appointed on a salaried basis or a senior member appointed on a salaried basis to act, for a period of no more than 3 months, as a jurisdictional area leader in relation to a jurisdictional area:
(6) 部長可與總統協商，指派一名受薪任命的非司法副總統或受薪任命的高級成員，在不超過 3 個月的時間內擔任與管轄區域有關的管轄區域領導人：
(a) during a vacancy in the position of a jurisdictional area leader in relation to the jurisdictional area (whether or not an assignment has previously been made to the position); or
(a) 在與管轄區域相關的管轄區域領導職位空缺期間（無論之前是否已分配該職位）；或
(b) during any period, or during all periods, when a jurisdictional area leader in relation to the jurisdictional area:
(b) 在任何時期或所有時期，管轄區領袖就其管轄區：
(i) is absent from duty or from Australia; or
(i) 缺席或離開澳洲；或
(ii) is, for any reason, unable to perform the duties of the position.
(ii) 因任何原因無法履行該職位的職責。
Note: For rules that apply to a person acting as a jurisdictional area leader, see section 33A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 .
注意：有關適用於擔任管轄區域領導者的規則，請參閱《1901 年法案解釋法》第 33A 條。

title: 198 Assignment of members to lead lists
zh: 198 將成員分配到領導名單
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Jurisdictional areas and lists
text:
Assignments
作業
(1) The President may assign a Deputy President or senior member to lead one or more lists.
(1) 主席可指派一名副主席或高級成員領導一個或多個名單。
(2) Subject to subsection (4), the President may vary or revoke an assignment under subsection (1).
（2）根據第（4）款，總統可以改變或撤銷第（1）款下的指派。
Acting assignments
代理任務
(3) The President may assign a Deputy President or senior member to act as the leader of a list:
(3) 主席可指派一位副主席或資深成員擔任名單的領導者：
(a) during a vacancy in the position of leader of that list (whether or not an assignment has previously been made to the position); or
(a) 在該名單的領導者職位空缺期間（無論之前是否已分配到該職位）；或
(b) during any period, or during all periods, when the leader of that list:
(b) 在任何時期或所有時期，當名單的領先者：
(i) is absent from duty or from Australia; or
(i) 缺席或離開澳洲；或
(ii) is, for any reason, unable to perform the duties of the position.
(ii) 因任何原因無法履行該職位的職責。
Note: For rules that apply to a person acting as the leader of a list, see section 33A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 .
注意：有關適用於作為名單領導者的人的規則，請參閱《1901 年法案解釋法》第 33A 條。
Consultation
諮詢
(4) The President must not make, vary or revoke an assignment under subsection (1) or (3) unless the President has consulted each jurisdictional area leader of each list affected by the making, variation or revocation.
(4) 總統不得依第 (1) 或 (3) 款作出、變更或撤銷指派，除非總統已諮詢受制定、變更或撤銷影響的每個名單的每個管轄區領導人。
Assignment not a legislative instrument
轉讓不是立法文書
(5) If an assignment under subsection (1) or (3) is made in writing, the assignment is not a legislative instrument.
(5) 若第 (1) 或 (3) 款規定的轉讓以書面形式作出，則該轉讓不是立法文書。

title: 199 Assignment of members to jurisdictional areas
zh: 第199章 成員管轄範圍的分配
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Jurisdictional areas and lists
text:
Deputy Presidents
副總裁
(1) A Deputy President is assigned to every jurisdictional area.
（一）各轄區設副院長一名。
Senior member leading a list
領導名單的高階成員
(2) A senior member assigned to lead a list is assigned to the jurisdictional area within which the list is established.
(2) 指定領導名單的高階成員被指派到名單所建立的管轄區域。
Assignment by President
主席的指派
(3) The President may, in writing, assign a member (other than the President or a Deputy President) to one or more jurisdictional areas.
(3) 主席可書面指派一名成員（主席或副主席除外）負責一個或多個管轄區域。
(4) However, the President must not do so if an assignment under subsection (8) in relation to the member has been made and has not been revoked.
(4) 但是，如果根據第 (8) 款對會員進行的指派已經作出且尚未撤銷，則主席不得這樣做。
(5) Before assigning a member to a jurisdictional area, the President must be satisfied that the member has the appropriate skills, qualifications and experience.
(5) 在將成員分配到管轄區域之前，主席必須確信該成員具有適當的技能、資格和經驗。
(6) The President may vary or revoke an assignment under subsection (3) at any time.
(6) 總統可隨時更改或撤銷第 (3) 款規定的指派。
(7) An assignment under subsection (3) is not a legislative instrument.
(7) 第 (3) 款規定的轉讓不是立法文書。
Assignment by Governor ‑ General
總督的指派
(8) The Governor ‑ General may, on the recommendation of the Minister, assign a member (other than the President or a Deputy President) to one or more jurisdictional areas by specifying the assignment in the member’s instrument of appointment.
(8) 總督可根據部長的建議，將一名成員（總統或副主席除外）指派到一個或多個管轄區域，並在成員的任命書中具體說明此指派。
(9) However, the Governor ‑ General must not do so if an assignment under subsection (8) in relation to the member has been made and has been revoked.
(9) 然而，如果根據第(8)款對成員進行的指派已經作出並已被撤銷，則總督不得這樣做。
(10) Before the Governor ‑ General assigns a member to a jurisdictional area, the Minister must be satisfied that:
(10) 在總督指派議員到管轄區域之前，部長必須確信：
(a) there are exceptional circumstances that justify the assignment; and
(a) 有證明該任務合理的特殊情況；和
(b) the member has the appropriate skills, qualifications and experience.
(b) 該成員具有適當的技能、資格和經驗。
(11) The Governor ‑ General may at any time, by varying a member’s instrument of appointment:
(11) 總督可隨時透過更改成員的任命書：
(a) assign the member to one or more additional jurisdictional areas; or
(a) 將成員指派到一個或多個附加管轄區域；或
(b) revoke the member’s assignment to each of the jurisdictional areas.
(b) 撤銷該成員對每個管轄區域的分配。

title: Subdivision C — Performance and conduct of members
zh: C 部分－成員的表現與行為
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision C — Performance and conduct of members

title: 200 President may give directions to members
zh: 200 主席可向會員發出指示
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision C — Performance and conduct of members
text:
(1) The President may give a written direction to a non ‑ judicial member relating to the performance of the member’s duties.
(1) 主席可向非司法成員發出有關其履行職責的書面指示。
(2) The member must comply with the direction.
(2) 會員必須遵守指示。
(3) A direction given under subsection (1):
(3) 依第 (1) 款給予的指示：
(a) must be consistent with the President’s functions; and
(a) 必須符合主席的職能；和
(b) must not relate to a particular proceeding in the Tribunal.
(b) 不得與仲裁庭的特定程序相關。
(4) A direction under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.
(4) 第 (1) 款的指示並非立法文書。

title: 201 Code of conduct
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision C — Performance and conduct of members
text:
(1) The President must, in writing, determine a code of conduct for non ‑ judicial members.
(1) 主席必須以書面形式確定非司法成員的行為準則。
Note: A serious breach of the code of conduct may lead to termination of a non ‑ judicial member’s appointment (see section 221).
註：嚴重違反行為準則可能會導致終止非司法成員的任命（見第 221 條）。
(2) Without limiting subsection (1), the code of conduct must make provision for the taking of action by the President or a jurisdictional area leader in relation to non ‑ judicial members upholding the code of conduct.
(2) 在不限制第(1)款的情況下，行為準則必須規定總統或管轄區領導人對維護行為準則的非司法成員採取行動。
(3) Subsection (1) does not limit section 36 (President may make practice directions).
(3) 第 (1) 款不限制第 36 條（總統可以做出實務指示）。
(4) The President must publish the code of conduct.
(4) 總統必須公佈行為準則。
(5) The code of conduct is not a legislative instrument.
(5) 行為準則不是立法文件。

title: 202 Performance standard
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision C — Performance and conduct of members
text:
(1) The President must, in writing, determine a performance standard for non ‑ judicial members.
(1) 主席必須以書面形式確定非司法成員的績效標準。
Note: A serious breach of the performance standard may lead to termination of a non ‑ judicial member’s appointment (see section 221).
註：嚴重違反績效標準可能會導致終止非司法成員的任命（請參閱第 221 條）。
(2) Without limiting subsection (1), the performance standard must make provision for the taking of action by the President or a jurisdictional area leader in relation to non ‑ judicial members meeting the performance standard.
(2) 在不限制第(1)款的情況下，績效標準必須規定總統或管轄區領導人對符合績效標準的非司法成員採取行動。
(3) Subsection (1) does not limit section 36 (President may make practice directions).
(3) 第 (1) 款不限制第 36 條（總統可以做出實務指示）。
(4) The President must publish the performance standard.
(4) 總統必須公佈績效標準。
(5) The performance standard is not a legislative instrument.
(5) 績效標準不是立法文件。

title: 203 President may investigate conduct of members
zh: 第203章 總統可以調查成員的行為
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision C — Performance and conduct of members
text:
(1) This section applies if the President forms the opinion that a non ‑ judicial member may have engaged in conduct that:
(1) 若主席認為非司法成員可能從事以下行為，則本節適用：
(a) may constitute a breach of the code of conduct; or
(a) 可能構成違反行為準則；或
(b) may constitute a breach of the performance standard; or
(b) 可能構成違反績效標準；或
(c) may constitute a ground for terminating the appointment of the member in accordance with section 221; or
(c) 可構成依第 221 條終止該成員任命的理由；或
(d) may adversely affect, or may have adversely affected, the performance of official duties by the member; or
(d) 可能對或可能已對會員履行公務產生不利影響；或
(e) may adversely affect, or may have adversely affected, public trust and confidence in the Tribunal.
(e) 可能對或可能已經對公眾對法庭的信任和信心產生不利影響。
Note: For example, the President may form the opinion because of a complaint made to the Tribunal in relation to the conduct.
註：例如，主席可能會因向法庭提出與該行為有關的投訴而形成意見。
(2) The President may:
(2) 主席可：
(a) do one or more of the following:
(a) 執行下列一項或多項操作：
(i) investigate the conduct;
(i) 調查該行為；
(ii) report on an investigation of the conduct;
(ii) 行為調查報告；
(iii) deal with a report of an investigation of the conduct;
(iii) 處理有關行為的調查報告；
(iv) refer the conduct to a person or body;
(iv) 將行為提交給個人或機構；
(v) direct a person or body to investigate the conduct;
(v) 指示個人或機構調查該行為；
(vi) authorise, in writing, a person or body to do any of the above;
(vi) 以書面授權個人或機構進行上述任何活動；
(vii) take any measures in relation to the member that the President believes are reasonably necessary to maintain public trust and confidence in the Tribunal; or
(vii) 採取主席認為合理必要的與該成員相關的任何措施，以維持公眾對法庭的信任和信心；或
(b) take no action, or no further action, in relation to the conduct.
(b) 不對該行為採取任何行動，或不採取進一步行動。
Note 1: The President is also required to notify the Minister if the President reasonably believes that there are grounds for terminating the member’s appointment under section 221 (see section 222).
註 1：如果總統合理地認為有理由根據第 221 條終止該成員的任命（見第 222 條），則總統也必須通知部長。
Note 2: For protections for persons involved in investigating conduct of members, see section 204.
註 2：參與調查會員行為的人員的保護，請參閱第 204 節。
(3) The President may, at any time after forming the opinion mentioned in subsection (1), temporarily restrict the member’s duties if the President reasonably believes that doing so is in the public, or the Tribunal’s, interest.
(3) 在形成第 (1) 款所述意見後，如果庭長合理地認為這樣做符合公眾或法庭的利益，則庭長可以隨時暫時限制該成員的職責。

title: 204 Protection of persons involved in investigating conduct of members etc.
zh: 204 保護參與調查會員行為的人員等
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision C — Performance and conduct of members
text:
(1) A person who is performing or exercising functions or powers under or for the purposes of section 203 in relation to conduct that was, or may have been, engaged in by a member, or assisting in performing or exercising those functions or powers, has the same protection and immunity as a Justice of the High Court.
(1) 根據第 203 條或為了第 203 條的目的，履行或行使與會員曾經或可能從事的行為有關的職能或權力，或協助履行或行使這些職能或權力的人，享有與高等法院法官相同的保護和豁免權。
(2) A person appearing before a person who is performing or exercising functions or powers under or for the purposes of section 203 in relation to conduct that was, or may have been, engaged in by a member has the same protection, and is subject to the same liabilities, as a witness in proceedings in the High Court.
(2) 出席根據第 203 條或為了第 203 條之目的履行或行使與會員曾經或可能已經從事的行為有關的職能或權力的人的出庭的人，與高等法院訴訟中的證人享有相同的保護，並承擔相同的責任。
(3) A legal practitioner assisting, or appearing on behalf of a person before, a person who is performing or exercising functions or powers for the purposes of section 203 in relation to conduct that was, or may have been, engaged in by a member has the same protection and immunity as a barrister appearing for a party in proceedings in the High Court.
(3) 為第 203 條之目的，協助或代表某人出庭，履行或行使與會員曾經或可能已經從事的行為有關的職能或權力的人，與在高等法院訴訟中代表一方出庭的大律師享有相同的保護和豁免權。

title: Division 3 — Member appointment provisions
zh: 第 3 分部 — 成員任命條款
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal

title: Subdivision A — Appointment of members
zh: A 分部 — 成員的任命
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal

title: 205 Appointment of President
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
Appointment by Governor ‑ General
由總督任命
(1) The President is to be appointed by the Governor ‑ General, by written instrument, on the recommendation of the Minister.
(1) 總統由總督根據部長的推薦以書面形式任命。
(2) Before the Minister makes a recommendation to the Governor ‑ General, the Minister must:
(2) 在部長向總督提出建議之前，部長必須：
(a) consult the Chief Justice of the Federal Court; and
(a) 諮詢聯邦法院首席法官；和
(b) be satisfied that the person was assessed, by a panel established under section 209, as suitable for the appointment through an assessment process that:
(b) 確信該人已由依第 209 條設立的小組透過以下評估程序評估為適合任命：
(i) was merit ‑ based; and
(i) 擇優錄取；和
(ii) included public advertising of the position; and
(ii) 包括該職位的公開廣告；和
(iii) complied with the requirements (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
(iii) 符合法規規定的要求（如有）。
Qualification for appointment
任職資格
(3) A person must not be appointed as the President unless the person is a Judge of the Federal Court.
(3) 除非是聯邦法院法官，否則不得被任命為總統。
Period of appointment
聘任期限
(4) The President holds office for a period of 5 years unless a shorter period is specified in the instrument of appointment.
(4) 主席的任期為 5 年，除非任命書中規定了較短的任期。
(5) If the instrument of appointment specifies a shorter period, the instrument must state the reasons why the shorter period is specified.
(5) 如果任命書規定了較短的期限，則該文書必須說明規定較短期限的理由。
Basis of appointment
任命依據
(6) The President must be appointed on a salaried basis.
(6) 主席必須按薪金任命。
Reappointment
重新任命
