(7) A person may be reappointed as the President by written instrument made within 6 months before the end of the period specified in the person’s instrument of appointment.
(7) 一個人可以在其任命書規定的期限結束前 6 個月內再次透過書面文件被任命為總統。
(8) Paragraph (2)(b) does not apply in relation to the reappointment of a person who, immediately before the start of the period of reappointment, holds office as the President under a previous appointment under subsection (1).
(8) 第 (2)(b) 款不適用於在重新任命期限開始之前根據第 (1) 款先前任命擔任總統的人的重新任命。

title: 206 Appointment of Judicial Deputy Presidents
zh: 第206章 任命司法副院長
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
Appointment by Governor ‑ General
由總督任命
(1) A Judicial Deputy President is to be appointed by the Governor ‑ General, by written instrument, on the recommendation of the Minister.
(1) 司法副院長由總督根據部長的推薦以書面形式任命。
(2) Before the Minister makes a recommendation to the Governor ‑ General, the Minister must:
(2) 在部長向總督提出建議之前，部長必須：
(a) consult the Chief Justice of the court of which the person is a Judge; and
(a) 諮詢該人擔任法官的法院的首席法官；和
(b) seek, and take into account, the advice of the President in relation to:
(b) 尋求並考慮總統對以下方面的建議：
(i) whether the appointment would meet the operational needs of the Tribunal; and
(i) 該任命是否能滿足法庭的業務需要；和
(ii) the effect of the appointment on the number of Judicial Deputy Presidents relative to the number of Non ‑ Judicial Deputy Presidents, senior members and general members.
(ii) 任命對司法副院長人數相對於非司法副院長、高級委員和普通委員人數的影響。
Qualification for appointment
任職資格
(3) A person must not be appointed as a Judicial Deputy President unless the person is:
(3) 不得任命司法副院長，除非該人：
(a) a Judge of the Federal Court; or
(a) 聯邦法院法官；或
(b) a Judge of the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 1).
(b) 澳洲聯邦巡迴法院和家事法院（第 1 庭）的法官。
Period of appointment
聘任期限
(4) A Judicial Deputy President holds office for a period of 5 years unless a shorter period is specified in the instrument of appointment.
(4) 司法副院長的任期為 5 年，除非任命書中規定了較短的期限。
(5) If the instrument of appointment specifies a shorter period, the instrument must state the reasons why the shorter period is specified.
(5) 如果任命書規定了較短的期限，則該文書必須說明規定較短期限的理由。
Basis of appointment
任命依據
(6) A Judicial Deputy President must be appointed on a sessional basis.
(6) 司法副院長必須依任期任命。

title: 207 Appointment of Non ‑ Judicial Deputy Presidents
zh: 第207條 任命非司法副院長
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
Appointment by Governor ‑ General
由總督任命
(1) A Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President is to be appointed by the Governor ‑ General, by written instrument, on the recommendation of the Minister.
(1) 非司法副總統由總督根據部長的推薦以書面形式任命。
(2) Before the Minister makes a recommendation to the Governor ‑ General, the Minister must:
(2) 在部長向總督提出建議之前，部長必須：
(a) seek, and take into account, the advice of the President in relation to:
(a) 尋求並考慮總統對以下方面的建議：
(i) whether the appointment would meet the operational needs of the Tribunal; and
(i) 該任命是否能滿足法庭的業務需要；和
(ii) the financial capacity of the Tribunal for the appointment; and
(ii) 法庭進行任命的財務能力；和
(iii) the effect of the appointment on the number of Non ‑ Judicial Deputy Presidents relative to the number of senior members and general members; and
(iii) 任命對非司法副主席人數相對於高級成員和普通成員人數的影響；和
(b) be satisfied that the person was assessed, by a panel established under section 209, as suitable for the appointment through an assessment process that:
(b) 確信該人已由依第 209 條設立的小組透過以下評估程序評估為適合任命：
(i) was merit ‑ based; and
(i) 擇優錄取；和
(ii) included public advertising of the position; and
(ii) 包括該職位的公開廣告；和
(iii) complied with the requirements (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
(iii) 符合法規規定的要求（如有）。
Qualification for appointment
任職資格
(3) A person must not be appointed as a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President unless:
(3) 任何人不得被任命為非司法副總統，除非：
(a) the person is enrolled as a legal practitioner and has been so enrolled for at least 10 years; and
(a) 該人註冊為法律執業者，並且已註冊至少 10 年；和
(b) either:
(b) 任一：
(i) the person is a former Judge; or
(i) 該人是前法官；或
(ii) the Minister is satisfied that the person has substantial expertise in one or more areas relevant to the jurisdiction of the Tribunal.
(ii) 部長信納此人在與法院管轄權相關的一個或多個領域擁有豐富的專業知識。
Period of appointment
聘任期限
(4) A Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President holds office for a period of 5 years unless a shorter period is specified in the instrument of appointment.
(4) 非司法副院長的任期為 5 年，除非任命書中規定了較短的期限。
(5) If the instrument of appointment specifies a shorter period, the instrument must state the reasons why the shorter period is specified.
(5) 如果任命書規定了較短的期限，則該文書必須說明規定較短期限的理由。
Basis of appointment
任命依據
(6) A Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President may be appointed on a salaried or sessional basis.
(6) 非司法副院長可以按薪金或會期任命。
Reappointment
重新任命
(7) A person may be reappointed as a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President by written instrument made within 6 months before the end of the period specified in the person’s instrument of appointment.
(7) 某人可以在其任命書規定的期限結束前 6 個月內再次透過書面文書被任命為非司法副院長。
(8) Before a person is reappointed as a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President, the Minister must seek, and take into account, the advice of the President in relation to the person’s performance against the performance standard.
(8) 在某人被重新任命為非司法副總統之前，部長必須尋求並考慮總統關於該人的績效是否符合績效標準的建議。
(9) Paragraph (2)(b) applies only in relation to every second reappointment of a person after the person’s first appointment under subsection (1).
(9) 第 (2)(b) 款僅適用於依第 (1) 款首次任命後的每兩次重新任命。

title: 208 Appointment of senior members and general members
zh: 第208條 高級會員及普通會員的任命
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
Appointment by Governor ‑ General
由總督任命
(1) A senior member or general member is to be appointed by the Governor ‑ General, by written instrument, on the recommendation of the Minister.
(1) 高級成員或普通成員由總督根據部長的推薦以書面形式任命。
(2) Before the Minister makes a recommendation to the Governor ‑ General, the Minister must:
(2) 在部長向總督提出建議之前，部長必須：
(a) seek, and take into account, the advice of the President in relation to:
(a) 尋求並考慮總統對以下方面的建議：
(i) whether the appointment would meet the operational needs of the Tribunal; and
(i) 該任命是否能滿足法庭的業務需要；和
(ii) the financial capacity of the Tribunal for the appointment; and
(ii) 法庭進行任命的財務能力；和
(iii) the effect of the appointment on the number of senior members and general members relative to the number of Non ‑ Judicial Deputy Presidents; and
(iii) 任命對高級成員和普通成員數量相對於非司法副主席數量的影響；和
(b) be satisfied that the person was assessed, by a panel established under section 209, as suitable for the appointment through an assessment process that:
(b) 確信該人已由依第 209 條設立的小組透過以下評估程序評估為適合任命：
(i) was merit ‑ based; and
(i) 擇優錄取；和
(ii) included public advertising of the position; and
(ii) 包括該職位的公開廣告；和
(iii) complied with the requirements (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
(iii) 符合法規規定的要求（如有）。
Qualification for appointment—senior member
任職資格－高級會員
(3) A person must not be appointed as a senior member unless:
(3) 除非符合以下條件，否則不得任命為高級會員：
(a) the person is enrolled as a legal practitioner and has been so enrolled for at least 7 years; or
(a) 該人已登記為法律執業者，並已登記至少 7 年；或
(b) the Minister is satisfied that the person has at least 7 years’ specialised training or experience in a subject matter relevant to the jurisdiction of the Tribunal.
(b) 部長信納此人在與法院管轄權相關的主題事項上擁有至少 7 年的專業訓練或經驗。
Qualification for appointment—general member
任職資格－普通會員
(4) A person must not be appointed as a general member unless:
(4) 任何人不得被任命為普通會員，除非：
(a) the person is enrolled as a legal practitioner and has been so enrolled for at least 5 years; or
(a) 該人已登記為法律執業者，並已登記至少 5 年；或
(b) the Minister is satisfied that the person has at least 5 years’ specialised training or experience in a subject matter relevant to the jurisdiction of the Tribunal.
(b) 部長信納此人在與法院管轄權相關的主題事項上擁有至少 5 年的專業訓練或經驗。
Period of appointment
聘任期限
(5) A senior member or general member holds office for a period of 5 years unless a shorter period is specified in the instrument of appointment.
(5) 高級會員或一般會員的任期為 5 年，除非任命書規定較短的期限。
(6) If the instrument of appointment specifies a shorter period, the instrument must state the reasons why the shorter period is specified.
(6) 如果任命書規定了較短的期限，則該任命書必須說明規定較短期限的理由。
Basis of appointment
任命依據
(7) A senior member or general member may be appointed on a salaried or sessional basis.
(7) 高級會員或普通會員可以按薪金或會期任命。
Reappointment
重新任命
(8) A person may be reappointed as a senior member or general member by written instrument made within 6 months before the end of the period specified in the person’s instrument of appointment.
(8) 可在其任命書規定的期限結束前 6 個月內以書面重新任命為高級會員或普通會員。
(9) Before a person is reappointed as a senior member or general member, the Minister must seek, and take into account, the advice of the President in relation to the person’s performance against the performance standard.
(9) 在某人被重新任命為高級會員或普通會員之前，部長必須尋求並考慮總統關於該人的表現是否符合績效標準的建議。
(10) Paragraph (2)(b) applies only in relation to every second reappointment of a person to an office after the person’s first appointment to that office under subsection (1).
(10) 第 (2)(b) 款僅適用於某人根據第 (1) 款首次被任命擔任某職位後的每兩次重新任命。

title: 209 Minister must establish assessment panel
zh: 第209章 部長必須成立評估小組
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
(1) The Minister must, from time to time, establish one or more panels ( assessment panels ) of persons for the purposes of assessing whether a candidate or candidates are suitable for appointment under section 205, 207, 208 or 227.
(1) 部長必須不時設立一個或多個人員小組（評估小組），以評估一名或多名候選人是否適合根據第 205、207、208 或 227 條進行任命。
(2) The regulations may make provision for and in relation to assessment panels.
(2) 條例可以對評估小組作出規定。
(3) Without limiting subsection (2), the regulations may make provision for and in relation to the following:
(3) 在不限制第(2)款的情況下，條例可以就下列內容作出規定：
(a) the establishment of assessment panels;
(a) 設立評估小組；
(b) the composition of assessment panels;
(b) 評估小組的組成；
(c) the operation and procedures of assessment panels;
(c) 評估小組的運作和程序；
(d) the methodology to be used by assessment panels in assessing candidates for appointment as a member;
(d) 評估小組在評估任命為成員的候選人時所使用的方法；
(e) the provision of assistance by the Department to assessment panels, including secretariat services and clerical assistance.
(e) 該部向評估小組提供協助，包括秘書處服務和文書協助。

title: 210 Appointment of a Judge not to affect tenure etc.
zh: 第210條 法官的任命不影響任期等
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
(1) The appointment of a Judge as a member, or service by a Judge as a member, does not affect:
(1) 任命法官為成員或法官擔任成員的服務不影響：
(a) the Judge’s tenure of office as a Judge; or
(a) 法官的任期；或
(b) the Judge’s rank, title, status, precedence, salary, annual or other allowances or other rights or privileges as the holder of the Judge’s office as a Judge.
(b) 法官的職級、頭銜、地位、優先順序、薪水、年度津貼或其他津貼或作為法官職位持有者的其他權利或特權。
(2) For all purposes, the Judge’s service as a member is taken to be service as a Judge.
(2) 就所有目的而言，法官作為成員的服務被視為作為法官的服務。
(3) A member who is a Judge ceases to hold office as a member if the member ceases to be a Judge.
(3) 擔任法官的會員如果不再擔任法官，則不再擔任會員職務。

title: 211 Extension of appointment
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
(1) The Minister may, at the request of the President and by written instrument, extend a member’s appointment if, apart from this section, the member’s appointment would cease to have effect (other than under section 220 or 221) on a day (the cessation day ).
(1) 若除本條規定外，該成員的任命在某一天（終止日）不再有效（第 220 或 221 條規定的情況除外），則部長可應主席的請求並透過書面文書延長該成員的任命。
(2) The extension must be made before the cessation day.
(2) 延期必須在終止日之前進行。
(3) The extended appointment has effect until the earliest of the following:
(3) 延長任命的有效期限至下列時間（以最早者為準）：
(a) the end of the period of 3 months after the cessation day;
(a) 終止日後 3 個月期間結束；
(b) if the member gives a resignation under section 220—the time when that resignation takes effect;
(b) 若該成員依第 220 條提出辭職－該辭職生效的時間；
(c) if the extended appointment is terminated under section 221—the time when that termination takes effect.
(c) 若延長任用依第 221 條終止－該終止生效的時間。
(4) An instrument made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.
(4) 依第 (1) 款制定的文書並非立法文書。

title: 212 Acting appointments
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
President
總統
(1) The Minister may, by written instrument, appoint a person to act as the President:
(1) 部長可以透過書面文書任命一人擔任主席：
(a) during a vacancy in the office of President (whether or not an appointment has previously been made to the office); or
(a) 在主席職位空缺期間（無論之前是否對該職位進行過任命）；或
(b) during any period, or during all periods, when the President:
(b) 在任何時期或所有時期，當主席：
(i) is absent from duty or from Australia; or
(i) 缺席或離開澳洲；或
(ii) is, for any reason, unable to perform the duties of the office.
(ii) 因任何原因無法履行職務。
Note: For rules that apply to acting appointments, see sections 33AB and 33A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 .
注意：有關適用於代理任命的規則，請參閱 1901 年《行為解釋法》第 33AB 和 33A 條。
(2) A person must not be appointed to act as the President in the circumstances mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) (vacancy in the office of President) unless:
(2) 在第 (1)(a) 款（主席職位空缺）所提及的情況下，不得任命某人擔任主席，除非：
(a) the person is qualified, as mentioned in subsection 205(3), to be appointed as the President; and
(a) 如第 205(3) 條所述，此人有資格被任命為總統；和
(b) the Minister has consulted the Chief Justice of the Federal Court.
(b) 部長已諮詢聯邦法院首席法官。
(2A) A person must not be appointed to act as the President in the circumstances mentioned in paragraph (1)(b) (absence, etc.) unless:
(2A) 在第 (1)(b) 款（缺席等）提及的情況下，不得任命某人擔任主席，除非：
(a) either:
(a) 任一：
(i) the person is qualified, as mentioned in subsection 205(3), to be appointed as the President; and
(i) 如第 205(3) 條所述，此人有資格被任命為總統；和
(ii) the Minister has consulted the Chief Justice of the Federal Court; or
(ii) 部長已諮詢聯邦法院首席法官；或
(b) the person is a member who is a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President.
(b) 此人是非司法副主席的成員。
(2B) An appointment of a member who is a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President to act as the President as mentioned in paragraph (2A)(b) must not be for a period of more than 3 weeks.
(2B) 任命一名非司法副主席擔任第 (2A)(b) 段所述的主席，任期不得超過 3 週。
Other members
其他成員
(3) The Minister may, at the request of the President and by written instrument, appoint a person to act as a member other than the President:
(3) 部長可以根據主席的要求並透過書面文件任命一人擔任主席以外的成員：
(a) during a vacancy in the office of a member other than the President (whether or not an appointment has previously been made to the office); or
(a) 在主席以外的成員職位空缺期間（無論之前是否對該職位進行過任命）；或
(b) during any period, or during all periods, when a member other than the President:
(b) 在任何時期或所有時期，主席以外的成員：
(i) is absent from duty or from Australia; or
(i) 缺席或離開澳洲；或
(ii) is, for any reason, unable to perform the duties of the office.
(ii) 因任何原因無法履行職務。
Note: For rules that apply to acting appointments, see sections 33AB and 33A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 .
注意：有關適用於代理任命的規則，請參閱 1901 年《行為解釋法》第 33AB 和 33A 條。
(4) A person must not be appointed to act as a member other than the President unless:
(4) 不得任命任何人擔任主席以外的成員，除非：
(a) if the person is to act as a Judicial Deputy President:
(a) 若此人擔任司法副院長：
(i) the person is qualified, as mentioned in subsection 206(3), to be appointed as a Judicial Deputy President; and
(i) 如第 206(3) 條所述，此人有資格被任命為司法副院長；和
(ii) the Minister has consulted the Chief Justice of the court of which the person is a Judge; or
(ii) 部長已諮詢該人擔任法官的法院首席法官；或
(b) if the person is to act as a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President—the person is qualified, as mentioned in subsection 207(3), to be appointed as a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President; or
(b) 若此人將擔任非司法副總統－如第 207(3) 款所述，此人有資格被任命為非司法副總統；或
(c) if the person is to act as a senior member—the person is qualified, as mentioned in subsection 208(3), to be appointed as a senior member; or
(c) 若此人將擔任高級會員－如第 208(3) 款所述，此人有資格被任命為高級會員；或
(d) if the person is to act as a general member—the person is qualified, as mentioned in subsection 208(4), to be appointed as a general member.
(d) 若該人將擔任普通會員－如第 208(4) 款所述，該人有資格被任命為普通會員。
Extension of acting appointment
延長署理委任
(5) If a person has been appointed under this section to act as a member, the Minister may extend the person’s appointment if the Minister is satisfied that it is necessary to do so by reason of a pending proceeding or other special circumstances.
(5) 如果某人已根據本條被任命為成員，並且部長認為由於未決訴訟或其他特殊情況有必要延長該任命，則部長可以延長該任命。
(6) The extension must be made:
(6) 延期必須：
(a) in writing; and
(a) 以書面形式；和
(b) before the day that the member who was absent or unable to perform the duties of the member’s office returns to perform those duties.
(b) 在缺席或無法履行會員職務的會員返回履行這些職責之日之前。
(7) The extension must not be for more than:
(7) 延期不得超過：
(a) unless paragraph (b) applies—12 months; or
(a) 除非(b)段適用－12個月；或
(b) in the case of a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President appointed to act as the President as mentioned in paragraph (2A)(b)—3 weeks.
(b) 若非司法副總統被任命為第 (2A)(b) 段所述的總統，則為 3 週。

title: 213 Oath or affirmation of office
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
(1) A person who is appointed or reappointed as a member or to act as a member must, before beginning to discharge the duties of the member’s office, take an oath or affirmation.
(1) 被任命或重新任命為會員或擔任會員的人，在開始履行會員職務之前，必須宣誓或確認。
(2) The oath or affirmation is an oath or affirmation that the person will well and truly serve in the office, and do right to all manner of people according to law without fear or favour, affection or ill ‑ will.
(2) 宣誓或誓言是指該人將在辦公室中良好、真實地服務，並依法善待所有人，不畏懼、不偏袒、不感情、不惡意。
(3) An oath or affirmation to be taken by the President must be taken before:
(3) 主席必須在以下時間之前宣誓或宣誓：
(a) the Governor ‑ General; or
(a) 總督；或
(b) a Justice of the High Court; or
(b) 高等法院法官；或
(c) a Judge of the Federal Court; or
(c) 聯邦法院法官；或
(d) a Judge of the Supreme Court of a State or a Territory.
(d) 州或地區最高法院的法官。
(4) An oath or affirmation to be taken by a member other than the President must be taken before:
(4) 主席以外的其他成員必須在以下時間之前宣誓或宣誓：
(a) the Governor ‑ General; or
(a) 總督；或
(b) a Justice of the High Court; or
(b) 高等法院法官；或
(c) a Judge of the Federal Court; or
(c) 聯邦法院法官；或
(d) a Judge of the Supreme Court of a State or a Territory; or
(d) 州或地區最高法院的法官；或
(e) the President.
(e) 主席。

title: Subdivision B — Members’ terms and conditions
zh: B 部分 — 會員條款與條件
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Members’ terms and conditions

title: 214 Remuneration
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Members’ terms and conditions
text:
(1) A non ‑ judicial member is to be paid the remuneration that is determined by the Remuneration Tribunal. If no determination of that remuneration by the Remuneration Tribunal is in operation, the member is to be paid the remuneration that is prescribed by the rules.
(1) 非司法成員應獲得由薪酬法庭決定的薪酬。若薪酬法庭未對薪酬作出決定，則應向會員支付規則規定的薪酬。
(2) A non ‑ judicial member is to be paid the allowances that are prescribed by the rules.
(2) 非司法人員應享有規則規定的津貼。
(3) This section has effect subject to the Remuneration Tribunal Act 1973 .
(3) 本條的效力受《1973 年薪酬法庭法》的約束。

title: 215 Leave
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Members’ terms and conditions
text:
Salaried members
受薪會員
(1) A salaried member has the recreation leave entitlements that are determined by the Remuneration Tribunal.
(1) 受薪員工享有由薪酬法庭決定的娛樂假權利。
(2) The Minister may grant the President leave of absence, other than recreation leave, on the terms and conditions as to remuneration or otherwise that the Minister determines.
(2) 部長可以按照有關報酬的條款和條件或部長確定的其他方式準許總統休假（娛樂假除外）。
(3) The President may grant a salaried member (other than the President) leave of absence, other than recreation leave, on the terms and conditions as to remuneration or otherwise that the President determines.
(3) 主席可以依照有關報酬的條款和條件或主席確定的其他規定，準許受薪成員（主席除外）休假，但娛樂假除外。
Sessional members
會期成員
(4) The President may grant leave of absence to a sessional member on the terms and conditions that the President determines.
(4) 主席可依主席決定的條款及條件準許會期成員休假。

title: 216 Other paid work
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Members’ terms and conditions
text:
Salaried non ‑ judicial members
受薪非司法人員
(1) A non ‑ judicial member appointed on a salaried basis must not engage in paid work outside the duties of the member’s office without the President’s approval.
(1) 未經總統批准，受薪任命的非司法委員不得從事其職責以外的有薪工作。
Sessional non ‑ judicial members
會期非司法成員
(2) A non ‑ judicial member appointed on a sessional basis must not engage in any paid work that conflicts or could conflict with the proper performance of the member’s duties.
(2) 會期任命的非司法成員不得從事任何與正確履行其職責相衝突或可能相衝突的有償工作。

title: 217 Appearances before Tribunal
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Members’ terms and conditions
text:
(1) A person covered by subsection (2) must not appear in a proceeding in the Tribunal:
(1) 第 (2) 款所涵蓋的人員不得出席法庭的訴訟：
(a) as a representative of a party to the proceeding; or
(a) 作為訴訟一方的代表；或
(b) as an expert witness in the proceeding.
(b) 作為訴訟中的專家證人。
(2) The following persons are covered by this subsection:
(2) 本款涵蓋以下人士：
(a) a member;
(a) 會員；
(b) a person who ceased to be a member during:
(b) 在下列期間已不再是會員的人：
(i) the 12 months before the day of the appearance; or
(i) 出庭日前 12 個月；或
(ii) if a law of a State or Territory has the effect of prescribing a longer period before the day of the appearance—that longer period.
(ii) 若州或地區的法律具有在出庭日期之前規定較長期限的效力－該較長期限。
(3) Subsection (1) does not apply if the person has permission to appear in the proceeding from:
(3) 若該人獲准在下列程序中出庭，則第 (1) 款不適用：
(a) if the person is the President—the Minister; or
(a) 若該人是總統－部長；或
(b) in any other case—the President.
(b) 在任何其他情況下－主席。

title: 218 Disclosure of interests
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Members’ terms and conditions
text:
General duty to disclose interests
揭露利益的一般義務
(1) If a member has an interest, pecuniary or otherwise, that conflicts or could conflict with the proper performance of the member’s duties, the member must disclose the nature of the interest to the President (or, if the member is the President, the Minister).
(1) 若會員的利益（無論是金錢利益或其他利益）與正確履行其職責相衝突或可能相衝突，則該會員必須向主席（或者，如果該會員是總統，則向部長）披露該利益的性質。
Disclosure of interests relating to proceedings
與訴訟程序相關的利益揭露
(2) If a member who is:
(2) 如果會員是：
(a) a member of the Tribunal as constituted for the purposes of a proceeding; or
(a) 為訴訟目的而組成的法庭成員；或
(b) performing or exercising a function or power of the Tribunal in relation to a proceeding;
(b) 履行或行使仲裁庭與訴訟有關的職能或權力；
has an interest, pecuniary or otherwise, that conflicts or could conflict with the proper performance of the member’s duties in the proceeding, the member:
擁有與該成員在訴訟中正確履行職責相衝突或可能相衝突的利益（無論是金錢利益還是其他利益），該成員：
(c) must disclose the nature of the interest to:
(c) 必須向下列人員揭露權益的性質：
(i) the parties to the proceeding; and
(i) 訴訟各方；和
(ii) the President (or, if the member is the President, the Minister); and
(ii) 主席（或者，如果該成員是主席，則為部長）；和
(d) must not take part in the proceeding or exercise any powers in relation to the proceeding unless the parties and the President (or, if the member is the President, the Minister) consent.
(d) 除非當事人和主席（或者，如果該成員是總統，則為部長）同意，否則不得參與訴訟程序或行使與訴訟程序有關的任何權力。
Timing of disclosure
揭露時間
(3) A disclosure under this section must be made as soon as possible after the relevant facts have come to the member’s knowledge.
(3) 在會員了解相關事實後，必須盡快根據本條進行揭露。

title: 219 Register of interests
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Members’ terms and conditions
text:
(1) The President must keep a register of disclosures made under section 218.
(1) 總統必須保存根據第 218 條所作出的披露的登記冊。
(2) The President may keep the register by electronic means.
(2) 主席可透過電子方式保存登記冊。
(3) The register must contain, for each disclosure:
(3) 每項揭露，登記冊必須包含：
(a) the nature of the interest disclosed; and
(a) 所揭露權益的性質；和
(b) any action taken as a result of the disclosure.
(b) 因揭露而採取的任何行動。
(4) The register is not a legislative instrument.
(4) 登記冊不是立法文件。

title: 220 Resignation
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Members’ terms and conditions
text:
(1) A member may resign the member’s appointment by giving the Governor ‑ General a written resignation.
(1) 成員可以向總督提出書面辭職，以辭去成員的任命。
(2) The member must also give a copy of the written resignation to the President.
(2) 會員也必須向主席提交書面辭職報告副本。
(3) The resignation takes effect on the day it is received by the Governor ‑ General or, if a later day is specified in the resignation, on that later day.
(3) 辭職自總督收到之日起生效，或者，如果辭職中指定了較晚的日期，則在該較晚的日期生效。

title: 221 Termination of appointment
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Members’ terms and conditions
text:
(1) The Governor ‑ General may, on the recommendation of the Minister, terminate the appointment of a non ‑ judicial member if:
(1) 在下列情況下，總督可依部長的建議終止非司法成員的任命：
(a) the member is convicted of an indictable offence; or
(a) 該成員被判犯有可公訴罪行；或
(b) the member is unable to perform the duties of the member’s office because of physical or mental incapacity; or
(b) 會員因身體或精神喪失行為能力而無法履行會員職務的職責；或
(c) the member’s conduct or behaviour amounts to serious misconduct by the member; or
(c) 會員的行為或舉止構成會員的嚴重不當行為；或
(d) the member is a salaried member and is absent, except on leave of absence, for 5 consecutive days or for 10 days in any 12 months; or
(d) 該會員為受薪會員，且連續缺勤 5 天或在任何 12 個月內缺勤 10 天（請假除外）；或
(e) the member is a sessional member and is unavailable, except on leave of absence, to perform the duties of the member’s office for more than 3 months; or
(e) 該成員為會期成員，除請假外，無法履行其職務的時間超過 3 個月；或
(f) the member engages in conduct that constitutes a serious breach of the code of conduct; or
(f) 會員的行為構成嚴重違反行為準則；或
(g) the member engages in conduct that constitutes a serious breach of the performance standard; or
(g) 會員的行為嚴重違反績效標準；或
(h) the member is a salaried member and engages, except with the President’s approval, in paid work outside the duties of the member’s office (see subsection 216(1)); or
(h) 該會員為受薪會員，除非經主席批准，否則從事其職責以外的有薪工作（見第 216(1) 款）；或
(i) the member is a sessional member and engages in paid work that conflicts or could conflict with the proper performance of the member’s duties (see subsection 216(2)); or
(i) 該會員為會期會員，並從事與正確履行會員職責相衝突或可能相衝突的有薪工作（見第 216(2) 款）；或
(j) the member fails, without reasonable excuse, to comply with section 218 (disclosure of interests).
(j) 會員無合理理由未能遵守第 218 條（利益揭露）的規定。
(2) Without limiting the kinds of conduct that may constitute a serious breach of the code of conduct or performance standard for the purposes of paragraph (1)(f) or (g), such conduct includes:
(2) 在不限制可能構成嚴重違反第 (1)(f) 或 (g) 款目的的行為準則或績效標準的行為種類的情況下，此類行為包括：
(a) repeatedly breaching the code of conduct or performance standard; and
(a) 屢次違反行為準則或績效標準；和
(b) breaching the code of conduct or performance standard in a way that is having, or is likely to have, a damaging effect on public trust and confidence in the Tribunal; and
(b) 違反行為守則或績效標準，從而對或可能對公眾對法庭的信任和信心產生破壞性影響；和
(c) breaching the code of conduct or performance standard and failing to comply with a direction under subsection 200(1) in relation to the breach.
(c) 違反行為準則或績效標準，且未遵守第 200(1) 款中與違規相關的指示。
(3) The Governor ‑ General must terminate the appointment of a non ‑ judicial member if the member:
(3) 總督必須終止對非司法成員的任命，如果該成員：
(a) becomes bankrupt; or
(a) 破產；或
(b) applies to take the benefit of any law for the relief of bankrupt or insolvent debtors; or
(b) 適用於利用任何法律救濟破產或資不抵債的債務人；或
(c) compounds with the member’s creditors; or
(c) 與會員的債權人達成和解；或
(d) makes an assignment of the member’s remuneration for the benefit of the member’s creditors.
(d) 為了會員債權人的利益而分配會員的報酬。

title: 222 President must notify Minister about grounds for termination
zh: 第222章 總統必須通知部長終止合約的理由
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Members’ terms and conditions
text:
If the President reasonably believes that there are grounds for terminating a non ‑ judicial member’s appointment under section 221, the President must notify the Minister as soon as possible.
如果總統合理地認為有理由根據第 221 條終止非司法成員的任命，則總統必須盡快通知部長。

title: 223 Additional terms and conditions
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Members’ terms and conditions
text:
A non ‑ judicial member holds office on the terms and conditions (if any) in relation to matters not covered by this Act that are determined by the Minister.
非司法成員依照部長確定的與本法未涵蓋的事項有關的條款和條件（如果有）任職。

title: Division 4 — Management of Tribunal
zh: 第 4 分部 — 仲裁庭的管理
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal

title: Subdivision A — Management functions of President
zh: A 分部 — 總裁的管理職能
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision A — Management functions of President

title: 224 Management of administrative affairs of Tribunal
zh: 第224條 法庭行政事務的管理
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision A — Management functions of President
text:
(1) The President is responsible for managing the administrative affairs of the Tribunal.
(1) 庭長負責管理法庭的行政事務。
(2) The administrative affairs of the Tribunal do not include the corporate and registry services of the Tribunal.
(2) 仲裁庭的行政事務不包括仲裁庭的公司及登記服務。

title: Subdivision B — Appointment and functions of Principal Registrar
zh: B 分部 — 首席書記官長的任命與職能
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Appointment and functions of Principal Registrar

title: 225 Principal Registrar
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Appointment and functions of Principal Registrar
text:
There is to be a Chief Executive Officer and Principal Registrar of the Administrative Review Tribunal .
行政復議法庭應有一名執行長和首席書記官。

title: 226 Functions of Principal Registrar
zh: 226 首席司法常務官的職能
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Appointment and functions of Principal Registrar

title: 227 Appointment of Principal Registrar
zh: 第227章 任命首席司法常務官
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Appointment and functions of Principal Registrar
text:
Appointment by Governor ‑ General
由總督任命
(1) The Chief Executive Officer and Principal Registrar is to be appointed by the Governor ‑ General, by written instrument, on the recommendation of the Minister.
(1) 執行長和首席書記官長由總督根據部長的推薦以書面形式任命。
(2) Before the Minister makes a recommendation to the Governor ‑ General, the Minister must:
(2) 在部長向總督提出建議之前，部長必須：
(a) be satisfied that the person has appropriate qualifications, knowledge or experience ; and
(a) 確信該人具有適當的資格、知識或經驗；和
(b) be satisfied that the person was assessed, by a panel established under section 209, as suitable for the appointment through an assessment process that:
(b) 確信該人已由依第 209 條設立的小組透過以下評估程序評估為適合任命：
(i) was merit ‑ based; and
(i) 擇優錄取；和
(ii) included public advertising of the position; and
(ii) 包括該職位的公開廣告；和
(iii) complied with the requirements (if any) prescribed by the regulations; and
(iii) 符合法規規定的要求（如有）；和
(c) obtain the agreement of the President to the appointment.
(c) 獲得主席對任命的同意。
Period of appointment
聘任期限
(3) The Principal Registrar holds office for a period of 5 years.
(3) 首席書記長的任期為 5 年。
Basis of appointment
任命依據
(4) The Principal Registrar must be appointed on a salaried basis.
(4) 首席書記官必須以薪金指派。
Reappointment
重新任命
(5) Paragraph (2)(b) does not apply in relation to the reappointment of a person who, immediately before the start of the period of reappointment, holds office as the Principal Registrar under a previous appointment under subsection (1).
(5) 第(2)(b)款不適用於在緊接重新任命期限開始之前根據第(1)款的先前任命擔任首席書記官長的人的重新任命。

title: 228 Acting appointments
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Appointment and functions of Principal Registrar
text:
The President may, by written instrument, appoint a person to act as the Principal Registrar:
總統可以透過書面文書任命一人擔任首席書記官長：
(a) during a vacancy in the office of Principal Registrar (whether or not an appointment has previously been made to the office); or
(a) 在首席書記官職位空缺期間（無論之前是否已對該職位進行過任命）；或
(b) during any period, or during all periods, when the Principal Registrar:
(b) 在任何期間或所有期間，當首席書記官長：
(i) is absent from duty or from Australia; or
(i) 缺席或離開澳洲；或
(ii) is, for any reason, unable to perform the duties of the office.
(ii) 因任何原因無法履行職務。
Note: For rules that apply to acting appointments, see sections 33AB and 33A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 .
注意：有關適用於代理任命的規則，請參閱 1901 年《行為解釋法》第 33AB 和 33A 條。

title: 229 Remuneration
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Appointment and functions of Principal Registrar
text:
(1) The Principal Registrar is to be paid the remuneration that is determined by the Remuneration Tribunal. If no determination of that remuneration by the Remuneration Tribunal is in operation, the Principal Registrar is to be paid the remuneration that is prescribed by the rules.
(1) 首席書記官應領取由薪酬法庭確定的薪酬。如果薪酬審裁處沒有對薪酬作出決定，則首席書記官長應獲得規則規定的薪酬。
(2) The Principal Registrar is to be paid the allowances that are prescribed by the rules.
(2) 首席註冊官領取規則規定的津貼。
(3) This section has effect subject to the Remuneration Tribunal Act 1973 .
(3) 本條的效力受《1973 年薪酬法庭法》的約束。

title: 230 Leave
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Appointment and functions of Principal Registrar
text:
(1) The Principal Registrar has the recreation leave entitlements that are determined by the Remuneration Tribunal.
(1) 首席書記官享有由薪酬法庭決定的娛樂假權利。
(2) The President may grant the Principal Registrar leave of absence, other than recreation leave, on the terms and conditions as to remuneration or otherwise that the Minister determines.
(2) 總統可依據有關報酬的條款和條件或部長決定的其他規定，准予首席書記官休假（娛樂假除外）。

title: 231 Other paid work
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Appointment and functions of Principal Registrar
text:
The Principal Registrar must not engage in paid work outside the duties of the Principal Registrar’s office without the President’s approval.
未經總統批准，首席書記官不得從事首席書記官辦公室職責以外的有償工作。

title: 232 Disclosure of interests
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Appointment and functions of Principal Registrar
text:
(1) A disclosure by the Principal Registrar under section 29 of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 (which deals with the duty to disclose interests) must be made to the President.
(1) 首席書記官根據《2013 年公共治理、績效和問責法》第 29 條（涉及披露利益的義務）必須向總統進行披露。
(2) Subsection (1) applies in addition to any rules made for the purposes of that section.
(2) 除為本節目的而製定的任何規則外，第 (1) 款也適用。
(3) For the purposes of this Act and the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 , the Principal Registrar is taken not to have complied with section 29 of that Act if the Principal Registrar does not comply with subsection (1) of this section.
(3) 就本法和 2013 年《公共治理、績效和責任法》而言，如果首席登記官不遵守本條第 (1) 款的規定，則視為首席登記官未遵守該法第 29 條的規定。

title: 233 Resignation
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Appointment and functions of Principal Registrar
text:
(1) The Principal Registrar may resign the Principal Registrar’s appointment by giving the Governor ‑ General a written resignation.
(1) 首席書記官可以向總督提出書面辭職，並辭去首席書記官的任命。
(2) The resignation takes effect on the day it is received by the Governor ‑ General or, if a later day is specified in the resignation, on that later day.
(2) 辭職自總督收到之日起生效，或者，如果辭職中指定了較晚的日期，則在該較晚的日期生效。

title: 234 Termination of appointment
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Appointment and functions of Principal Registrar
text:
(1) The Governor ‑ General may, on the recommendation of the Minister, terminate the appointment of the Principal Registrar if:
(1) 在下列情況下，總督可依部長的建議終止首席書記官長的任命：
(a) the Principal Registrar is convicted of an indictable offence; or
(a) 首席書記官被判犯有可公訴罪行；或
(b) the Principal Registrar is unable to perform the duties of the Principal Registrar’s office because of physical or mental incapacity; or
(b) 首席書記官因身體或精神上無行為能力而無法履行首席書記官辦公室的職責；或
(c) the Principal Registrar’s conduct or behaviour amounts to serious misconduct by the Principal Registrar; or
(c) 首席書記官長的行為或舉止構成首席書記官長的嚴重不當行為；或
(d) the Minister is satisfied that the performance of the Principal Registrar has been unsatisfactory for a significant period; or
(d) 部長信納首席書記官長的表現在相當長的一段時間內不能令人滿意；或
(e) the Principal Registrar is absent, except on leave of absence, for 5 consecutive days or for 10 days in any 12 months; or
(e) 首席書記官缺席連續 5 天或在任何 12 個月內缺席 10 天，請假除外；或
(f) the Principal Registrar engages, except with the President’s approval, in paid work outside the duties of the Principal Registrar’s office (see section 231); or
(f) 除非經總統批准，首席書記官長從事首席書記官長辦公室職責以外的有薪工作（見第 231 條）；或
(g) the Principal Registrar fails, without reasonable excuse, to comply with section 29 of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 (which deals with the duty to disclose interests) or rules made for the purposes of that section.
(g) 主登記官無合理理由未能遵守《2013 年公共治理、績效和問責法》第 29 條（該法涉及披露利益的義務）或為本條目的製定的規則。
(1A) Before the Minister makes a recommendation to the Governor ‑ General, the Minister must consult the President.
(1A) 在部長向總督提出建議之前，部長必須諮詢總統。
(2) The Governor ‑ General must terminate the appointment of the Principal Registrar if the Principal Registrar:
(2) 若首席書記官長出現以下情況，總督必須終止首席書記官長的任命：
(a) becomes bankrupt; or
(a) 破產；或
(b) applies to take the benefit of any law for the relief of bankrupt or insolvent debtors; or
(b) 適用於利用任何法律救濟破產或資不抵債的債務人；或
(c) compounds with the Principal Registrar’s creditors; or
(c) 與首席書記官長的債權人達成和解；或
(d) makes an assignment of the Principal Registrar’s remuneration for the benefit of the Principal Registrar’s creditors.
(d) 為了主要書記官長債權人的利益，分配首席書記官長的薪酬。

title: 235 Additional terms and conditions
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Appointment and functions of Principal Registrar
text:
The Principal Registrar holds office on the terms and conditions (if any) in relation to matters not covered by this Act that are determined by the Minister.
首席書記官根據部長確定的本法未涵蓋事項的條款和條件（如果有）任職。

title: Subdivision C — Leadership of Tribunal
zh: C 分部 — 仲裁庭的領導
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal

title: 236 Tribunal Advisory Committee
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
(1) The Tribunal Advisory Committee is established by this section.
(1) 仲裁庭諮詢委員會依本條設立。
Membership
會員資格
(2) The Tribunal Advisory Committee consists of:
(2) 仲裁庭諮詢委員會由下列人員組成：
(a) the President; and
(a) 主席；和
(b) the Principal Registrar; and
(b) 首席書記長；和
(c) the jurisdictional area leaders; and
（三）轄區領導；和
(d) such other members or staff members as are nominated in writing by the President.
(d) 其他主席書面提名的成員或工作人員。
(3) The President is the Chair of the Tribunal Advisory Committee.
(3) 庭長擔任仲裁庭諮詢委員會主席。
Functions
功能
(4) The Tribunal Advisory Committee has the following functions:
(4) 仲裁庭諮詢委員會具有下列職能：
(a) to promote the Tribunal’s objective in section 9;
(a) 促進法庭達成第 9 條的目標；
(b) to promote the training, education and professional development of members;
(b) 促進會員的訓練、教育和專業發展；
(c) to oversee the caseload of the Tribunal;
(c) 監督法庭的案件量；
(d) to review the performance of the Tribunal, including its financial performance;
(d) 審查法庭的業績，包括其財務業績；
(e) to oversee trends and patterns across, and systemic issues arising in, the jurisdictional areas;
(e) 監督管轄範圍內的趨勢和模式以及出現的系統性問題；
(f) to advise the President and the Principal Registrar on any matter relating to the above functions;
(f) 就與上述職能有關的任何事宜向院長和首席書記官長提出建議；
(g) to advise the President on any matter relating to the code of conduct, the performance standard or the practice directions;
(g) 就與行為準則、績效標準或實務指示有關的任何事項向主席提供建議；
(h) to do anything incidental to the performance of the above functions.
(h) 做與履行上述職能相關的任何事情。
(5) In performing the functions of the Tribunal Advisory Committee, the members of the Committee (other than a member of the Committee who is a Judge) must have regard to any views expressed by stakeholders.
(5) 在執行法庭諮詢委員會的職能時，委員會成員（委員會成員中的法官除外）必須考慮利害關係人表達的任何意見。
(6) Subsection (5) does not apply if the matter relates to a particular proceeding in the Tribunal.
(6) 若該事項與仲裁庭的特定程序有關，則第 (5) 款不適用。
Meetings
會議
(7) The President must convene such meetings of the Tribunal Advisory Committee as are necessary for the performance of the Committee’s functions.
(7) 庭長必須召集法庭諮詢委員會執行委員會職能所需的會議。
(8) The President must preside at all meetings at which the President is present.
(8) 主席必須主持主席出席的所有會議。
(9) If the President is unable to attend a meeting, the President must nominate another member of the Tribunal Advisory Committee to preside at the meeting.
(9) 若庭長無法出席會議，庭長必須提名仲裁庭諮詢委員會的另一位成員主持會議。

title: Division 5 — Staff and consultants
zh: 第 5 分部 — 員工與顧問
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal

title: 237 Appointment of registrars
zh: 第237條 註冊官的任命
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
Appointment by Principal Registrar
首席司法常務官的任命
(1) A registrar is to be appointed by the Principal Registrar by written instrument.
(1) 書記官長由首席書記官長以書面任命。
Qualification for appointment
任職資格
(2) A person must not be appointed as a registrar unless:
(2) 任何人不得被任命為登記官，除非：
(a) the person is a staff member; and
(a) 該人是一名工作人員；和
(b) the person:
(b) 該人：
(i) has obtained a degree from a university, or an educational qualification of a similar standing, in the field of law; or
(i) 已取得法律領域的大學學位或類似資格的教育資格；或
(ii) has obtained an educational qualification, or has training or experience, related to dispute resolution; or
(ii) 已取得與爭議解決相關的教育資格，或具有相關訓練或經驗；或
(iii) has, in the opinion of the Principal Registrar, experience related to one or more functions or powers of the Tribunal.
(iii) 首席書記官認為具有與法庭一項或多項職能或權力有關的經驗。
Registrar in each State, in the Australian Capital Territory and in the Northern Territory
各州、澳洲首都領地和北領地的登記官
(3) The Principal Registrar must ensure that at least one registrar is appointed in each State, in the Australian Capital Territory and in the Northern Territory.
(3) 首席書記官必須確保每個州、澳洲首都領地和北領地至少任命一名書記官。

title: 238 Staff
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
(1) The staff of the Tribunal must be persons engaged under the Public Service Act 1999 .
(1) 法庭工作人員必須是依據 1999 年公共服務法聘用的人員。
(2) For the purposes of the Public Service Act 1999 :
(2) 就《1999 年公共服務法》而言：
(a) the Principal Registrar and the APS employees assisting the Principal Registrar together constitute a Statutory Agency; and
(a) 首席註冊官和協助首席註冊官的 APS 員工共同構成法定機構；和
(b) the Principal Registrar is the Head of that Statutory Agency.
(b) 書記官長是該法定機構的負責人。

title: 239 APS employees and others made available
zh: 239 名 APS 員工和其他人員可用
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
(1) The Tribunal may be assisted by the following persons, whose services are made available to the Tribunal in connection with the performance or exercise of any of the Tribunal’s functions or powers:
(1) 仲裁庭可由下列人員協助，他們的服務是在仲裁庭履行或行使任何職能或權力時向仲裁庭提供的：
(a) an employee of an Agency (within the meaning of the Public Service Act 1999 );
(a) 機構僱員（1999 年《公共服務法》的涵義內）；
(b) an officer of the Supreme Court of Norfolk Island.
(b) 諾福克島最高法院的一名官員。
(2) When performing services for the Tribunal under subsection (1), a person is subject to the directions of the Principal Registrar.
(2) 在根據第 (1) 款為法庭提供服務時，任何人須服從首席書記官長的指示。

title: 240 Consultants
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
The Principal Registrar may, on behalf of the Commonwealth, engage consultants to assist in the performance of the Tribunal’s functions.
首席書記官長可以代表聯邦聘請顧問協助法庭履行職能。

title: Division 6 — Application of finance law and reporting requirements
zh: 第 6 分部 — 金融法的適用和報告要求
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Division 6 — Application of finance law and reporting requirements

title: 241 Application of finance law
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Division 6 — Application of finance law and reporting requirements
text:
For the purposes of the finance law (within the meaning of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 ):
就《金融法》而言（《2013 年公共治理、績效與問責法》意義內）：
(a) the following group of persons is a listed entity:
(a) 下列人員屬於名單所列實體：
(i) the Principal Registrar;
(i) 首席書記長；
(ii) the staff members;
㈡ 工作人員；
(iii) persons engaged under subsection 90(1);
(iii) 依第 90(1) 款聘用的人員；
(iv) consultants engaged under section 240; and
(iv) 根據第 240 條聘請的顧問；和
(b) the listed entity is to be known as the Administrative Review Tribunal; and
(b) 所列實體稱為行政復議法庭；和
(c) the Principal Registrar is the accountable authority of the listed entity; and
(c) 主要註冊官是上市實體的問責機構；和
(d) the persons mentioned in paragraph (a) are officials of the listed entity; and
(d) (a) 段所提及的人員是名單所列實體的官員；和
(e) the purposes of the listed entity include the functions of the Principal Registrar mentioned in section 226.
(e) 上市實體的目的包括第 226 條所提及的主要註冊官的職能。

title: 242 Report by President
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
Division 6 — Application of finance law and reporting requirements
text:
(1) As soon as practicable after 30 June in each financial year, the President must prepare a report on the management of the administrative affairs of the Tribunal during the financial year.
(1) 每個財政年度 6 月 30 日後，庭長必須在切實可行的情況下盡快編寫一份關於該財政年度法庭行政事務管理的報告。
(2) The report for a financial year must include:
(2) 財政年度報告必須包括：
(a) a description of any measures taken by the Tribunal during that year to pursue the objective in section 9; and
(a) 說明法庭在當年為實現第 9 條的目標所採取的任何措施；和
(b) an assessment of the operation of each jurisdictional area during that year; and
(b) 對當年各管轄區運作情況的評估；和
(c) an assessment of the operation of the Tribunal constituted by the guidance and appeals panel for the purposes of proceedings during that year; and
(c) 對指導和上訴小組為該年訴訟目的組成的法庭運作情況進行評估；和
(d) the number of applications made during the year to the Tribunal for review of decisions; and
(d) 年內向法庭提出複審決定的申請數量；和
(e) particulars of the results of reviews of decisions by the Tribunal during the year; and
(e) 法庭年內裁決審查結果的詳情；和
(f) the number of guidance and appeals panel proceedings in the Tribunal during that year, and particulars of the results of those proceedings; and
(f) 該年法庭的指導和上訴小組程序的數量，以及這些程序結果的詳情；和
(g) the number of proceedings in the Tribunal involving non ‑ participating parties during that year; and
(g) 當年法庭涉及非參與方的訴訟數量；和
(h) a summary of any actions taken by the Tribunal under section 185 (referring questions of law) during that year; and
(h) 當年法庭根據第 185 條（涉及法律問題）採取的任何行動的摘要；和
(ha) the number of decisions made in accordance with section 103 (if parties reach agreement—review of decisions only) during that year in each jurisdictional area and by the Tribunal as constituted by the guidance and appeals panel for the purposes of proceedings; and
(ha) 當年每個司法管轄區以及由指導和上訴小組組成的法庭為訴訟目的根據第 103 條（如果當事各方達成一致——僅審查決定）作出的決定數量；和
(hb) the number of Tribunal decisions affirmed by a federal court during that year; and
(hb) 當年聯邦法院確認的法庭裁決數量；和
(hc) the number of Tribunal decisions overturned by a federal court during that year; and
(hc) 當年被聯邦法院推翻的法庭裁決數量；和
(i) a summary of any actions taken by the President or jurisdictional area leaders during that year to:
(i) 總統或轄區領導人在這一年中為以下目的所採取的任何行動的摘要：
(i) identify systemic issues related to the making of reviewable decisions arising in the caseload of the Tribunal; and
(i) 找出法庭案件中出現的與作出可審查決定有關的系統性問題；和
(ii) inform relevant Ministers, relevant Commonwealth entities and the Council of those issues; and
(ii) 將這些問題通知相關部長、相關英聯邦實體和理事會；和
(j) an overview of any actions taken during that year (including any actions taken under section 203) in relation to:
(j) 當年採取的任何行動概述（包括根據第 203 條採取的任何行動）：
(i) non ‑ judicial members upholding the code of conduct; or
(i) 維護行為準則的非司法成員；或
(ii) non ‑ judicial members meeting the performance standard; or
(ii) 符合績效標準的非司法成員；或
(iii) the training, education and professional development of members; and
(iii) 會員的培訓、教育和專業發展；和
(k) a description of any measures taken by the President during that year to engage with:
(k) 描述總統在該年採取的任何措施：
(i) civil society; or
㈠ 民間社會；或
(ii) persons whose interests are affected by reviewable decisions; and
(ii) 利益受到可審查決定影響的人；和
(l) any other information prescribed by the rules.
(l) 規則規定的其他資訊。
(3) A report prepared under this section after 30 June in a year must be given to the Minister by 15 October of that year.
(3) 每年 6 月 30 日之後根據本節準備的報告必須在該年 10 月 15 日之前提交給部長。
(4) The Minister must cause a copy of the report to be tabled in each House of the Parliament within 15 sitting days of that House after the report is given to the Minister.
(4) 部長必須在報告提交給部長後的 15 天內將報告副本提交給議會各議院。
(5) A report prepared under this section may be included in a report prepared and given to the Minister under section 46 of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 in relation to the Tribunal.
(5) 根據本節所準備的報告可以包含在根據《2013 年公共治理、績效和問責法》第 46 節準備並提交給部長的與法庭有關的報告中。

title: Division 7 — Other matters concerning management
zh: 第 7 分部 — －其他有關管理的事項
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal

title: 243 Registries
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
The Minister must cause such registries of the Tribunal to be established as the Minister thinks fit, but so that at least one registry shall be established in each State, in the Australian Capital Territory and in the Northern Territory.
部長必須促使建立部長認為合適的法庭登記處，但每個州、澳洲首都領地和北領地至少應設立一個登記處。

title: 244 Proceedings arising out of management of Tribunal
zh: 第244章 法庭管理引起的訴訟
path: Part 8 — Members and staff of Tribunal
text:
Any judicial or other proceeding relating to a matter arising out of the management of the administrative affairs of the Tribunal, including any proceeding relating to anything done by the President or the Principal Registrar under Divisions 4 to 7, may be instituted by or against the Commonwealth.
與法庭行政事務管理所引起的事項有關的任何司法或其他程序，包括與庭長或首席書記官長根據第 4 至 7 條所做的任何事情有關的任何程序，可由聯邦提起或針對聯邦提起。

title: Part 9 — Administrative Review Council
zh: 第 9 部 — 行政覆核委員會

title: 245 Simplified outline of this Part
zh: 第245章 本部分的簡化概要
text:
This Part establishes the Administrative Review Council. The Council is separate from the Tribunal.
本部設立行政復議委員會。理事會與法庭是分開的。
The Council does not review individual decisions. Its functions relate to the Commonwealth administrative law system. Those functions include matters relating to:
理事會不審查個人決定。其職能涉及英聯邦行政法體系。這些職能包括以下事項：
(a) monitoring the integrity and operation of the Commonwealth administrative law system; and
(a) 監督聯邦行政法律體系的完整性和運作；和
(b) inquiring into and reporting on matters related to the making of administrative decisions and the exercise of administrative discretions; and
（二）調查、報告與作出行政決定及行使行政裁量權有關的事項；和
(c) supporting education and training in relation to the Commonwealth administrative law system, the making of administrative decisions and the exercise of administrative discretions.
(c) 支持與英聯邦行政法體系、行政決策的製定和行政裁量權的行使有關的教育和培訓。
The Council consists of the President, the Commonwealth Ombudsman, the Australian Information Commissioner and other members appointed by the Governor ‑ General. To be appointed, a member must have knowledge or experience in a specified area, or be a senior official of a Commonwealth entity. The Governor ‑ General appoints one of the members to be the Chair of the Council.
該委員會由總統、聯邦監察員、澳洲資訊專員和總督任命的其他成員組成。要獲得任命，成員必須具備特定領域的知識或經驗，或是英聯邦實體的高級官員。總督任命其中一名成員擔任理事會主席。
The staff assisting the Council are to be APS employees in the Department whose services are made available to the Council. For the purposes of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 , the Council is part of the Department.
協助理事會的工作人員應是該部門的 APS 僱員，他們的服務是為理事會提供的。就《2013 年公共治理、績效和問責法》而言，該委員會是該部門的一部分。
The Council must report annually in relation to its operations and some systemic issues related to the making of reviewable decisions.
理事會必須每年報告其運作以及與做出可審查決定有關的一些系統性問題。

title: 246 Administrative Review Council
text:
The Administrative Review Council is established by this section.
依本條規定設立行政複議委員會。

title: 247 Membership of Council
text:
(1) The Administrative Review Council consists of the following members:
(一)行政復議委員會由下列成員組成：
(a) the President;
(a) 主席；
(b) the Commonwealth Ombudsman;
(b) 聯邦監察員；
(c) the Australian Information Commissioner;
(c) 澳洲資訊專員；
(d) at least 3, but not more than 10, other members.
(d) 至少 3 名但不超過 10 名其他成員。
(2) The performance or exercise of the functions or powers of the Council is not affected by reason of the number of appointed members falling below 3 for less than 6 months.
（二）當選委員人數減少到三人以下且時間不滿六個月的，不影響理事會履行或行使職權。

title: 248 Application of finance law
text:
(1) For the purposes of paragraph (a) of the definition of Department of State in section 8 of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 , the Administrative Review Council is prescribed in relation to the Department.
(1) 就《2013 年公共治理、績效和問責法》第 8 條中國務院定義 (a) 段而言，行政審查委員會是針對該部門而規定的。
(2) If a Council member is an official of a Commonwealth entity other than the Department, then, for the purposes of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 , the Council member is not an official of the Department merely because they are a Council member.
(2) 如果理事會成員是該部門以外的英聯邦實體的官員，那麼，就《2013 年公共治理、績效和問責法》而言，該理事會成員不能僅因為其是理事會成員而成為該部門的官員。

title: Division 3 — Council functions etc.
zh: 第 3 分部 — 理事會職能等

title: 249 Functions and powers of Council
zh: 第249條 理事會的功能與權力
text:
(1) The Council has the following functions:
（一）理事會行使下列職權：
(a) to monitor the integrity and operation of the Commonwealth administrative law system;
(a) 監督聯邦行政法律體系的完整性和運作；
(b) to:
(b) 至：
(i) inquire into the adequacy of procedures used in relation to the making of administrative decisions and the exercise of administrative discretions; and
(i) 調查與作出行政決定和行使行政裁量權有關的程序是否充分；和
(ii) consult and advise in relation to those procedures;
(ii) 就這些程序進行諮詢和提供建議；
(c) to inquire into systemic issues related to the making of administrative decisions and the exercise of administrative discretions;
(c) 調查與作出行政決定和行使行政裁量權有關的系統性問題；
(d) to inquire into the availability, accessibility and effectiveness of review of administrative decisions and administrative discretions;
(d) 調查行政決定和行政裁量權審查的可用性、可及性和有效性；
(e) to develop and publish guidance in relation to the making of administrative decisions and the exercise of administrative discretions;
(e) 制定和發布有關行政決策和行政裁量權行使的指南；
(f) to support education and training for officials of Commonwealth entities in relation to:
(f) 支持對英聯邦實體官員進行以下方面的教育和培訓：
(i) making administrative decisions and exercising administrative discretions; and
(i) 作出行政決定和行使行政裁量權；和
(ii) the Commonwealth administrative law system;
(ii) 英聯邦行政法體系；
(g) any other function conferred on the Council by this Act or another Act;
(g) 本法或其他法賦予理事會的任何其他功能；
(h) to do anything incidental or conducive to the performance of any of the above functions.
(h) 做任何附帶或有利於履行任何上述職能的事情。
(2) The Council may, on its own initiative or at the request of the Minister, do any or all of the following:
(2) 理事會可自行或應部長的要求，採取以下任何或全部行動：
(a) inquire into;
(a) 調查；
(b) prepare a report relating to;
(b) 準備一份有關下列事項的報告；
(c) make recommendations to the Minister in relation to;
(c) 就以下方面向部長提出建議；
a matter relating to any of the Council’s functions.
與理事會任何職能有關的事宜。
(3) The Council may do all things necessary or convenient to be done for or in connection with the performance of its functions.
(3) 理事會可以為履行其職能或與履行其職能有關而採取一切必要或方便的行動。
(4) A reference in this Division to an administrative decision or an administrative discretion includes a reference to an administrative decision made, or administrative discretion exercised, otherwise than under an enactment.
(4) 本節所述的行政決定或行政裁量權包括提及根據成文法之外作出的行政決定或行使的行政裁量權。

title: 250 Reports by Council
text:
(1) When the Council concludes its consideration of a matter in respect of which the Council has determined a report is to be prepared, the Council must prepare a report on the matter and give the report to the Minister.
(1) 當理事會結束對理事會決定要編寫報告的事項的審議時，理事會必須就該事項編寫一份報告並將報告提交給部長。
(2) The Minister must cause a copy of the report to be tabled in each House of the Parliament within 15 sitting days of that House after the report is given to the Minister.
(2) 部長必須在報告提交給部長後的 15 天內將報告副本提交給議會各議院。

title: 251 Meetings of Council
text:
Convening meetings
召開會議
(1) The Council must hold such meetings as are necessary for the efficient performance of its functions.
(1) 理事會必須召開有效履行其職能所需的會議。
(2) The Chair of the Council may convene a meeting at any time.
(2) 理事會主席可隨時召集會議。
Presiding at meetings
主持會議
(3) The Chair of the Council must preside at all meetings at which the Chair is present.
(3) 理事會主席必須主持主席出席的所有會議。
(4) If the Chair is not present at a meeting, the Council members present must elect one of themselves to preside at the meeting.
(4) 若主席未能出席會議，出席的理事會成員必須選出一名自行主持會議。
Quorum
法定人數
(5) At a meeting of the Council, a quorum is constituted by 5 Council members.
(5) 理事會會議的法定人數為 5 名理事會成員。
Voting at meetings
在會議上投票
(6) A question arising at a meeting of the Council is to be determined by a majority of the votes of the Council members present and voting.
(6) 理事會會議上提出的問題須經出席並參加表決的理事會成員的過半數票決定。
(7) The person presiding at a meeting of the Council has a deliberative vote and, if the votes are equal, a casting vote.
（七）理事會會議主持人有審議票，票數相等時有決定票。
Conduct of meetings
舉行會議
(8) The Council may, subject to this Part, regulate proceedings at its meetings as it considers appropriate.
(8) 理事會可依本部分的規定，在其認為適當的情況下規範其會議的程序。
Note: Section 33B of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 contains further information about the ways in which Council members may participate in meetings.
註：1901 年《法案解釋法案》第 33B 節包含有關理事會成員參加會議的方式的更多資訊。

title: 252 Appointment of certain Council members
zh: 第252條 任命某些理事會成員
text:
(1) Appointed members are to be appointed by the Governor ‑ General by written instrument.
(1) 指定成員由總督以書面任命。
(2) An appointed member holds office on a part ‑ time basis.
(2) 指定成員兼職。

title: 253 Appointment of Chair of Council
zh: 第253章 任命理事會主席
text:
(1) One Council member is to be appointed by the Governor ‑ General by written instrument as the Chair of the Council.
(1) 理事會成員由總督以書面任命為理事會主席。
(2) An appointed member whose instrument of appointment contains a statement of the kind mentioned in subsection 255(2) (exception—appointment for specified project) cannot be appointed as the Chair of the Council.
(2) 其任命書包含第 255(2) 款中提到的那種聲明（特定項目的任命例外）的任命成員不能被任命為理事會主席。

title: 254 Qualification for appointment
text:
(1) A person is not to be appointed as an appointed member unless the person:
(1) 任何人不得被任命為指定成員，除非該人：
(a) has an extensive knowledge of administrative law or public administration; or
(a) 具有廣泛的行政法或公共行政知識；或
(b) has extensive experience providing legal services related to administrative law; or
(b) 具備提供行政法相關法律服務的豐富經驗；或
(c) has direct experience, and has direct knowledge, of the needs of people, or groups of people, significantly affected by government decisions; or
(c) 對受政府決策重大影響的人民或人群的需求有直接經驗和直接了解；或
(d) is an official of a Commonwealth entity who:
(d) 是英聯邦實體的官員，其：
(i) is an Agency Head (within the meaning of the Public Service Act 1999 ); or
(i) 是機構負責人（1999 年《公共服務法》含義內）；或
(ii) is an SES employee; or
(ii) 是 SES 員工；或
(iii) holds a position that is equivalent to, or higher than, a position occupied by an SES employee.
(iii) 所擔任的職位相當於或高於 SES 員工所擔任的職位。
Note: The expression SES employee is defined in section 2B of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 .
註：「SES 僱員」這一表述在《1901 年法案解釋法案》第 2B 節中定義。
(2) Before a person is appointed as an appointed member, the Minister must:
(2) 在某人被任命為任命成員之前，部長必須：
(a) take into account the need for a diversity of skills, expertise, experience and knowledge within the Council; and
(a) 考慮理事會內部對技能、專業知識、經驗和知識多樣性的需求；和
(b) be satisfied that:
(b) 確信：
(i) there will be at least 2 appointed members who were not officials of a Commonwealth entity immediately before their appointment; and
(i) 至少有 2 名被任命成員在任命前不是英聯邦實體的官員；和
(ii) there will be at least one appointed member of the kind mentioned in subparagraph (i) who is qualified as mentioned in paragraph (1)(c).
(ii) 至少有一位符合第 (1)(c) 款所述資格的第 (i) 項所述類型的指定成員。

title: 255 Period of appointment
text:
General rule
一般規則
(1) An appointed member holds office for the period specified in the instrument of appointment. The period must not exceed 5 years.
(1) 被任命的成員的任期在任命書規定的期限內。期限不得超過5年。
Exception—appointment for specified project
例外－指定項目的預約
(2) An instrument appointing an appointed member may state that the member is appointed for the purpose of taking part in a project specified in the instrument that is being, or is to be, undertaken by the Council.
(2) 任命一名被任命成員的文書可以規定該成員的任命是為了參加該文書中規定的理事會正在或將要進行的項目。
(3) If an instrument appointing an appointed member contains such a statement:
(3) 如果指定成員的文書包含這樣的聲明：
(a) the member is to take part in the project and has the rights of a Council member only for the purposes of taking part in the project; and
(a) 會員將參與該項目並僅出於參與該項目的目的而享有理事會成員的權利；和
(b) despite subsection (1), if the appointment has not ceased under subsection (1) and has not been terminated under section 261—the appointment ceases when the Chair of the Council certifies, in writing, that the Council has finished the project.
(b) 儘管有第 (1) 款的規定，如果任命未根據第 (1) 款終止且未根據第 261 條終止－當理事會主席以書面形式證明理事會已完成該項目時，任命終止。

title: 256 Acting appointments
text:
The Minister may, by written instrument, appoint a Council member to act as the Chair of the Council:
部長可以透過書面文書任命一名理事會成員擔任理事會主席：
(a) during a vacancy in the office of the Chair of the Council (whether or not an appointment has previously been made to the office); or
(a) 在理事會主席職位空缺期間（無論之前是否對該職位進行過任命）；或
(b) during any period, or during all periods, when the Chair of the Council:
(b) 在任何時期或所有時期，當理事會主席：
(i) is absent from duty or from Australia; or
(i) 缺席或離開澳洲；或
(ii) is, for any reason, unable to perform the duties of the office.
(ii) 因任何原因無法履行職務。
Note: For rules that apply to acting appointments, see sections 33AB and 33A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 .
注意：有關適用於代理任命的規則，請參閱 1901 年《行為解釋法》第 33AB 和 33A 條。

title: 257 Remuneration
text:
(1) An appointed member is to be paid the remuneration that is determined by the Remuneration Tribunal. If no determination of that remuneration by the Remuneration Tribunal is in operation, the appointed member is to be paid the remuneration that is prescribed by the rules.
(1) 被任命的成員應獲得由薪酬法庭決定的薪酬。如果薪酬法庭沒有確定該薪酬，則應向被任命的成員支付規則規定的薪酬。
(2) An appointed member is to be paid the allowances that are prescribed by the rules.
（二）被任命為會員的，依章程規定領取津貼。
(3) This section has effect subject to the Remuneration Tribunal Act 1973 .
(3) 本條的效力受《1973 年薪酬法庭法》的約束。

title: 258 Leave
text:
The Minister may grant leave of absence to an appointed member on the terms and conditions that the Minister determines.
部長可以根據部長確定的條款和條件向指定成員准予休假。

title: 259 Disclosure of interests
text:
(1) A Council member who has an interest, pecuniary or otherwise, in a matter being considered or about to be considered by the Council must disclose the nature of the interest to a meeting of the Council.
(1) 理事會成員在理事會正在審議或即將審議的事項中擁有金錢或其他利益時，必須向理事會會議披露該利益的性質。
(2) The disclosure must be made as soon as possible after the relevant facts have come to the Council member’s knowledge.
(2) 理事會成員知悉相關事實後，必須盡快揭露。
(3) The disclosure must be recorded in the minutes of the meeting of the Council.
（三）揭露事項應記入理事會會議紀錄。
(4) Unless the Council otherwise determines, the Council member:
(4) 除非理事會另有決定，理事會成員：
(a) must not be present during any deliberation by the Council on the matter; and
(a) 不得出席理事會就該事項進行的任何審議；和
(b) must not take part in any decision of the Council with respect to the matter.
(b) 不得參與理事會就此事所做的任何決定。
(5) For the purposes of making a determination under subsection (4), the Council member:
(5) 為了根據第 (4) 款做出決定，理事會成員：
(a) must not be present during any deliberation of the Council for the purpose of making the determination; and
(a) 不得出席理事會為作出決定而進行的任何審議；和
(b) must not take part in making the determination.
(b) 不得參與作出決定。
(6) A determination under subsection (4) must be recorded in the minutes of the meeting of the Council.
(6) 第(4)款規定的決定必須記錄在理事會會議記錄中。

title: 260 Resignation
text:
(1) An appointed member may resign the appointed member’s appointment by giving the Governor ‑ General a written resignation.
(1) 任命成員可以向總督提出書面辭職，並辭去任命成員的任命。
(2) The Chair of the Council may resign the Chair’s appointment as the Chair without resigning the Chair’s appointment as a Council member by giving the Governor ‑ General a written resignation.
(2) 理事會主席可辭去主席的任命，但無須向總督提出書面辭職，並辭去主席為理事會成員的任命。
(3) The resignation takes effect on the day it is received by the Governor ‑ General or, if a later day is specified in the resignation, on that later day.
(3) 辭職自總督收到之日起生效，或者，如果辭職中指定了較晚的日期，則在該較晚的日期生效。

title: 261 Termination of appointment
text:
Termination of appointed members
委任成員的終止
(1) The Governor ‑ General may, on the recommendation of the Minister, terminate the appointment of an appointed member if:
(1) 在下列情況下，總督可依部長的建議終止指定成員的任命：
(a) the appointed member is convicted of an indictable offence; or
(a) 被任命的成員被判犯有可公訴罪行；或
(b) the appointed member is unable to perform the duties of the appointed member’s office because of physical or mental incapacity; or
(b) 指定成員因身體或精神上無行為能力而無法履行指定成員的職責；或
(c) the appointed member’s conduct or behaviour amounts to serious misconduct by the appointed member; or
(c) 指定成員的行為或舉止構成指定成員的嚴重不當行為；或
(d) the appointed member is absent, except on leave of absence, from 3 consecutive meetings of the Council; or
(d) 被任命的成員連續 3 次缺席理事會會議，請假除外；或
(e) the appointed member fails, without reasonable excuse, to comply with section 259 (disclosure of interests).
(e) 指定成員無合理理由未遵守第 259 條（利益揭露）的規定。
(2) The Governor ‑ General must terminate the appointment of an appointed member if the appointed member:
(2) 若指定成員出現以下情況，總督必須終止其任命：
(a) becomes bankrupt; or
(a) 破產；或
(b) applies to take the benefit of any law for the relief of bankrupt or insolvent debtors; or
(b) 適用於利用任何法律救濟破產或資不抵債的債務人；或
(c) compounds with the appointed member’s creditors; or
(c) 與指定成員的債權人達成和解；或
(d) makes an assignment of the appointed member’s remuneration for the benefit of the appointed member’s creditors.
(d) 為了指定成員債權人的利益，分配指定成員的薪酬。
Termination of members appointed for a specified project
終止為特定項目任命的成員
(3) The Governor ‑ General may at any time terminate the appointment of an appointed member whose instrument of appointment contains a statement of the kind mentioned in subsection 255(2) (exception—appointment for specified project).
(3) 總督可隨時終止任命書包含第 255(2) 款所述類型聲明的指定成員的任命（例外情況－特定項目的任命）。

title: 262 Additional terms and conditions
text:
An appointed member holds office on the terms and conditions (if any) in relation to matters not covered by this Act that are determined by the Minister.
指定成員依照部長確定的與本法未涵蓋的事項有關的條款和條件（如果有）任職。

title: Division 5 — Staff to assist Council
zh: 第 5 分部 — 協助理事會的工作人員

title: 263 Arrangements relating to staff of the Department
zh: 第263章 與部門職員有關的安排
text:
(1) The staff assisting the Council are to be APS employees in the Department whose services are made available to the Council, by the Secretary of the Department, in connection with the performance or exercise of any of the Council’s functions or powers.
(1) 協助理事會的工作人員應是該部門的 APS 僱員，其服務由部門秘書向理事會提供與履行或行使理事會的任何職能或權力有關的服務。
Note: The expression APS employee is defined in section 2B of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 .
註：「APS 僱員」此表述在《1901 年法案解釋法案》第 2B 節中定義。
(2) The Secretary of the Department must consult the Chair of the Council before making staff available to the Council.
(2) 部門秘書在提供理事會工作人員之前必須諮詢理事會主席。
(3) When performing services for the Council, the staff are subject to the directions of the Council.
(3) 工作人員為理事會提供服務時，必須服從理事會的指示。

title: Division 6 — Annual report
zh: 第 6 分部 — 年度報告

title: 264 Annual report
text:
(1) After the end of each financial year, the Council must prepare and give a report to the Minister for presentation to the Parliament on the operations of the Council during that financial year.
(1) 在每個財政年度結束後，理事會必須編寫並向部長提交一份報告，以向議會提交有關理事會在該財政年度的運作情況的報告。
(2) The report for a financial year must include:
(2) 財政年度報告必須包括：
(a) a description of any systemic issues related to the making of reviewable decisions that the President has informed the Council of during that year; and
(a) 主席在當年向理事會通報的與作出可審查決定有關的任何系統性問題的描述；和
(b) a description of any information given to the Council under section 294B during that year.
(b) 當年根據第 294B 條向理事會提供的任何資訊的描述。
Note 1: One of the President’s functions is to inform relevant Ministers, relevant Commonwealth entities and the Council of any systemic issues related to the making of reviewable decisions that have been identified in the caseload of the Tribunal: see paragraph 193(i).
註 1：庭長的職責之一是向相關部長、相關英聯邦實體和理事會通報與法庭案件數量中已確定的可審查決定的製定有關的任何系統性問題：見第 193(i) 段。
Note 2: Section 294B requires Ministers and Commonwealth entities to inform the Council of action taken or proposed to be taken in relation to some systemic issues.
註 2：第 294B 條要求部長和英聯邦實體向理事會通報針對某些系統性問題已採取或擬採取的行動。
(3) The report for a financial year may include a description of any actions taken by the Council during that year in response to a systemic issue related to the making of reviewable decisions.
(3) 財政年度的報告可包括理事會在該年度為因應與可審查決策相關的系統性問題所採取的任何行動的描述。

title: Part 10 — Notice and information about administrative decision
zh: 第 10 部 — 行政決定的通知及資料
path: Part 10 — Notice and information about administrative decision

title: Division 1 — Preliminary
path: Part 10 — Notice and information about administrative decision

title: 265 Simplified outline of this Part
zh: 第265章 本部分的簡化概要
path: Part 10 — Notice and information about administrative decision
text:
Generally, decision ‑ makers must take reasonable steps to give notice of reviewable decisions to anyone whose interests are affected. This requirement also applies to some decisions that are related to reviewable decisions. Notices must include notice of any review rights and decision ‑ makers must have regard to matters prescribed by the rules.
一般來說，決策者必須採取合理步驟，向任何利益受到影響的人發出可審查決定的通知。此要求也適用於與可審查決策相關的一些決策。通知必須包括任何審查權的通知，決策者必須考慮規則規定的事項。
A person whose interests are affected by a reviewable decision may request the decision ‑ maker to give a statement of reasons for the decision. Applications can be made to the Tribunal if a statement of reasons is not given or is inadequate.
利益受到可審查決定影響的人可以要求決策者說明該決定的理由。如果沒有給出理由說明或理由說明不充分，可以向仲裁庭提出申請。
This Part contains the standard provisions for these matters. Other legislation can include provisions that apply in addition to, or instead of, these standard provisions.
本部分包含這些事項的標準規定。其他立法可以包括除這些標準條款之外或替代這些標準條款而適用的條款。

title: Division 2 — Decision ‑ makers to give notice of decisions
zh: 第 2 分部 — 決策者發出決定通知
path: Part 10 — Notice and information about administrative decision
Division 2 — Decision ‑ makers to give notice of decisions

title: 266 Decision ‑ maker to give notice of decision and review rights
zh: 266 決策者發出決定通知和審查的權利
path: Part 10 — Notice and information about administrative decision
Division 2 — Decision ‑ makers to give notice of decisions
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) If any decision in a review pathway is or would be a reviewable decision, this section applies in relation to every decision in the review pathway.
(1) 如果審查途徑中的任何決定是或將是可審查的決定，則本節適用於審查途徑中的每項決定。
(2) However, this section does not apply in relation to a decision by a court or a decision by the Tribunal under this Act.
(2) 然而，本條不適用於法院或法庭依本法所做的決定。
(3) A review pathway is a decision and any decision on review or further review of the decision.
(3) 審查途徑是一項決定以及任何關於審查的決定或對該決定的進一步審查。
General rules
一般規則
(4) The decision ‑ maker must take reasonable steps to give notice of the decision to any person whose interests are affected by the decision.
(4) 決策者必須採取合理步驟，將該決定通知利益受到該決定影響的任何人。
(5) The notice must include notice of the right (if any) to have the decision reviewed, including, for a reviewable decision, the right to apply to the Tribunal for review of the decision.
(5) 該通知必須包括複審決定的權利（如果有）的通知，包括對於可複核的決定，向仲裁庭申請複審該決定的權利。
Exceptions
例外情況
(6) However, subsection (4) does not require the decision ‑ maker to give notice if:
(6) 然而，第(4)款並未要求決策者在下列情況下發出通知：
(a) another Act or an instrument made under an Act requires notice to be given of review rights for the decision; or
(a) 另一項法案或根據一項法案製定的文書要求發出對決定的審查權的通知；或
(b) the decision is taken to have been made by:
(b) 該決定被認為是由下列人員做出的：
(i) section 16 of this Act (decision is taken to be made if timeframe expires); or
(i) 本法第 16 條（期限屆滿時將作出決定）；或
(ii) section 10 of the Ombudsman Act 1976 (unreasonable delay in exercising power); or
(ii) 1976 年《監察員法》第 10 條（無理拖延行使權力）；或
(c) the decision is:
(c) 決定是：
(i) a decision not to impose a liability, penalty or any kind of limitation on a person; or
(i) 決定不對某人施加責任、處罰或任何類型的限制；或
(ii) a decision making an adjustment to the level of periodic payments to be made to a person as a member of a class of persons where a similar adjustment is being made to the level of such payments to the other members of the class; or
(ii) 對某一類別人員的定期付款水準進行調整的決定，而對該類別其他成員的付款水準也進行了類似的調整；或
(iii) a decision that determines a person to be in the most favourable of several categories of entitlement to a monetary benefit established by an Act or an instrument made under an Act;
(iii) 一項決定，確定一個人享有某項法案或根據該法案製定的文書所規定的幾類貨幣利益中最有利的權利；
and does not adversely affect the interests of any other person.
並且不會對任何其他人的利益產生不利影響。
Effect of failure to comply
不遵守規定的影響
(7) A failure to comply with this section does not affect the validity of the decision.
(7) 不遵守本條規定並不影響決定的有效性。

title: 267 Decision ‑ maker must have regard to rules when giving notice of decision
zh: 267 決策者在發出決定通知時必須遵守規則
path: Part 10 — Notice and information about administrative decision
Division 2 — Decision ‑ makers to give notice of decisions
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) If any decision in a review pathway is or would be a reviewable decision, this section applies in relation to every decision in the review pathway.
(1) 如果審查途徑中的任何決定是或將是可審查的決定，則本節適用於審查途徑中的每項決定。
(2) However, this section does not apply in relation to a decision by a court or a decision by the Tribunal under this Act.
(2) 然而，本條不適用於法院或法庭依本法所做的決定。
General rule
一般規則
(3) In giving notice of the decision to a person whose interests are affected by the decision, the decision ‑ maker must have regard to the matters (if any) prescribed by the rules.
(3) 在向利益受到該決定影響的人發出該決定通知時，決策者必須考慮規則規定的事項（如果有）。
(4) Subsection (3) does not apply if the decision ‑ maker has had regard to the matters in giving notice of a decision of the same kind.
(4) 若決策者在發出同類決定通知時已考慮到該事項，則第(3)款不適用。
(5) Subsection (3) applies in relation to a notice given under:
(5) 第 (3) 款適用於以下方式發出的通知：
(a) subsection 266(4); or
(a) 第 266(4) 款；或
(b) another Act or an instrument made under an Act.
(b) 另一項法案或依一項法案製定的文書。
Effect of failure to comply
不遵守規定的影響
(6) A failure to comply with this section does not affect the validity of the decision.
(6) 不遵守本條規定並不影響決定的有效性。

title: Division 3 — Decision ‑ makers to give reasons for decisions
zh: 第 3 分部 — 決策者給予決策理由
path: Part 10 — Notice and information about administrative decision
Division 3 — Decision ‑ makers to give reasons for decisions

title: 268 Requesting reasons for reviewable decision from decision ‑ maker
zh: 268 向決策者索取可審查決定的理由
path: Part 10 — Notice and information about administrative decision
Division 3 — Decision ‑ makers to give reasons for decisions
text:
(1) A person whose interests are affected by a reviewable decision may request the decision ‑ maker to give the person a statement of reasons for the decision.
(1) 其利益受到可審查決定影響的人可以要求決策者向該人提供該決定的理由說明。
Note 1: For which decisions are reviewable decisions, see section 12.
註 1：對於哪些決定是可審查的決定，請參閱第 12 節。
Note 2: For when an organisation’s or association’s interests are taken to be affected, see section 15.
註 2：當組織或協會的利益被視為受到影響時，請參閱第 15 節。
Note 3: For what must be included in a statement of reasons, see the definition of statement of reasons in section 4.
註3：理由陳述必須包含的內容，請參閱第4節理由陳述的定義。
(2) The request must be given to the decision ‑ maker in writing.
(2) 請求必須以書面形式提交給決策者。
Note: Requests may be refused if made outside specified timeframes (see subsection 269(8)).
注意：如果在規定的時間範圍之外提出請求，可能會被拒絕（請參閱第 269(8) 款）。

title: 269 Decision ‑ maker to give statement of reasons
zh: 第269章 決策者應說明理由
path: Part 10 — Notice and information about administrative decision
Division 3 — Decision ‑ makers to give reasons for decisions
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies if a person requests the decision ‑ maker for a reviewable decision to give the person a statement of reasons for the decision under section 268.
(1) 如果某人要求決策者做出可審查的決定，並根據第 268 條向該人提供該決定的理由說明，則本節適用。
General rules
一般規則
(2) Within 28 days after receiving the request, the decision ‑ maker must give the person a statement of reasons for the decision.
(2) 在收到請求後 28 天內，決策者必須向當事人提供做出該決定的理由說明。
(3) Before giving the statement of reasons to the person, the decision ‑ maker may remove from the statement any information that concerns another person.
(3) 在向當事人陳述理由之前，決策者可以從陳述中刪除任何涉及他人的資訊。
(4) Before giving the statement of reasons to the person, the decision ‑ maker may remove from the statement any information specified in a certificate under section 272 (public interest certificate in relation to statement of reasons).
(4) 在向該人提供理由陳述之前，決策者可以從該陳述中刪除第 272 條（與理由陳述有關的公共利益證明）下的證書中指定的任何資訊。
(5) If the decision ‑ maker removes information from a statement of reasons under subsection (3) or (4), the decision ‑ maker must, when giving the statement, notify the applicant of the removal and the reasons for it.
(5) 若決策者根據第(3)或(4)款從理由陳述中刪除訊息，決策者必須在作出該聲明時，通知申請人刪除的情況及其原因。
Exception—person is not affected
例外－人不受影響
(6) Despite subsection (2), the decision ‑ maker must refuse the request if the person’s interests are not affected by the decision.
(6) 儘管有第(2)款的規定，如果該人的利益沒有受到該決定的影響，決策者必須拒絕該請求。
Exception—person has already been given reasons
例外－已經給出原因的人
(7) Despite subsection (2), the decision ‑ maker may refuse the request if the person has already been given a statement of reasons for the decision.
(7) 儘管有第(2)款的規定，如果已向當事人提供了做出該決定的理由說明，則決策者可以拒絕該請求。
Note: A statement of reasons for a decision may be given in the document setting out the decision or separately.
註：決定理由的說明可以在決定的文件中給出，也可以單獨給出。
Exception—timeframes
例外——時間範圍
(8) Despite subsection (2):
(8) 儘管有第(2)款的規定：
(a) if the decision was set out in a document given to the person, the decision ‑ maker may refuse the request if the request is not made within 28 days after the document was given to the person; and
(a) 若決定載於向該人提供的文件中，且在向該人提供該文件後 28 天內未提出請求，則決策者可以拒絕該請求；和
(b) if the decision was not set out in a document given to the person, the decision ‑ maker may refuse the request if the request is not made within a reasonable time after the decision is made.
(b) 如果該決定未在向該人提供的文件中列出，且該請求未在作出決定後的合理時間內提出，則決策者可以拒絕該請求。
Exception—would disclose information that concerns another person
例外－會揭露涉及他人的訊息
(9) Despite subsections (2) and (3), the decision ‑ maker may refuse the request if:
(9) 儘管有第(2)和(3)款的規定，決策者可以在下列情況下拒絕請求：
(a) giving the statement of reasons to the person would disclose information that concerns another person; and
(a) 提供該人理由說明會揭露涉及他人的資訊；和
(b) it is not reasonably practicable for the decision ‑ maker to remove the information from the statement.
(b) 決策者從聲明中刪除該資訊是不合理可行的。
Exception—public interest certificate
例外——公共利益證明
(10) Despite subsections (2) and (4), the decision ‑ maker may refuse the request if:
(10) 儘管有第(2)和(4)款的規定，決策者可以在下列情況下拒絕請求：
(a) giving the statement of reasons would disclose information specified in a certificate under section 272 (public interest certificate in relation to statement of reasons); and
(a) 提供理由說明將揭露第 272 條（與理由說明相關的公共利益證明）下的證書中指定的資訊；和
(b) the statement would be false or misleading if the information were removed.
(b) 如果資訊被刪除，該陳述將是虛假的或具有誤導性的。
Decision ‑ maker must explain refusal to give statement of reasons
決策者必須解釋拒絕說明理由的原因
(11) If the decision ‑ maker refuses to give a statement of reasons for the decision (other than under subsection (7)), the decision ‑ maker must give the person written notice that the request is refused.
(11) 若決策者拒絕說明該決定的理由（第（7）款規定的情況除外），決策者必須向該人發出書面通知，表明其請求被拒絕。
(12) The notice must:
(12) 通知必須：
(a) explain the reason for the refusal; and
(a) 解釋拒絕的原因；和
(b) be given within 28 days after receiving the request.
(b) 在收到請求後 28 天內給予。

title: 270 Applying to Tribunal to obtain reasons for reviewable decision
zh: 第270條 向法庭申請取得可審查決定的理由
path: Part 10 — Notice and information about administrative decision
Division 3 — Decision ‑ makers to give reasons for decisions
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies if a person requests the decision ‑ maker for a reviewable decision to give the person a statement of reasons for the decision under section 268 and:
(1) 如果某人請求決策者做出可審查的決定，並根據第 268 條向該人提供該決定的理由說明，則本節適用，並且：
(a) the person is given notice that the request is refused; or
(a) 該人收到要求被拒絕的通知；或
