(b) the person is not given a statement in response to the request within 28 days after the request is received.
(b) 在收到請求後 28 天內，該人沒有收到針對請求的聲明。
Tribunal may require decision ‑ maker to give statement of reasons
仲裁庭可要求決策者陳述理由
(2) The person may apply to the Tribunal for a decision about whether the decision ‑ maker should give the person the statement of reasons.
(2) 該人可以向仲裁庭申請決定決策者是否應向該人提供理由說明。
(3) The Tribunal must decide whether the decision ‑ maker should give the person the statement of reasons.
(3) 仲裁庭必須決定決策者是否應向當事人提供理由說明。
(4) If the Tribunal decides that the decision ‑ maker should give the person the statement of reasons, the decision ‑ maker must give the person the statement of reasons within 28 days after the Tribunal notifies the decision ‑ maker of the Tribunal’s decision.
(4) 如果仲裁庭決定決策者應向該人提供理由說明，則決策者必須在仲裁庭將仲裁庭的決定通知決策者後 28 天內向該人提供理由說明。

title: 271 Applying to Tribunal to obtain adequate statement of reasons
zh: 第271章 向法庭申請獲得充分的理由陳述
path: Part 10 — Notice and information about administrative decision
Division 3 — Decision ‑ makers to give reasons for decisions
text:
When this section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies if:
(1) 本節適用於：
(a) both of the following apply:
(a) 下列兩項均適用：
(i) a person requests the decision ‑ maker for a reviewable decision to give the person a statement of reasons for the decision under section 268;
(i) 某人請求決策者做出可審查的決定，並根據第268條向該人提供該決定的理由說明；
(ii) the person is given a statement of reasons for the decision under section 269 or 270; or
(ii) 向該人提供了根據第 269 或 270 條做出決定的理由說明；或
(b) a person applies to the Tribunal for review of a reviewable decision for which the decision ‑ maker has given the person a statement of reasons.
(b) 某人向法庭申請複審可複審的決定，而決策者已向該人提供了理由說明。
Tribunal may require decision ‑ maker to give adequate information
仲裁庭可能要求決策者提供充分的訊息
(2) The person may apply to the Tribunal for a decision about whether the statement contains adequate information about any of the following matters in relation to the decision:
(2) 該人可以向仲裁庭申請決定該聲明是否包含與該決定相關的以下任何事項的充分資訊：
(a) the findings on material questions of fact;
(a) 關於重大事實問題的調查結果；
(b) the evidence or other material on which the findings are based;
(b) 調查結果所依據的證據或其他資料；
(c) the reasons for the decision.
(c) 決定的理由。
(3) The Tribunal must decide whether the statement contains adequate information about the matter.
(3) 仲裁庭必須決定該陳述是否包含有關該事項的充分資訊。
(4) If the Tribunal decides that the statement does not contain adequate information about the matter, the decision ‑ maker must give the person an additional statement containing adequate information about the matter within 28 days after the Tribunal notifies the decision ‑ maker of the Tribunal’s decision.
(4) 如果仲裁庭認為該陳述未包含有關該事項的充分信息，則決策者必須在仲裁庭將仲裁庭的決定通知該決策者後 28 天內，向該人提供包含有關該事項的充分信息的附加聲明。

title: 272 Public interest certificate in relation to statement of reasons
zh: 272 與理由陳述相關的公共利益證明
path: Part 10 — Notice and information about administrative decision
Division 3 — Decision ‑ makers to give reasons for decisions
text:
(1) The Attorney ‑ General of the Commonwealth may certify, in writing, that the disclosure of specified information in a statement of reasons for a decision would be contrary to the public interest for one or more of the following reasons:
(1) 聯邦總檢察長可以書面證明，由於以下一個或多個原因，在決定理由說明中披露特定資訊將違背公共利益：
(a) the disclosure would prejudice the security, defence or international relations of the Commonwealth;
(a) 揭露會損害英聯邦的安全、國防或國際關係；
(b) the disclosure would involve the disclosure of deliberations or decisions of the Cabinet or of a Committee of the Cabinet;
(b) 揭露涉及內閣或內閣委員會的審議或決定的揭露；
(c) any other reason that could form the basis for a claim by the Crown in right of the Commonwealth in a judicial proceeding that the information should not be disclosed.
(c) 任何其他可能構成英國政府在司法程序中主張不應披露資訊的依據的理由。
(2) If an application is made under subsection 270(2) or 271(2) in relation to the decision, the Attorney ‑ General of the Commonwealth is taken to have certified under subsection 91(1) that the disclosure of the specified information in the proceeding in relation to the application would be contrary to the public interest for the reason specified in the certificate.
(2) 如果根據第 270(2) 或 271(2) 款提出與該決定相關的申請，則認為英聯邦總檢察長已根據第 91(1) 款證明，在與該申請相關的訴訟中披露特定資訊將違反公共利益，原因在證書中指明。
(3) If an application is made for review of the decision, the Attorney ‑ General of the Commonwealth is taken to have certified under subsection 91(1) that the disclosure of the specified information in the proceeding for the review would be contrary to the public interest for the reason specified in the certificate.
(3) 如果申請對決定進行複審，則認為聯邦總檢察長已根據第 91(1) 款證明，由於證書中指明的原因，在復審程序中披露特定信息將違背公共利益。
(4) A certificate under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.
(4) 第 (1) 款規定的證書不是立法文件。

title: 273 Simplified outline of this Part
zh: 第273章 本部分的簡化概要
text:
Limitations apply to production and disclosure of some documents and information by entrusted persons. An entrusted person is any person who is, or has been, a member, the Principal Registrar, a staff member or engaged to provide services to the Tribunal.
受託人製作和揭露某些文件和資訊有限制。受託人是指任何現在或曾經是法庭成員、首席書記官、工作人員或受聘為法庭提供服務的人。
Some functions and powers of the Minister, President and Principal Registrar may be delegated.
部長、院長和首席書記官長的某些職能和權力可以被委託。
Functions or powers of the Tribunal in relation to a proceeding may be performed or exercised by the Tribunal constituted for the purposes of the proceeding under Division 4 of Part 4. In some circumstances, Tribunal functions or powers may also be performed or exercised by a member, the Principal Registrar, a registrar or a staff member authorised by the President to do so. The President may also perform or exercise Tribunal functions or powers in some circumstances.
法庭與訴訟程序相關的職能或權力可由根據第 4 部分第 4 分部為訴訟目的而組成的法庭履行或行使。在某些情況下，法庭的職能或權力也可由成員、首席書記官長、書記長或庭長授權的工作人員履行或行使。在某些情況下，庭長也可以履行或行使法庭職能或權力。
Matters dealt with in Division 5 include advisory opinions, communicating electronically, giving documents, calculating short periods of time, immunities, fees, legal or financial assistance and review of the operation of this Act. There is also a requirement that Ministers and Commonwealth entities inform the Council of action taken or proposed to be taken in relation to some systemic issues.
第 5 部分處理的事項包括諮詢意見、電子通訊、提供文件、計算短期期限、豁免權、費用、法律或財務援助以及本法實施的審查。也要求部長和英聯邦實體向理事會通報針對某些系統性問題已採取或擬採取的行動。
Rules and regulations may be made relating to this Act.
可以製定與本法有關的規則和條例。

title: 274 Protected information and documents
text:
General rule
一般規則
(1) An entrusted person must not be required to produce or disclose a protected document or protected information to a court, tribunal, authority or person (other than a parliament) that has the power to require the production of documents or the answering of questions.
(1) 不得要求受託人向有權要求出示文件或回答問題的法院、法庭、當局或個人（議會除外）出示或披露受保護的文件或受保護的資訊。
Exception
例外
(2) However, subsection (1) does not apply to the extent that the production or disclosure is necessary for the purposes of:
(2) 但是，第 (1) 款不適用於為以下目的而需要提供或揭露的情況：
(a) this Act; or
(a) 本法；或
(b) another Act or instrument made under an Act conferring power on the Tribunal.
(b) 另一項依據某項法案所製定的賦予法庭權力的法案或文書。
Meaning of protected document
受保護文件的含義
(3) A document is a protected document if the document:
(3) 若文件符合下列條件，則該文件是受保護的文件：
(a) concerns another person; and
(a) 涉及另一個人；和
(b) was obtained by the entrusted person in the performance or exercise of the entrusted person’s functions or powers under this Act, another Act or an instrument made under an Act.
(b) 是由受託人在履行或行使本法、另一法或根據某法制定的文書規定的受託人的職能或權力時獲得的。
Meaning of protected information
受保護資訊的含義
(4) Information is protected information if the information:
(4) 若資訊符合下列條件，則屬於受保護資訊：
(a) concerns another person; and
(a) 涉及另一個人；和
(b) was obtained by the entrusted person in the performance or exercise of the entrusted person’s functions or powers under this Act, another Act or an instrument made under an Act.
(b) 是由受託人在履行或行使本法、另一法或根據某法制定的文書規定的受託人的職能或權力時獲得的。

title: 275 Evidence about Tribunal proceedings
zh: 第275章 法庭程序的證據
text:
An entrusted person must not be required to give evidence to a court, tribunal, authority or person (other than a parliament) in relation to any Tribunal proceeding.
不得要求受託人就任何法庭程序向法院、法庭、當局或個人（議會除外）提供證據。

title: 276 Application of confidentiality provisions in other Acts and instruments
zh: 276 其他法案和文書中保密條款的適用
text:
(1) If:
(1) 如果：
(a) a provision of an Act (other than this Act) or an instrument made under an Act prohibits the disclosure of information by persons who:
(a) 某項法案（本法案除外）或依某項法案所製定的文書的規定禁止下列人員揭露資訊：
(i) are included in a particular class of persons; and
(i) 屬於特定類別的人員；和
(ii) obtain the information in the performance or exercise of functions or powers under the Act or instrument; and
(ii) 在履行或行使法案或文書規定的職能或權力時獲取資訊；和
(b) an entrusted person obtains any such information in the performance or exercise of the entrusted person’s functions or powers as an entrusted person;
(b) 受託人在履行或行使受託人作為受託人的職能或權力時獲得任何此類資訊；
the provision applies to the entrusted person as if the entrusted person:
該規定適用於受託人，如同受託人：
(c) were included in the particular class of persons; and
(c) 屬於特定類別的人員；和
(d) obtained the information in the performance or exercise of functions or powers under the Act or instrument.
(d) 在執行或行使法案或文書規定的職能或權力時所獲得的資訊。
(2) Paragraph (1)(a) applies whether the provision prohibits the disclosure of information absolutely, in certain circumstances only or subject to conditions.
(2) 無論該條款是絕對禁止揭露資訊、僅在某些情況下禁止揭露資訊或受條件限制，第 (1)(a) 款均適用。

title: Division 3 — Delegation
zh: 第 3 分部 — 代表團

title: 278 Delegation by Minister
text:
General rule
一般規則
(1) The Minister may, in writing, delegate the Minister’s functions or powers under this Act to:
(1) 部長可以書面將本法規定的部長職能或權力委託給：
(a) the Secretary of the Department; or
(a) 部門秘書；或
(b) the President.
(b) 主席。
Exception—functions and powers that must not be delegated
例外－不得委託的職能和權力
(2) Despite subsection (1), the Minister must not delegate a function or power the Minister has under section 295 (rules).
(2) 儘管有第 (1) 款的規定，部長不得委託其根據第 295 條（規則）所擁有的職能或權力。
Secretary of the Department must comply with directions
部門秘書必須遵守指示
(3) In performing or exercising a function or power delegated under this section, the Secretary of the Department must comply with any written directions of the Minister.
(3) 在執行或行使本條下授予的職能或權力時，部門秘書必須遵守部長的任何書面指示。
Interaction with the Law Officers Act 1964
與 1964 年《執法人員法》的互動
(4) This section does not affect or limit the operation of section 17 of the Law Officers Act 1964 in relation to a function or power under:
(4) 本條不影響或限制 1964 年《律師法》第 17 條關於下列職能或權力的實施：
(a) section 59 (Attorney ‑ General of the Commonwealth may become a party) of this Act; or
(a) 本法第 59 條（聯邦總檢察長可以成為一方）；或
(b) section 294 (legal or financial assistance) of this Act.
(b) 本法第 294 條（法律或財務援助）。
Note: Section 17 of the Law Officers Act 1964 provides for the Attorney ‑ General to delegate any of the Attorney ‑ General’s powers or functions.
註：1964 年《律師法》第 17 條規定總檢察長可以委託總檢察長的任何權力或職能。

title: 279 Delegation by President
text:
General rule
一般規則
(1) The President may, in writing, delegate the President’s functions or powers under this Act, another Act or an instrument made under an Act to:
(1) 總統可以書面形式將本法、另一項法案或根據某項法案製定的文書所規定的總統職能或權力委託給：
(a) a member; or
(a) 會員；或
(b) the Principal Registrar; or
(b) 首席書記官長；或
(c) a registrar; or
(c) 登記官；或
(d) a staff member.
(d) 一名工作人員。
Exception—functions and powers that must not be delegated
例外－不得委託的職能和權力
(2) Despite subsection (1), the President must not delegate:
(2) 儘管有第(1)款的規定，主席不得授權：
(a) a function or power the President has because the President is:
(a) 總統所擁有的功能或權力，因為總統是：
(i) a member of the Tribunal as constituted for the purposes of a proceeding; or
(i) 為訴訟目的而組成的法庭成員；或
(ii) a Council member; or
(ii) 理事會成員；或
(iii) authorised under section 281 to perform or exercise the function or power; or
(iii) 依第 281 條授權履行或行使職能或權力；或
(ab) other than in accordance with subsection (2A)—a function or power under section 200 (giving directions) or subsection 203(3) (restricting member’s duties); or
(ab) 除第 (2A) 款規定外－第 200 條（發出指示）或第 203(3) 款（限製成員職務）所規定的職能或權力；或
(b) a function or power under a provision listed in the following table.
(b) 下表所列條款所規定的職能或權力。
Functions and powers the President must not delegate
Item | Column 1 Provision | Column 2 Summary of topic of provision
1 | section 14 | decision ‑ maker
2 | Division 3 of Part 4 | practice directions
3 | subsection 109(2) | Tribunal guidance decisions
4 | Division 5 of Part 7 | referring questions of law
5 | section 196 | jurisdictional areas and lists
6 | section 197 | jurisdictional area leaders
7 | section 199 | assignment of members to jurisdictional areas
9 | section 201 | code of conduct
10 | section 202 | performance standard
12 | section 222 | President must notify Minister about grounds for termination
13 | Subdivision B of Division 4 of Part 8 | appointment and functions of Principal Registrar
總統不得委託的職能與權力
項目 |第 1 欄 規定 |第 2 欄 條款主題摘要
1 |第 14 節 |決策者
2 |第 4 部分第 3 部分 |練習方向
3 |第 109(2) 款 |法庭指導決定
4 |第 7 部分第 5 部分 |轉交法律問題
5 |第 196 條 |管轄區域及清單
6 |第 197 條 |轄區領導
7 |第 199 條 |將成員分配到管轄區域
9 |第201條|行為準則
10 | 10第202條|績效標準
12 | 12第222條|總統必須通知部長終止合約的理由
13 |第 8 部分第 4 部分 B 部分 |首席書記官長的任命和職能
Functions and powers that may only be delegated to a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President
只能授予非司法副院長的職能和權力
(2A) The President may, in writing, delegate the President’s functions or powers under section 200 (giving directions) or subsection 203(3) (restricting member’s duties) to a member who is a Non ‑ Judicial Deputy President.
(2A) 主席可以書面形式將第 200 條（發出指示）或第 203（3）款（限製成員職責）下的主席職能或權力委託給非司法副主席成員。
Delegates must comply with directions
代表必須遵守指示
(3) In performing or exercising a function or power delegated under this section, the delegate must comply with any written directions of the President.
(3) 在執行或行使本條所授予的職能或權力時，代表必須遵守主席的書面指示。

title: 280 Delegation by Principal Registrar
zh: 第280章 首席書記官長的代表團
text:
General rule
一般規則
(1) The Principal Registrar may, in writing, delegate the Principal Registrar’s functions or powers under this Act, another Act or an instrument made under an Act to a registrar or staff member.
(1) 首席書記官可以書面形式將本法、其他法案或根據某項法案製定的文書賦予首席書記官的職能或權力委託給書記官或工作人員。
Exception—functions and powers that must not be delegated
例外－不得委託的職能和權力
(2) Despite subsection (1), the Principal Registrar must not delegate a function or power that the Principal Registrar has because the Principal Registrar is authorised under section 283 to perform or exercise the function or power.
(2) 儘管有第 (1) 款的規定，首席註冊官不得將其所擁有的職能或權力委託給其他人，因為首席註冊官已根據第 283 條被授權執行或行使該職能或權力。
Delegates must comply with directions
代表必須遵守指示
(3) In performing or exercising a function or power delegated under this section, the delegate must comply with any written directions of the Principal Registrar.
(3) 在執行或行使本條所授予的職能或權力時，代表必須遵守首席書記官長的任何書面指示。

title: Division 4 — Performing and exercising functions and powers of Tribunal
zh: 第 4 分部 — 履行和行使仲裁庭的職能和權力
path: Division 4 — Performing and exercising functions and powers of Tribunal

title: Subdivision A — Performance and exercise of functions and powers
zh: A 部分－職能和權力的履行和行使
path: Division 4 — Performing and exercising functions and powers of Tribunal
Subdivision A — Performance and exercise of functions and powers

title: 281 Who may perform or exercise functions or powers
zh: 第281章 誰可以履行或行使職能或權力
path: Division 4 — Performing and exercising functions and powers of Tribunal
Subdivision A — Performance and exercise of functions and powers
text:
(1) A function or power of the Tribunal in relation to a proceeding may be performed or exercised as follows:
(1) 仲裁庭與訴訟有關的職能或權力可依下列方式履行或行使：
(a) by the Tribunal as constituted for the purposes of the proceeding;
(a) 由為訴訟目的而組成的法庭；
(b) before the start of the hearing of the proceeding—by:
(b) 在訴訟聽證會開始之前－透過：
(i) the President; or
(i) 主席；或
(ii) an authorised person;
(ii) 獲授權人；
(c) after the start of the hearing of the proceeding—by an authorised person, but only as approved by the Tribunal as constituted for the purposes of the proceeding;
(c) 訴訟程序聽證會開始後－由授權人員進行，但僅限於為程序目的而組成的法庭批准的人員；
(ca) for a function or power under subsection 114(1) to alter the text of a decision or statement of reasons for a decision—by the person who made the decision;
(ca) 第 114(1) 款規定的職能或權力可以由做出決定的人更改決定文本或決定理由說明；
(d) for a function or power under subsection 114(1) to alter the text of a decision or statement of reasons for a decision—by an authorised person, but:
(d) 第 114(1) 款規定的職能或權力可以由授權人更改決定文本或決定理由說明，但是：
(i) only as approved by the President; and
(i) 僅經總統批准；和
(ii) not if the Tribunal as constituted for the purposes of the proceeding or the person who made the decision is available;
(ii) 若為訴訟目的而組成的仲裁庭或做出決定的人在場，則不可以；
(e) for a function or power under section 102 (reinstatement of application), subsection 115(2) (taxing costs) or a provision mentioned in paragraph 286(a)—by an authorised person at any time.
(e) 第 102 條（恢復適用）、第 115(2) 款（徵稅費用）或第 286(a) 段中提到的規定所規定的職能或權力－由授權人隨時執行。
(2) To avoid doubt, the paragraphs of subsection (1) do not limit each other.
(2) 為避免疑問，第 (1) 款的各段不互相限制。
(3) For the purposes of paragraph (1)(c) and subparagraph (1)(d)(i), an approval does not need to be in writing.
(3) 就第 (1)(c) 款和第 (1)(d)(i) 項而言，批准無須採用書面形式。

title: 282 How functions or powers must be performed or exercised
zh: 282 職能或權力必須如何履行或行使
path: Division 4 — Performing and exercising functions and powers of Tribunal
Subdivision A — Performance and exercise of functions and powers
text:
Authorised person must comply with President’s directions
授權人必須遵守總統的指示
(1) In performing or exercising a function or power of the Tribunal, an authorised person must comply with any directions given by the President under this section.
(1) 在執行或行使法庭的職能或權力時，授權人員必須遵守庭長依本條所發出的任何指示。
(2) If the direction is made in writing, the direction is not a legislative instrument.
(2) 若指示以書面形式作出，則該指示並非立法文書。
Applying opinion, belief or state of mind
應用意見、信念或心態
(3) If performing or exercising a function or power of the Tribunal depends on the Tribunal’s opinion, belief or state of mind in relation to a matter, the President or an authorised person may perform or exercise the function or power on the opinion, belief or state of mind of the President or authorised person in relation to the matter.
(3) 如果法庭的職能或權力的履行或行使取決於法庭對某一事項的意見、信念或心態，則庭長或授權人可以根據庭長或授權人對此事的意見、信念或心態履行或行使職能或權力。

title: Subdivision B — Authorisations to perform and exercise functions and powers of Tribunal
zh: B 分部 — 執行和行使仲裁庭職能和權力的授權
path: Division 4 — Performing and exercising functions and powers of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Authorisations to perform and exercise functions and powers of Tribunal

title: 283 Authorisations for Principal Registrar
zh: 第283章 首席註冊官的授權
path: Division 4 — Performing and exercising functions and powers of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Authorisations to perform and exercise functions and powers of Tribunal
text:
The President may, in writing, authorise the Principal Registrar to perform or exercise a function or power of the Tribunal if:
在下列情況下，庭長可以書面授權首席書記官執行或行使法庭的職能或權力：
(a) the President could authorise:
(a) 總統可以授權：
(i) a registrar to perform or exercise the function or power of the Tribunal (see section 285); or
(i) 書記官長履行或行使仲裁庭的職能或權力（參閱第 285 條）；或
(ii) a staff member to perform or exercise the function or power of the Tribunal (see section 286); or
(ii) 履行或行使法庭職能或權力的工作人員（參閱第 286 條）；或
(b) the rules prescribe that the Principal Registrar may be authorised to perform the function or exercise the power.
(b) 規則規定首席書記官長可獲授權履行職能或行使權力。

title: 284 Authorisations for members
path: Division 4 — Performing and exercising functions and powers of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Authorisations to perform and exercise functions and powers of Tribunal
text:
(1) The President may, in writing, authorise a member to perform or exercise a function or power of the Tribunal if:
(1) 庭長可以書面授權一名成員履行或行使仲裁庭的職能或權力，如果：
(a) the President could authorise:
(a) 總統可以授權：
(i) a registrar to perform or exercise the function or power (see section 285); or
(i) 履行或行使職能或權力的註冊官（參閱第 285 條）；或
(ii) a staff member to perform or exercise the function or power (see section 286); or
(ii) 履行或行使職能或權力的工作人員（參閱第 286 條）；或
(b) the rules prescribe that a member may be authorised to perform or exercise the function or power; or
(b) 規則規定會員可被授權履行或行使職能或權力；或
(c) the function or power is a function or power under a provision listed in the following table.
(c) 此職能或權力是下表所列條款所規定的職能或權力。

title: 286 Authorisations for staff members
zh: 第286章 工作人員的授權
path: Division 4 — Performing and exercising functions and powers of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Authorisations to perform and exercise functions and powers of Tribunal
text:
The President may, in writing, authorise a staff member to perform or exercise a function or power of the Tribunal if:
在下列情況下，庭長可以書面授權工作人員履行或行使法庭的職能或權力：
(a) it is a function or power of the Tribunal under:
(a) 這是仲裁庭的功能或權力：
(i) subsection 21(2) (parties and potential parties to be notified of application); or
(i) 第 21(2) 款（申請通知的當事人和潛在當事人）；或
(ii) subsection 22(3) (parties to proceeding for review); or
(ii) 第 22(3) 款（審查程序的當事人）；或
(iii) section 72 (Tribunal must notify parties of Tribunal case event); or
(iii) 第 72 條（仲裁庭必須將仲裁庭案件事件通知當事人）；或
(iv) section 126 (parties to be notified of application); or
(iv) 第 126 條（申請通知當事人）；或
(v) section 139 (additional persons to be notified of applications for review); or
(v) 第 139 條（審查申請需通知的其他人員）；或
(b) the rules prescribe that a staff member may be authorised to perform or exercise the function or power.
(b) 《細則》規定工作人員可獲授權履行或行使職能或權力。

title: 287 Authorisations are subject to conditions
zh: 第287章 授權須遵守條件
path: Division 4 — Performing and exercising functions and powers of Tribunal
Subdivision B — Authorisations to perform and exercise functions and powers of Tribunal
text:
An authorisation by the President under this Subdivision is subject to any conditions specified in the authorisation.
總統根據本款的授權須遵守授權中規定的任何條件。

title: Division 5 — Other matters
zh: 第 5 分部 — 其他事項

title: 288 Tribunal may give advisory opinion
zh: 第288條 仲裁庭可提供諮詢意見
text:
If another Act or an instrument made under an Act so provides, the Tribunal may give an advisory opinion on a matter or question referred to it in accordance with the Act or instrument and, for the purpose of giving such an opinion, the Tribunal may hold such hearings and inform itself in such manner as it considers appropriate.
如果另一法案或根據該法案製定的文書有如此規定，仲裁庭可就根據該法案或文書提交給其的事項或問題發表諮詢意見，並且為了發表此類意見，仲裁庭可以舉行此類聽證會並以其認為適當的方式通知自己。

title: 289 Certain things required to be done in writing may be done electronically
zh: 第289章 某些需要以書面完成的事情可以透過電子方式完成

title: 290 Giving documents
text:
(1) A document or thing that is required or permitted by this Act or any other law to be produced or given to the Tribunal must be produced or given in accordance with the requirements (if any) in:
(1) 本法或任何其他法律要求或允許向仲裁庭出示或提供的文件或物品必須按照下列要求（如有）來出示或提供：
(a) the practice directions; and
(a) 實踐指導；和
(b) the rules.
(b) 規則。
(2) A document or thing that is required or permitted by this Act or any other law to be produced or given to a person for the purposes of a proceeding in the Tribunal must be produced or given in accordance with the requirements (if any) in:
(2) 本法或任何其他法律要求或允許為法庭訴訟目的而向某人出示或提供的文件或物品，必須按照下列要求（如果有）來出示或提供：
(a) the practice directions; and
(a) 實踐指導；和
(b) the rules.
(b) 規則。

title: 291 Giving documents etc. to decision ‑ maker
text:
When section applies
本節適用時
(1) This section applies if the Tribunal or any person is permitted or required under this Act to give a document or thing in relation to a decision to the decision ‑ maker for the decision.
(1) 若法院或任何人依本法被允許或要求向決策者提供與決定有關的文件或物品，則本節適用。
Giving documents etc. to Secretary
向秘書提供文件等
(2) The Tribunal or person may instead give the document or thing to the Secretary of the Department administered by the Minister who administers:
(2) 仲裁庭或個人可以將文件或物品交給部長管理的部門的秘書，該部門負責管理：
(a) the Act under which the decision was made; or
(a) 做出決定所依據的法案；或
(b) if the decision was made under an instrument—the Act under which the instrument is made.
(b) 若決定是根據文書作出的－作出該文書所依據的法案。
Giving documents etc. to holder of office
提供任職者文件等
(3) If the holder of a particular office is prescribed by the rules, an Act or an instrument made under an Act as a person to whom documents or things may be given under this Act in relation to a class of decisions that includes the decision, the Tribunal or person may instead give the document or thing to the holder of that office.
(3) 如果規則、法案或根據法案製定的文書規定特定職位的持有者可以根據本法向其提供與包括該決定在內的一類決定有關的文件或物品，則仲裁庭或個人可以將文件或物品轉交給該職位的持有者。
Note: Sections 28A and 29 of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 deal with the manner in which the documents may be given.
註：1901 年《法案解釋法》第 28A 和 29 條涉及提供文件的方式。

title: 292 Calculation of short periods of time
zh: 第292章 短時間的計算
text:
If the period of time for doing anything:
如果做某事的時間段：
(a) under this Act, any other Act or an instrument made under an Act; or
(a) 依本法、任何其他法案或依某項法案所製定的文書；或
(b) in accordance with an order of the Tribunal;
(b) 依仲裁庭的命令；
in relation to a proceeding in the Tribunal is less than 7 days, do not count any day on which the registry of the Tribunal concerned is not open to the public in working out whether the period has ended.
就仲裁庭的訴訟程序而言，期限不足 7 天的，在計算該期間是否結束時，不計算有關仲裁庭登記處不向公眾開放的任何一天。

title: 293 Protection and immunity
text:
Tribunal personnel
法庭人員
(1) Each of the following has the same protection and immunity as a Justice of the High Court:
(1) 以下各項均享有與高等法院法官相同的保護和豁免權：
(a) a member, in the performance of the member’s duties;
(a) 會員，履行會員職務；
(b) the Principal Registrar, in the performance of the Principal Registrar’s duties under Part 3 (starting a review), Part 4 (proceedings), Part 5 (guidance and appeals panel), Part 6 (proceedings in Intelligence and Security jurisdictional area) or Part 7 (appeals and references of questions of law to Federal Court);
(b) 首席書記官根據第 3 部分（開始審查）、第 4 部分（訴訟程序）、第 5 部分（指導和上訴小組）、第 6 部分（情報和安全管轄範圍內的訴訟程序）或第 7 部分（向聯邦法院上訴和提出法律問題）履行首席書記官長的職責；
(c) an authorised person, in the performance of the person’s duties as an authorised person;
(c) 被授權人，履行其作為被授權人的職責；
(d) a person conducting a dispute resolution process under this Act, in conducting the dispute resolution process.
(d) 依本法進行爭議解決程序的人員，在進行爭議解決程序時。
Representatives
代表
(2) A legal practitioner or other person appearing before the Tribunal on behalf of a party has the same protection and immunity as a barrister appearing for a party in proceedings in the High Court.
(2) 代表一方出庭的法律執業者或其他人享有與在高等法院訴訟中代表一方出庭的大律師相同的保護和豁免權。
Witnesses
證人
(3) Subject to this Act, a person appearing before the Tribunal to give evidence has the same protection, and is, in addition to the penalties provided by this Act, subject to the same liabilities, as a witness in proceedings in the High Court.
(3) 根據本法，出庭作證的人享有與高等法院訴訟中的證人相同的保護，並且除了本法規定的處罰外，還應承擔相同的責任。

title: 294 Legal or financial assistance
text:
Applicants to Tribunal
仲裁庭申請人
(1) A person who applies, or proposes to apply, to the Tribunal for review of a reviewable decision may apply to the Attorney ‑ General of the Commonwealth for assistance in respect of the proceeding in relation to the application to the Tribunal.
(1) 向法院申請或擬向法院申請複審可複核決定的人可以向英聯邦總檢察長申請與向法庭提出申請有關的訴訟程序的協助。
(2) A person who makes an application, or proposes to make an application, to refer a decision of the Tribunal to the guidance and appeals panel (a leave application ) may apply to the Attorney ‑ General of the Commonwealth for assistance in respect of the leave application and the proceeding in relation to the guidance and appeals panel application (if any) taken to be made because of the referral.
(2) 提出申請或擬提出申請將仲裁庭的決定提交給指導和上訴小組（許可申請）的人可以向聯邦總檢察長申請有關許可申請以及因提交而提出的與指導和上訴小組申請（如果有）相關的訴訟程序的協助。
Other parties to Tribunal proceedings
法庭程序的其他當事人
(3) A person who is, or proposes to become, a party to a proceeding in the Tribunal may apply to the Attorney ‑ General of the Commonwealth for assistance in respect of the proceeding.
(3) 作為或擬成為法庭訴訟當事人的人可以向英聯邦總檢察長申請有關訴訟的協助。
Court proceedings
法庭訴訟
(4) A person who:
(4) 符合下列條件的人：
(a) institutes, or proposes to institute; or
(a) 設立或提議設立；或
(b) is, or proposes to become, a party to;
(b) 是或擬成為締約方；
a proceeding in a court in respect of a matter arising under this Act may apply to the Attorney ‑ General of the Commonwealth for assistance in respect of the proceeding.
就根據本法引起的事項向法院提起的訴訟可以向聯邦總檢察長申請有關該訴訟的協助。
Exceptions—proceedings prescribed by the rules
例外情況－規則規定的程序
(5) Subsections (1) to (4) do not apply in relation to a kind of proceeding prescribed by the rules.
(5) 第 (1) 至 (4) 款不適用於規則規定的某種程序。
(6) Subsection (2) does not apply in relation to a kind of leave application prescribed by the rules.
(6) 第(2)款不適用於規則規定的某種許可申請。
Provision of assistance
提供協助
(7) If the Attorney ‑ General of the Commonwealth considers that:
(7) 如果英聯邦總檢察長認為：
(a) it would involve hardship to the person to refuse the person’s application; and
(a) 拒絕該人的申請會給該人帶來困難；和
(b) in all the circumstances, it is reasonable that the person’s application should be granted;
(b) 在所有情況下，批准該人的申請是合理的；
the Attorney ‑ General may authorise the provision by the Commonwealth to the person of legal or financial assistance determined by the Attorney ‑ General in respect of the proceeding.
總檢察長可以授權聯邦向總檢察長確定的與訴訟有關的人提供法律或經濟援助。
(8) The legal or financial assistance is subject to any conditions determined by the Attorney ‑ General of the Commonwealth.
(8) 法律或經濟援助須遵守聯邦總檢察長所確定的任何條件。
Time for making applications not affected
申請時間不受影響
(9) Nothing done under, or for the purposes of, this section extends a period for making an application to the Tribunal.
(9) 依本節或為了本節的目的所做的任何行為均不會延長向仲裁庭提出申請的期限。

title: 294A Review of operation of this Act
zh: 第294A條 本法實施審查
text:
(1) The Minister must cause to be conducted a review into the operation of this Act and any Act dealing with consequential or transitional matters arising from the enactment of this Act.
(1) 部長必須對本法以及涉及因本法頒布而產生的後果性或過渡性問題的任何法案的實施情況進行審查。
(2) Without limiting subsection (1), the review must include consideration of:
(2) 在不限制第 (1) 款的情況下，審查必須包括考慮：
(a) whether the Tribunal is achieving the objective in section 9; and
(a) 仲裁庭是否正在實現第 9 條的目標；和
(b) any other matters relating to the operation of this Act determined by the Minister.
(b) 部長確定的與本法實施有關的任何其他事項。
(3) The review must start within the 3 months before the fifth anniversary of the commencement of this Act.
(3) 審查必須在本法生效五週年之前的三個月內開始。
(4) The review must be undertaken by one or more persons (the reviewers ) who, in the Minister’s opinion, have appropriate expertise in administrative review.
(4) 審查必須由部長認為具有適當行政審查專業知識的一名或多名人員（審查員）進行。
(5) The review must include consultation with the Council, members of the public, Tribunal users and any other person or organisation the reviewers consider appropriate.
(5) 審查必須包括與理事會、公眾、仲裁庭使用者以及審查者認為適當的任何其他個人或組織的協商。
(6) The reviewers must give the Minister a written report on the review within 12 months after the fifth anniversary of the commencement of this Act.
(6) 審查人員必須在本法生效五週年後 12 個月內向部長提交書面審查報告。
(7) The Minister must cause a copy of the report to be tabled in each House of the Parliament within 15 sitting days of that House after the Minister receives the report.
(7) 部長必須在收到報告後 15 天內將報告副本提交至議會各議院。

title: 294B Minister and Commonwealth entities to inform Council of action on systemic issues
zh: 294B 部長和英聯邦實體向理事會通報有關系統性問題的行動
text:
Within 3 months after the President informs a Minister or Commonwealth entity in writing of a systemic issue related to the making of reviewable decisions that has been identified in the caseload of the Tribunal, the Minister or entity must inform the Council of the action the Minister or entity has taken or proposes to take in relation to the systemic issue.
在總統以書面形式向部長或聯邦實體通報法庭案件中發現的與可審查決定相關的系統性問題後 3 個月內，部長或實體必須向理事會通報部長或實體已採取或擬採取的與系統性問題相關的行動。
Note: For the President’s functions in relation to systemic issues, see paragraph 193(i). For the Council’s functions and reports in relation to systemic issues, see paragraph 249(1)(c) and section 264.
註：關於總統在系統性議題上的功能，請參閱第 193(i) 段。有關理事會與系統性問題有關的職能和報告，請參閱第 249(1)(c) 段和第 264 條。

title: Division 6 — Rules and regulations
zh: 第 6 分部 — 規則和條例

title: 295 Rules
text:
(1) The Minister may, by legislative instrument, make rules prescribing matters:
(1) 部長可以透過立法文書製定規定以下事項的規則：
(a) required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed by the rules; or
(a) 本法要求或允許由規則規定的；或
(b) necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
(b) 為執行或實施本法所必需或方便的規定。
(2) To avoid doubt, the rules may not do the following:
(2) 為避免疑義，規則不得做出下列行為：
(a) create an offence or civil penalty;
(a) 構成犯罪或民事處罰；
(b) provide powers of:
(b) 提供以下權力：
(i) arrest or detention; or
(i) 逮捕或拘留；或
(ii) entry, search or seizure;
(ii) 進入、搜索或扣押；
(c) impose a tax;
(c) 徵稅；
(d) set an amount to be appropriated from the Consolidated Revenue Fund under an appropriation in this Act;
(d) 依本法的撥款規定從綜合收入基金中撥款的金額；
(e) directly amend the text of this Act.
(e) 直接修改本法文本。
(3) Rules that are inconsistent with the regulations have no effect to the extent of the inconsistency, but rules are taken to be consistent with the regulations to the extent that the rules are capable of operating concurrently with the regulations.
（三）規則與本條例不一致的，在不一致的範圍內不產生效力，但在能與本條例同時實施的範圍內，視為與本條例一致。
(4) The rules may make provision in relation to a matter by applying, adopting or incorporating, with or without modification, a matter contained in the practice directions:
(4) 規則可以透過應用、採用或納入（無論是否經過修改）實踐指南中包含的事項來對某一事項做出規定：
(a) as in force or existing at a particular time; or
(a) 在特定時間有效或存在；或
(b) as in force or existing from time to time.
(b) 有效或不時存在。
(5) Subsection (4) has effect despite anything in subsection 14(2) of the Legislation Act 2003 .
(5) 儘管《2003 年立法法》第 14(2) 款有任何規定，第 (4) 款仍然有效。
(6) Before making rules affecting the practice, procedure or operations of the Tribunal, the Minister must consult the President.
(6) 在製定影響法庭實務、程序或運作的規則之前，部長必須諮詢院長。

title: 296 Tribunal may charge fees
zh: 第296條 仲裁庭可以收取費用
text:
(1) The Tribunal may, on behalf of the Commonwealth, charge fees in accordance with the rules.
(1) 仲裁庭可以代表英聯邦依規則收取費用。
(2) The rules may provide for fees to be payable in respect of the following:
(2) 規則可規定以下費用：
(a) applications to the Tribunal (including applications taken to be made to the Tribunal);
(a) 向法庭提出的申請（包括向法庭提出的申請）；
(b) applications to the President;
(b) 向總統提出的申請；
(c) taxation of costs by the Tribunal;
(c) 法庭對費用課稅；
(d) proceedings in the Tribunal;
(d) 法庭的訴訟程序；
(e) services provided by the Tribunal.
(e) 法庭提供的服務。
(3) Without limiting the scope of rules that may be made for the purposes of subsection (2), those rules may prescribe, or prescribe matters relating to, any or all of the following:
（3）在不限制為第（2）款目的而製定的規則範圍的情況下，這些規則可以規定以下任何或全部內容，或規定與以下任何或所有內容有關的事項：
(a) the circumstances in which a fee is to be paid;
(a) 須繳付費用的情況；
(b) who must pay;
(b) 誰必須付款；
(c) the time when payment is required;
(c) 要求付款的時間；
(d) remittal, refund and waiver of fees.
(d) 費用的匯出、退款和減免。
(4) Rules made for the purposes of subsection (2) may do any or all of the following:
(4) 為第 (2) 款目的而製定的規則可以執行以下任何或所有操作：
(a) prescribe fees in respect of a particular class or classes of applications, costs, proceedings or services;
(a) 規定特定類別或類別的申請、費用、程序或服務的費用；
(b) prescribe different fees in respect of different classes of applications, costs, proceedings or services;
(b) 針對不同類別的申請、費用、程序或服務規定不同的費用；
(c) prescribe the amount of, or a method for working out the amount of, a fee;
(c) 規定費用的金額或計算金額的方法；
(d) make provision in relation to the whole or a part of a fee;
(d) 就全部或部分費用作出規定；
(e) provide for the Tribunal to make orders relating to the payment of a fee in relation to a proceeding.
(e) 規定仲裁庭可以就訴訟費用的支付作出命令。
(5) A fee must not be such as to amount to taxation.
(5) 費用不得相當於稅金。
(6) A fee charged under subsection (1):
(6) 依第 (1) 款收取的費用：
(a) is a debt due to the Tribunal, on behalf of the Commonwealth; and
(a) 是代表聯邦欠法庭的債務；和
(b) is recoverable by the Tribunal, on behalf of the Commonwealth, in a court of competent jurisdiction.
(b) 法院可代表英聯邦在有管轄權的法院追回。

title: 297 Regulations
text:
(1) The Governor ‑ General may make regulations prescribing matters:
(1) 總督可訂定規定下列事項的條例：
(a) required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed by the regulations; or
(a) 本法要求或允許由法規規定的；或
(b) necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
(b) 為執行或實施本法所必需或方便的規定。
Norfolk Island enactments
諾福克島立法
(2) The regulations may provide for:
(2) 條例可以規定：
(a) applications to be made to the Tribunal for review of decisions made in the exercise of powers conferred by a Norfolk Island enactment; and
(a) 向法庭申請複審諾福克島一項法令所賦予的權力時所作出的決定；和
(b) such modifications to the operation of this Act as are necessary to provide for, and in relation to, the review of those decisions in like manner to the review of equivalent reviewable decisions under this Act; and
(b) 對本法的實施進行必要的修改，以規定對這些決定的審查，以與根據本法審查同等可審查決定的方式進行審查；和
(c) the Tribunal to give an advisory opinion on a matter or question referred to it under a Norfolk Island enactment.
(c) 法院就根據諾福克島法令提交給其的事項或問題提供諮詢意見。

title: Endnote 1—About the endnotes
text:
The endnotes provide information about this compilation and the compiled law.
尾註提供了有關本彙編和已彙編法律的資訊。
The following endnotes are included in every compilation:
每個彙編中都包含以下尾註：
Endnote 1—About the endnotes
尾註 1——關於尾註
Endnote 2—Abbreviation key
尾註 2——縮寫鍵
Endnote 3—Legislation history
尾註 3——立法歷史
Endnote 4—Amendment history
尾註 4——修改歷史
Abbreviation key—Endnote 2
縮寫鍵－尾註 2
The abbreviation key sets out abbreviations that may be used in the endnotes.
縮寫鍵列出了尾註中可能使用的縮寫。
Legislation history and amendment history—Endnotes 3 and 4
立法歷史和修訂歷史—尾註3和4
Amending laws are annotated in the legislation history and amendment history.
修改法律在立法史和修改史都有註釋。
The legislation history in endnote 3 provides information about each law that has amended (or will amend) the compiled law. The information includes commencement details for amending laws and details of any application, saving or transitional provisions that are not included in this compilation.
尾註 3 中的立法歷史提供了已修訂（或將修訂）法律彙編的每項法律的資訊。這些資訊包括修訂法律的開始細節以及本彙編中未包含的任何應用、保存或過渡條款的詳細資訊。
The amendment history in endnote 4 provides information about amendments at the provision (generally section or equivalent) level. It also includes information about any provision of the compiled law that has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law.
尾註 4 中的修訂歷史記錄提供了有關條款（通常是章節或同等級別）級別修訂的資訊。它還包括有關已根據法律條款廢除的已編纂法律的任何條款的資訊。
Editorial changes
編輯修改
The Legislation Act 2003 authorises First Parliamentary Counsel to make editorial and presentational changes to a compiled law in preparing a compilation of the law for registration. The changes must not change the effect of the law. Editorial changes take effect from the compilation registration date.
《2003 年立法法》授權第一議會律師在準備登記法律彙編時對已彙編的法律進行編輯和表述上的修改。變更不得改變法律的效力。編輯修改自編譯註冊之日起生效。
If the compilation includes editorial changes, the endnotes include a brief outline of the changes in general terms. Full details of any changes can be obtained from the Office of Parliamentary Counsel.
如果彙編包含編輯性更改，則尾註包括通用術語更改的簡要概述。任何變更的完整細節可以從議會法律顧問辦公室獲得。
Misdescribed amendments
錯誤描述的修正案
A misdescribed amendment is an amendment that does not accurately describe how an amendment is to be made. If, despite the misdescription, the amendment can be given effect as intended, then the misdescribed amendment can be incorporated through an editorial change made under section 15V of the Legislation Act 2003 .
錯誤描述的修正案是指沒有準確描述如何進行修正案的修正案。儘管有錯誤描述，如果修正案能夠如預期生效，那麼可以根據《2003 年立法法》第 15V 條進行編輯修改，將錯誤描述的修正案納入其中。
If a misdescribed amendment cannot be given effect as intended, the amendment is not incorporated and “(md not incorp)” is added to the amendment history.
如果錯誤描述的修正案無法如預期生效，則該修正案不會被納入，並且「（md not incorp）」將添加到修正案歷史中。

title: Endnote 4—Amendment history
zh: 附註 4 — 條文修訂沿革

title: 1 Name
text:
This instrument is the Administrative Review Tribunal Rules 2024 .
該文書就是《2024 年行政復審法庭規則》。

title: 3 Authority
text:
This instrument is made under the Administrative Review Tribunal Act 2024 .
該文書是根據《2024 年行政復審法庭法》制定的。

title: 4 Definitions
text:
Note: A number of expressions used in this instrument are defined in the Act, including the following:
註：該法案中定義了本文書中使用的許多術語，包括以下內容：
(a) decision ‑ maker;
(a) 決策者；
(b) election notice;
(b) 選舉通知；
(c) Principal Registrar;
(c) 首席書記長；
(d) second review;
(d) 第二次審查；
(e) statement of reasons;
(e) 理由說明；
(f) Tribunal case event.
(f) 法庭案件事件。
In this instrument:
在本儀器中：
Act means the Administrative Review Tribunal Act 2024 .
該法案是指《2024 年行政復審法庭法案》。
original decision ‑ maker , in relation to an application under section 123 of the Act to the President to refer a decision of the Tribunal to the guidance and appeals panel, means the decision ‑ maker of the reviewable decision that the Tribunal’s decision relates to.
原始決策者，就根據該法第 123 條向總統提出的將法庭決定提交指導和上訴小組的申請而言，是指與法庭決定相關的可審查決定的決策者。
small business entity has the same meaning as in the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 .
小型企業實體與 1997 年所得稅評估法中的意義相同。
small business taxation decision means a decision made:
小企業稅務決策是指所做的決策：
(a) under a taxation law (within the meaning of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 ); and
(a) 根據稅法（1997 年所得稅評估法的含義）；和
(b) in relation to a small business entity.
(b) 與小型企業實體有關。

title: Part 2 — Applying for review of decision
zh: 第 2 部 — 申請覆核決定
path: Part 2 — Applying for review of decision

title: 5 When to apply—notice of decision given in writing
zh: 5 何時申請－以書面發出決定通知
path: Part 2 — Applying for review of decision
text:
Purpose of this section
本節的目的
(1) This section is made for the purposes of subsection 18(1) of the Act.
(1) 本條是為了該法案第 18(1) 款的目的而製定的。
When this section applies
本節適用時
(2) This section applies in relation to an application for review of a decision (the decision under review ), other than a decision taken to be made by section 16 of the Act or a provision of another Act or legislative instrument, if the applicant is given notice of the decision in writing.
(2) 本條適用於對某項決定（正在審查的決定）進行複審的申請，但該法第 16 條或其他法案或立法文書的規定作出的決定除外，如果申請人收到了該決定的書面通知。
General rule—period ends 28 days after notice is given
一般規則－期限在發出通知後 28 天結束
(3) The period starts on the day the decision under review is made and ends on the day that is 28 days after the day the applicant is given the notice.
（三）期限自複議決定作出之日起至申請人收到通知之日起滿二十八日止。
Exception—if statement of reasons is given
例外情況－如果給出原因說明
(4) Despite subsection (3), if the applicant is given a statement of reasons for the decision under review, the period starts on the day the decision under review is made and ends on the day that is 28 days after the day the applicant is given the statement of reasons.
(4) 儘管有第(3)款的規定，如果向申請人提供了審查決定的理由陳述，則期限從做出審查決定之日開始，到申請人收到理由陳述之日後28天結束。
Exception—if statement of reasons is requested but not provided
例外情況－如果要求說明原因但未提供
(5) Despite subsection (3), if:
(5) 儘管有第(3)款的規定，如果：
(a) the applicant is not given a statement of reasons for the decision under review; and
(a) 未提供申請人審查決定的理由說明；和
(b) the applicant requests a statement of reasons for the decision under review under section 268 of the Act; and
(b) 申請人請求根據該法第 268 條說明接受審查的決定的理由；和
(c) the applicant is given written notice that the request is refused;
(c) 向申請人發出請求被拒絕的書面通知；
the period starts on the day the decision under review is made and ends on the day that is 28 days after the applicant is given written notice that the request is refused.
該期限自做出審查決定之日起至申請人收到請求被拒絕的書面通知後 28 天之日結束。
Exception—if applicant applies to Tribunal to obtain adequate statement of reasons
例外情況－如果申請人向仲裁庭申請獲得充分的理由陳述
(6) Despite subsections (3), (4) and (5), if:
(6) 儘管有第 (3)、(4) 和 (5) 款的規定，如果：
(a) the applicant requests a statement of reasons for the decision under review under section 268 of the Act; and
(a) 申請人請求根據該法第 268 條說明接受審查的決定的理由；和
(b) the applicant is given a statement of reasons for the decision under review under section 269 or 270 of the Act; and
(b) 向申請人提供根據該法第 269 或 270 條進行審查的決定的理由說明；和
(c) the applicant applies to the Tribunal under section 271 of the Act for a decision about whether the statement of reasons contains adequate information about a matter; and
(c) 申請人根據該法第 271 條向仲裁庭申請就理由陳述是否包含有關某事項的充分資訊作出決定；和
(d) the Tribunal decides that the statement of reasons does not contain adequate information about the matter;
(d) 仲裁庭裁定理由陳述未包含有關該事項的充分資訊；
the period starts on the day the decision under review is made and ends on the day that is 28 days after the day the applicant is given an additional statement containing adequate information about the matter.
該期限從做出審查決定之日開始，到申請人收到包含有關事項的充分資訊的補充聲明之日起 28 天後結束。
Note: A person may apply to the Tribunal to extend the period during which the person may apply for review of a decision (see section 19 of the Act).
注意：某人可以向法院申請延長其申請複審決定的期限（參見該法第 19 條）。

title: 6 When to apply—decisions taken to be made because timeframe expires
zh: 6 何時申請－因期限到期而做出的決定
path: Part 2 — Applying for review of decision
text:
Purpose of this section
本節的目的
(1) This section is made for the purposes of subsection 18(1) of the Act.
(1) 本條是為了該法案第 18(1) 款的目的而製定的。
When this section applies
本節適用時
(2) This section applies in relation to an application for review of a decision (the decision under review ) that is taken to be made by section 16 of the Act or a provision of another Act or legislative instrument.
(2) 本節適用於根據本法第 16 條或其他法案或立法文書的規定所做的決定（正在審查的決定）進行複審的申請。
General rule—period ends 28 days after decision is taken to be made
一般規則－期限在做出決定後 28 天結束
(3) The period starts on the day the decision under review is taken to be made and ends on the day that is 28 days after the day the decision under review is taken to be made.
（三）期限自複議決定作出之日起，至複議決定作出之日後28日止。
Exception—if decision is subsequently made
例外情況－如果隨後做出決定
(4) Despite subsection (3), if:
(4) 儘管有第(3)款的規定，如果：
(a) the decision under review is a decision not to do a thing; and
(a) 正在審查的決定是不做某事的決定；和
(b) after the decision under review is taken to be made, the decision ‑ maker makes or purports to make a decision (the subsequent decision ) to do or not do the thing; and
(b) 在接受審查的決定被認為作出後，決策者做出或意圖做出做或不做某事的決定（後續決定）；和
(c) the applicant is given notice of the subsequent decision in writing;
(c) 向申請人發出後續決定的書面通知；
the period starts on the day the decision under review is taken to be made and ends at the end of the period that applies or would apply in relation to the subsequent decision under section 5.
該期限從做出正在審查的決定之日開始，到適用或將適用於第 5 條下的後續決定的期限結束時為止。
Note: A person may apply to the Tribunal to extend the period during which the person may apply for review of a decision (see section 19 of the Act).
注意：某人可以向法院申請延長其申請複審決定的期限（參見該法第 19 條）。

title: Part 3 — Proceedings
zh: 第 3 部 — 審理程序

title: Division 1 — Elections not to participate in kind of proceeding or Tribunal case event
zh: 第 1 分部 — 選擇不參加某種訴訟或法庭案件活動
path: Division 1 — Elections not to participate in kind of proceeding or Tribunal case event

title: 7 Election notices
path: Division 1 — Elections not to participate in kind of proceeding or Tribunal case event
text:
Requirements for giving election notices
發出選舉通知的要求
(1) For the purposes of paragraph 64(2)(a) of the Act, this section sets out requirements for giving election notices.
(1) 就該法第 64(2)(a) 條而言，本節規定了發出選舉通知的要求。
Note: If a purported election notice does not comply with the requirements set out in this section, it is not a valid election notice.
註：如果聲稱的選舉通知不符合本節規定的要求，則該通知不是有效的選舉通知。
Election notices in relation to a kind of proceeding
與某種程序有關的選擇通知
(2) An election notice in relation to a kind of proceeding in the Tribunal must:
(2) 與仲裁庭某類訴訟相關的選舉通知必須：
(a) identify the kind of proceeding; and
(a) 確定程序的類型；和
(b) if the election notice relates to a proceeding for review of a reviewable decision—identify:
(b) 如果選舉通知涉及可審查決定的審查程序－請確定：
(i) the legislative provision under which the decision is made; and
(i) 作出決定所依據的立法規定；和
(ii) who the decision ‑ maker for the decision is.
(ii) 該決定的決策者是誰。
Note: For example, a kind of proceeding may be identified by reference to the period (if any) within which the proceeding starts.
注意：例如，可以透過參考程序開始的時間段（如果有）來識別程序的類型。
Election notices in relation to a kind of Tribunal case event
與審裁處案件事件有關的選擇通知
(3) An election notice in relation to a kind of Tribunal case event in relation to a kind of proceeding in the Tribunal must:
(3) 與仲裁庭某類訴訟相關的仲裁庭案件事件的選舉通知必須：
(a) identify the kind of Tribunal case event and the kind of proceeding; and
(a) 確定仲裁庭案件事件的類型和程序的類型；和
(b) if the election notice relates to a proceeding for review of a reviewable decision—identify:
(b) 如果選舉通知涉及可審查決定的審查程序－請確定：
(i) the legislative provision under which the decision is made; and
(i) 作出決定所依據的立法規定；和
(ii) who the decision ‑ maker for the decision is.
(ii) 該決定的決策者是誰。
Note: Election notices cannot be given in relation to certain Tribunal case events (see paragraph 60(1)(b) of the Act).
注意：不能就某些法庭案件事件發出選舉通知（參見該法第 60(1)(b) 段）。
Election notices in relation to proceedings for review of a reviewable decision
與可複審決定複審程序有關的選舉通知
(4) An election notice that gives the Tribunal notice that a person does not wish to participate in a proceeding for review of a reviewable decision (the review proceeding ) must also give the Tribunal notice that the person does not wish to participate in any proceeding related to an incidental application to the Tribunal made in the course of, or in connection with, the review proceeding.
(4) 向仲裁庭通知某人不希望參加可複核決定的複核程序（複核程序）的選舉通知也必須向仲裁庭通知該人不希望參加與在復核程序過程中或與復核程序有關的附帶向仲裁庭提出的申請有關的任何程序。
(5) An election notice that gives the Tribunal notice that a person does not wish to participate in a kind of Tribunal case event in relation to a proceeding for review of a reviewable decision (the review proceeding ) must also give the Tribunal notice that the person does not wish to participate in that kind of Tribunal case event in relation to any proceeding related to an incidental application to the Tribunal made in the course of, or in connection with, the review proceeding.
(5) 如果選舉通知通知仲裁庭某人不希望參與與可複核決定複核程序（複核程序）有關的某類仲裁庭案件事件，則該選擇通知還必須向仲裁庭通知該人不希望參加與在復核程序過程中或與復核程序相關的附帶向仲裁庭提出的申請有關的任何程序的該類仲裁庭案件事件。

title: 8 Conditions to be satisfied for a person to be a non ‑ participating party
zh: 8 成為非參與方應滿足的條件
path: Division 1 — Elections not to participate in kind of proceeding or Tribunal case event
text:
Non ‑ participating party to a proceeding
不參與訴訟的一方
(1) For the purposes of paragraph 61(1)(e) of the Act, it is a condition that the election notice is given at least 14 days before the start of the proceeding.
(1) 就該法第 61(1)(e) 條而言，一個條件是選舉通知至少在程序開始前 14 天發出。
Non ‑ participating party to a Tribunal case event
未參與法庭案件活動的一方
(2) For the purposes of paragraph 61(1A)(e) of the Act, it is a condition that the election notice is given at least 14 days before the start of the proceeding.
(2) 就該法第 61(1A)(e) 條而言，一個條件是選舉通知至少在程序開始前 14 天發出。

title: 9 Additional circumstances in which a person is a non ‑ participating party
zh: 9 某人為非參與方的其他情況
path: Division 1 — Elections not to participate in kind of proceeding or Tribunal case event
text:
(1) For the purposes of subsection 61(3) of the Act, a person is a non ‑ participating party to a proceeding if, but for the person’s withdrawal of an election notice:
(1) 就該法第 61(3) 款而言，如果一個人沒有撤回選舉通知，則該人屬於訴訟的非參與者：
(a) during the proceeding; or
(a) 訴訟期間；或
(b) within 14 days before the start of the proceeding;
(b) 訴訟開始前 14 天內；
the person would be a non ‑ participating party to the proceeding under subsection 61(1) of the Act.
該人將是該法第 61(1) 款規定的訴訟的非參與者。
(2) For the purposes of subsection 61(3) of the Act, a person is a non ‑ participating party to a Tribunal case event in relation to a proceeding if, but for the person’s withdrawal of an election notice:
(2) 就該法第 61(3) 款而言，如果某人撤回了選舉通知，則該人是與訴訟相關的法庭案件事件的非參與方：
(a) during the proceeding; or
(a) 訴訟期間；或
(b) within 14 days before the start of the proceeding;
(b) 訴訟開始前 14 天內；
the person would be a non ‑ participating party to the Tribunal case event in relation to the proceeding under subsection 61(1A) of the Act.
該人將是與該法第 61(1A) 款規定的訴訟相關的法庭案件事件的非參與者。

title: 10 Publication
path: Division 1 — Elections not to participate in kind of proceeding or Tribunal case event
text:
For the purposes of paragraph 64(2)(b) of the Act, if the Tribunal is given an election notice, the Principal Registrar must publish a copy of the election notice.
就該法第 64(2)(b) 段而言，如果向仲裁庭發出選舉通知，首席書記官長必須公佈選舉通知的副本。

title: 11 Participation notices
path: Division 1 — Elections not to participate in kind of proceeding or Tribunal case event
text:
Participation notices must give reasons
參加通知須說明理由
(1) For the purposes of paragraph 64(2)(a) of the Act, a participation notice in relation to a proceeding or Tribunal case event in relation to a proceeding must identify the reason why the non ‑ participating party to the proceeding or Tribunal case event wishes to participate in the proceeding or Tribunal case event.
(1) 就該法第 64(2)(a) 段而言，與訴訟或仲裁庭案件事件有關的參與通知必須說明訴訟或仲裁庭案件事件的非參與方希望參與訴訟或仲裁庭案件事件的原因。
Other parties to be notified
需通知的其他各方
(2) For the purposes of paragraph 64(1)(b) of the Act, if a non ‑ participating party to a proceeding or Tribunal case event in relation to a proceeding gives the Tribunal a participation notice, the party must give a copy of the notice to each of the other parties to the proceeding.
(2) 就該法第 64(1)(b) 段而言，如果訴訟或與訴訟相關的仲裁庭案件事件的非參與方向仲裁庭發出參與通知，則該方必須向訴訟的其他各方提供該通知的副本。

title: 12 Participation of non ‑ participating parties
path: Division 1 — Elections not to participate in kind of proceeding or Tribunal case event
text:
Matters for Tribunal consideration
供仲裁庭審議的事項
(1) For the purposes of paragraph 64(1)(a) of the Act, in deciding whether or not a party is to participate in a proceeding or Tribunal case event in relation to a proceeding under section 62 of the Act, the Tribunal may have regard to the following:
(1) 就該法第 64(1)(a) 段而言，在決定當事人是否參與與該法第 62 條規定的訴訟相關的訴訟或仲裁庭案件事件時，仲裁庭可考慮以下因素：
(a) the effect that the participation of the party would have on the ability of the Tribunal to achieve the objective in section 9 of the Act;
(a) 當事人的參與將對仲裁庭實現該法第 9 條的目標的能力產生影響；
(b) the timeliness of the participation notice given to the Tribunal by the party;
(b) 當事人向仲裁庭發出參與通知的及時性；
(c) the circumstances of the parties to the proceeding;
(c) 訴訟各方的情況；
(d) whether the proceeding:
(d) 程序是否：
(i) is, or is likely to be, complex; or
(i) 是或可能是複雜的；或
(ii) involves, or is likely to involve, a significant conclusion of law; or
(ii) 涉及或可能涉及重大法律結論；或
(iii) has, or is likely to have, significant implications for Commonwealth policy or administration; or
(iii) 對聯邦政策或管理有或可能有重大影響；或
(iv) could be resolved using dispute resolution processes;
(iv) 可透過爭議解決程序來解決；
(e) any other matters that the Tribunal considers relevant.
(e) 仲裁庭認為相關的任何其他事項。
(2) For the purposes of paragraph 64(1)(a) of the Act, before ordering a party to do a thing in relation to a proceeding under subsection 63(2) of the Act, the Tribunal may have regard to the following:
(2) 就該法第 64(1)(a) 段而言，在命令一方當事人根據該法第 63(2) 款採取與訴訟相關的行動之前，仲裁庭可以考慮以下事項：
(a) the effect that it would have on the ability of the Tribunal to achieve the objective in section 9 of the Act;
(a) 它將對法庭實現該法第 9 條目標的能力產生影響；
(b) the circumstances of the parties to the proceeding;
(b) 訴訟各方的情況；
(c) whether the proceeding:
(c) 程序是否：
(i) is, or is likely to be, complex; or
(i) 是或可能是複雜的；或
(ii) involves, or is likely to involve, a significant conclusion of law; or
(ii) 涉及或可能涉及重大法律結論；或
(iii) has, or is likely to have, significant implications for Commonwealth policy or administration; or
(iii) 對聯邦政策或管理有或可能有重大影響；或
(iv) could be resolved using dispute resolution processes;
(iv) 可透過爭議解決程序來解決；
(d) any other matters that the Tribunal considers relevant.
(d) 仲裁庭認為相關的任何其他事項。
Tribunal must notify parties of participation
仲裁庭必須通知當事人參與
(3) For the purposes of paragraph 64(1)(a) of the Act, if the Tribunal decides under section 62 of the Act whether or not a party is to participate in a proceeding or Tribunal case event in relation to a proceeding, or orders a party to do a thing in relation to a proceeding under subsection 63(2) of the Act, the Tribunal must give written notice of the decision or order to the parties to the proceeding.
(3) 就該法第 64(1)(a) 款而言，如果仲裁庭根據該法第 62 條決定一方當事人是否參加訴訟或與訴訟有關的仲裁庭案件事件，或根據該法第 63(2) 款命令一方當事人做與訴訟有關的某件事，仲裁庭必須向訴訟各方發出有關該決定或命令的書面通知。
(4) A failure to comply with subsection (3) does not affect the validity of the decision or order.
(4) 不遵守第 (3) 款並不影響決定或命令的有效性。

title: Division 2 — Witness fees and expenses
zh: 第 2 分部 — 證人費用和開支

title: 13 Entitlement to fees and allowances
zh: 13 享受費用和津貼的權利
text:
Fees for compliance with summons
遵守傳票的費用
(1) For the purposes of subsection 77(1) of the Act, the following fees are prescribed for compliance with a summons under subsection 74(1) of the Act for a person to give evidence:
(1) 就該法第 77(1) 款而言，為遵守該法第 74(1) 款規定的傳票提供證據，規定了以下費用：
(a) if the person has an occupation and is remunerated in that occupation by wages, salary or fees—the amount of wages, salary or fees that are not paid to the person because the person appears before the Tribunal;
(a) 如果該人有職業，並且在該職業中以工資、薪水或費用作為報酬－由於該人出庭而未支付給該人的工資、薪水或費用金額；
(b) in any other case—a reasonable amount, up to a maximum of $75 for each day on which the person appears before the Tribunal.
(b) 在任何其他情況下－合理的金額，該人出庭的每天最多可達 75 美元。
Allowances for compliance with summons
遵守傳票的津貼
(2) For the purposes of subsection 77(1) of the Act, the following allowances are prescribed:
(2) 就該法第 77(1) 條而言，規定了下列津貼：
(a) for compliance with a summons under subsection 74(1) of the Act for a person to give evidence:
(a) 為了遵守該法第 74(1) 款規定的傳票，要求某人提供證據：
(i) a reasonable amount for travel between the person’s usual place of employment or residence and the place where the person appears before the Tribunal; and
(i) 該人通常的工作或居住地與該人出庭地點之間的合理旅行費用；和
(ii) if the person is required to be absent overnight from the person’s usual place of residence—a reasonable amount for meals and accommodation;
(ii) 若該人被要求離開慣常居住地過夜－合理的膳食及住宿費用；
(b) for compliance with a summons under subsection 74(1) of the Act for a person to produce a document or thing to the Tribunal—the person’s reasonable expenses in producing the document or thing.
(b) 為了遵守該法第 74(1) 款規定的傳票，要求某人向法庭出示文件或物品－該人出示該文件或物品的合理費用。

title: 14 Fees and allowances
text:
Circumstances in which a person is not to be paid
不向某人支付報酬的情況
(1) Despite section 13 of this instrument, for the purposes of paragraph 77(2)(b) of the Act:
(1) 儘管有本文書第 13 條，但就該法第 77(2)(b) 段而言：
(a) fees and allowances in relation to a proceeding are not to be paid to a person who is a party to the proceeding, unless the Tribunal orders otherwise; and
(a) 與訴訟相關的費用和津貼不得支付給訴訟當事人，除非法庭另有命令；和
(b) an allowance mentioned in paragraph 13(2)(a) of this instrument is not to be paid to a person if the person is given the equivalent in kind (such as access to pre ‑ paid travel, meals or accommodation) by the person who would otherwise have been required to pay the allowance under subsection (2) or (3) of this section.
(b) 若本應依本條第(2)或(3)款支付津貼的人給予該人同等的實物（例如預付旅費、膳食或住宿），則不應向該人支付本文書第13(2)(a)款所提及的津貼。
Who must pay
誰必須支付
(2) For the purposes of paragraph 77(2)(c) of the Act, a fee mentioned in subsection 13(1) or an allowance mentioned in subsection 13(2) of this instrument must be paid by:
(2) 就該法第 77(2)(c) 段而言，本文件第 13(1) 款所提及的費用或本文第 13(2) 款所提及的津貼必須由下列人員支付：
(a) if the person summoned under subsection 74(1) of the Act was summoned at the request of a party to a proceeding—the party; or
(a) 若依該法第 74(1) 款被傳喚的人是應訴訟一方的請求傳喚的－該方；或
(b) in any other case—the Commonwealth.
(b) 在任何其他情況下－英聯邦。
(3) Despite paragraph (2)(a), the Tribunal may order that a fee or allowance mentioned subsection (2) be paid, in whole or in part, by the Commonwealth.
(3) 儘管有第 (2)(a) 款的規定，仲裁庭仍可命令聯邦支付全部或部分第 (2) 款所述的費用或津貼。
When fees and allowances must be paid
何時必須支付費用和津貼
(4) For the purposes of paragraph 77(2)(d) of the Act, a person who is summoned under subsection 74(1) of the Act must be paid:
(4) 就該法第 77(2)(d) 條而言，根據該法第 74(1) 款被傳喚的人必須支付：
(a) the fees for compliance with the summons as soon as practicable after the person has complied with the summons; and
(a) 在該人遵從傳票後，在切實可行的情況下盡快支付遵從傳票的費用；和
(b) the allowances for compliance with the summons:
(b) 遵守傳票的津貼：
(i) when the person is given the summons; or
(i) 當該人收到傳票時；或
(ii) within a reasonable time before the day the person is required to comply with the summons.
(ii) 在該人被要求遵守傳票的日期之前的合理時間內。
Tribunal may make orders relating to the payment of a fee or allowance
仲裁庭可作出與支付費用或津貼有關的命令
(5) For the purposes of paragraph 77(3)(c) of the Act, on application by a person summoned under subsection 74(1) of the Act at the request of a party to a proceeding, the Tribunal may, by order, determine the amount of fees or allowances to be paid under this Division if the person and the party cannot agree on the amount.
(5) 就該法第 77(3)(c) 款而言，根據該法第 74(1) 款應訴訟一方請求而被傳喚的人提出申請，如果該人和當事人無法就金額達成一致，仲裁庭可以透過命令確定根據本節支付的費用或津貼的數額。

title: Division 3 — Guidance and appeals panel
zh: 第 3 分部 — 指導與上訴小組

title: 15 Applications for referral to the guidance and appeals panel cannot be made for certain decisions
zh: 15 某些決定不能申請轉介給指導和上訴小組

title: Part 4 — Notice and information about administrative decisions
zh: 第 4 部 — 行政決定的通知及資料

title: 16 Decision ‑ maker must have regard to matters when giving notice of decisions in certain review pathways
zh: 16 決策者在某些審查途徑中發出決定通知時必須考慮事項
path: Part 4 — Notice and information about administrative decisions
text:
(1) For the purposes of subsection 267(3) of the Act, the decision ‑ maker must have regard to the matters set out in subsections (2) to (6) of this section.
(1) 就該法第 267(3) 款而言，決策者必須考慮本條第 (2) 至 (6) 款所規定的事項。
(2) A notice of a decision should be in plain language and be as clear and simple as possible.
（二）決定通知應使用簡單易懂的語言，並盡可能清晰、簡單。
(3) A notice of a decision should be given in an accessible manner.
(3) 決定通知應以易於理解的方式發出。
(4) A notice of a decision should clearly explain:
（四）決定通知應明確說明：
(a) the legislative provision under which the decision was made; and
(a) 作出決定所依據的立法規定；和
(b) who the decision ‑ maker for the decision is; and
(b) 該決定的決策者是誰；和
(c) how a person can obtain further information about the decision, including:
(c) 一個人如何獲得有關該決定的進一步信息，包括：
(i) where a person can seek further information about the decision; and
(i) 某人可以尋求有關該決定的進一步資訊；和
(ii) if a statement of reasons for the decision has not already been given—how a person can request a statement of reasons for the decision; and
(ii) 如果尚未給出該決定的理由說明－一個人如何請求該決定的理由說明；和
(iii) if a statement of reasons for the decision has been given—steps a person can take if the person is not satisfied with the statement of reasons; and
(iii) 如果已經給出了該決定的理由陳述－如果該人對理由陳述不滿意，可以採取的步驟；和
(d) if a person can seek access to documents or information about the decision under the Freedom of Information Act 1982 or any other Act—how that access can be sought; and
(d) 如果某人可以根據《1982 年資訊自由法》或任何其他法案尋求獲取有關該決定的文件或資訊－如何尋求這種獲取；和
(e) the following matters in relation to the right (if any) to have the decision reviewed:
(e) 與覆核決定的權利（如有）相關的下列事項：
(i) the kind of review available;
(i) 可用的審查類型；
(ii) how a person can apply for the review;
(ii) 一個人如何申請審查；
(iii) if an application for the review must be made within a period—the start and end of the period;
(iii) 若覆核申請必須在一段時間內提出－該段的開始和結束；
(iv) if a fee is payable for the review—the amount of the fee, when the fee is payable and whether there are any fee waivers, concessions or refunds available;
(iv) 如果審查需要支付費用－費用金額、支付時間以及是否有任何費用減免、優惠或退款；
(v) how the person or body that may conduct the review can be contacted;
(v) 如何聯絡可以進行審查的個人或機構；
(vi) where a person can seek further information about how the person can have the decision reviewed; and
(vi) 某人可以尋求有關如何對決定進行審查的進一步資訊；和
(f) how a person can make a complaint in relation to the decision; and
(f) 一個人如何就該決定提出投訴；和
(g) any legal, financial or other forms of advice and assistance that may be available to a person whose interests are affected by the decision; and
(g) 利益受到該決定影響的人可以獲得的任何法律、財務或其他形式的建議和援助；和
(h) any other matter that the decision ‑ maker considers appropriate in the circumstances.
(h) 決策者認為適合情況的任何其他事項。
(5) It is possible for a notice of a decision to explain a matter mentioned in subsection (4) by providing an electronic link or website address that can be used to access an explanation.
(5) 決定通知可以透過提供可用於取得解釋的電子連結或網站位址來解釋第 (4) 款所提及的事項。
Note: Whether it is appropriate to explain a matter by providing an electronic link or website address that can be used to access the explanation will depend on the circumstances.
注意：透過提供可用於存取解釋的電子連結或網站地址來解釋問題是否合適，將取決於具體情況。
(6) A decision ‑ maker should publish, on the internet or in any other way the decision ‑ maker considers appropriate, a notice of a decision if:
(6) 在下列情況下，決策者應在網路上或以決策者認為適當的任何其他方式發布決定通知：
(a) one or more of the persons whose interests are affected by the decision are not readily identifiable; or
(a) 利益受到該決定影響的一個或多個人不易識別；或
(b) there is a large number of persons whose interests are affected by the decision; or
(b) 該決定影響了眾多利益的人；或
(c) the cost of giving a notice of the decision to each person whose interests are affected by the decision would be substantial.
(c) 向其利益受到該決定影響的每個人發出該決定通知的費用將是巨大的。
Note: In addition to publishing a notice of a decision, a decision ‑ maker may also give a notice of the decision to a person whose interests are affected by the decision.
注意：除了發布決定通知外，決策者還可以向利益受到該決定影響的人發出決定通知。

(1A) For the purposes of paragraph 286(b) of the Act, a staff member may be authorised to perform or exercise a function or power of the Tribunal under any of the following provisions of the Act:
(1A) 就該法第 286(b) 款而言，工作人員可被授權根據該法的以下任何規定執行或行使法庭的職能或權力：
(a) subsection 19(5) (notice to persons affected by application to extend period to apply for review);
(a) 第 19(5) 款（向受申請影響的人發出延長申請審查期限的通知）；
(b) subsection 21(3) (notice to persons who may be affected by decision under review);

(c) subsection 68(2) or (3) (appointment of interpreter);
(c) 第 68(2) 或 (3) 款（指定口譯員）；
(d) subsection 74(1) (summoning of persons to give evidence etc.);
(d) 第 74(1) 款（傳喚人員作證等）；
(e) subsection 113(1) (publishing Tribunal decisions and reasons);
(e) 第 113(1) 款（公佈仲裁庭的裁決和理由）；

title: 20 Purpose of this Division
path: Subdivision A — Purpose and scope of operation of this Division
text:
For the purposes of paragraphs 296(2)(a) and (b) of the Act, this Division provides for fees to be payable in respect of the following:
就該法第 296(2)(a) 和 (b) 段而言，本節規定了下列各項應繳納的費用：
(a) applications to the Tribunal (including applications taken to be made to the Tribunal, and applications referred to the guidance and appeals panel under section 122 of the Act);
(a) 向法庭提出的申請（包括向法庭提出的申請，以及根據該法第 122 條提交給指導和上訴小組的申請）；
(b) applications to the President under section 123 of the Act.
(b) 根據該法第 123 條向總統提出的申請。

title: 21 Scope of operation of this Division
path: Subdivision A — Purpose and scope of operation of this Division
text:
This Division does not apply in relation to a review of the following, within the meaning of the Migration Act 1958 :
本節不適用於 1958 年《移民法》含義內的以下審查：
(a) a reviewable migration decision;
(a) 可審查的移民決定；
(b) a reviewable protection decision.
(b) 可審查的保護決定。

title: 22 Fees for applications to the Tribunal

path: Subdivision B — Applications to the Tribunal
text:
Standard application fee
標準申請費
(1) The fee of $1,121 is prescribed in respect of:
(1) 規定費用為 1,121 美元：
(a) an application to the Tribunal for review of a decision (other than an application referred to in subsection (2) or (3), or an application referred to in section 30 in respect of which no fee is prescribed); or
(a) 向仲裁庭提出複核決定的申請（第（2）或（3）款中提到的申請或第 30 條中提到的不收取任何費用的申請除外）；或
(b) an application to the Tribunal under subsection 270(2) of the Act; or
(b) 依該法第 270(2) 款向法庭提出申請；或
(c) an application to the Tribunal under subsection 62(2) of the Freedom of Information Act 1982 .
(c) 依據《1982 年資訊自由法》第 62(2) 款向法院提出申請。
Note: The fee is indexed under section 33.
注意：該費用已在第 33 條下索引。
Lower application fee for small business taxation decisions
降低小型企業稅務決策的申請費
(2) The fee of $602 is prescribed in respect of an application for review of a small business taxation decision (other than an application referred to in subsection (3)).
(2) 小型企業稅務決定覆核申請（第 (3) 款提及的申請除外）規定費用為 602 美元。
Note: The fee is indexed under section 33.
注意：該費用已在第 33 條下索引。
Lower application fee for certain other taxation decisions
某些其他稅務決定的申請費較低
(3) The fee of $111 is prescribed in respect of an application for review of a decision:
(3) 決定複審申請的費用為 111 美元：
(a) that is a reviewable objection decision under Part IVC of the Taxation Administration Act 1953 , where either:
(a) 根據《1953 年稅務管理法》第 IVC 部分，這是一項可審查的反對決定，其中：
(i) the application states that the amount that the applicant considers to be the amount of tax in dispute is less than $5,000; or
(i) 申請書中註明，申請人認為爭議稅款金額低於 5,000 美元；或
(ii) after the application is made, but before the start of the hearing of the application, the applicant notifies the Tribunal in writing that the amount that the applicant considers to be the amount of tax in dispute is less than $5,000; or
(ii) 提出申請後，但在申請聽證會開始之前，申請人以書面通知仲裁庭，申請人認為爭議稅款金額少於 5,000 美元；或
(b) that is a decision refusing a request for an extension of time within which to make a taxation objection under section 14ZX of the Taxation Administration Act 1953 .
(b) 該決定拒絕根據《1953 年稅務管理法》第 14ZX 條提出稅務異議延長期限的請求。

注意：該費用已在第 33 條下索引。

優惠情況下的費用
(4) However, the fee of $100 is prescribed instead of the amount referred to in subsection (1), (2) or (3) if any of the circumstances in subsection 29(1) exist.

title: 23 No additional fee for application referred to the guidance and appeals panel
zh: 23 提交給指導和上訴小組的申請無需額外費用
path: Subdivision B — Applications to the Tribunal
text:
No fee is payable in respect of an application that a person is taken to have made to the Tribunal under subsection 130(2) of the Act.
對於根據該法第 130(2) 款向法庭提出的申請，無需支付任何費用。
Note: Under subsection 130(2) of the Act, a person may be taken to have made an application to the Tribunal if the President refers a decision to the guidance and appeals panel under section 128 of the Act. No fee is payable for the application that the person is taken to have made (although a fee may be payable for the application under section 123 of the Act that resulted in the President making the referral—see Subdivision C of this Division).
註：根據該法第 130(2) 款，如果總統根據該法第 128 條將決定提交給指導和上訴小組，則可能被視為已向法庭提出申請。該人被視為已提出的申請無需繳納任何費用（儘管根據該法案第 123 條導致總統做出轉介的申請可能需要繳納費用 - 參見本分部 C 分部）。

title: 24 Consequence if application not accompanied by prescribed fee
zh: 24 申請未附上規定費用的後果
path: Subdivision B — Applications to the Tribunal
text:
(1) If an application is not accompanied by the prescribed fee, the Tribunal is not required to deal with the application unless, and until, the fee is paid.
(1) 若申請未附有規定的費用，仲裁庭無需處理該申請，除非且直至繳納費用。
(2) For the purposes of section 98 of the Act, the time by which the fee must be paid is the end of the 6 weeks starting on the day the application is made.
(2) 就該法第 98 條而言，必須繳交費用的時間是自提出申請之日起 6 週結束時。
Note: The Tribunal may dismiss the application under that section if the fee is not paid by that time.
注意：如果屆時未支付費用，仲裁庭可以駁回該條規定的申請。

title: 25 Consequences if the Tribunal considers that the amount in dispute is not less than $5,000
zh: 25 如果仲裁庭認為爭議金額不少於 5,000 美元的後果
path: Subdivision B — Applications to the Tribunal
text:
(1) If:
(1) 如果：
(a) an applicant paid the fee mentioned in subsection 22(3) on the basis that the applicant considers that the amount of tax in dispute is less than $5,000; and
(a) 申請人認為爭議稅款金額低於 5,000 美元，因此支付了第 22(3) 款所述的費用；和
(b) the Tribunal considers that the amount of tax in dispute is not less than $5,000;
(b) 仲裁庭認為爭議稅款金額不少於 5,000 美元；
then the Tribunal may make an order declaring that the prescribed fee in respect of the application is:
則審裁處可作出命令，宣布與申請有關的訂明費用為：
(c) the fee prescribed by subsection 22(1); or
(c) 第 22(1) 款規定的費用；或
(d) if the Tribunal considers that subsection 22(2) applies in relation to the application—the fee prescribed by that subsection; or
(d) 若仲裁庭認為第 22(2) 款適用於該申請－該項規定的費用；或
(e) if any of the circumstances in subsection 29(1) exist—the fee prescribed by subsection 22(4).
(e) 若有第29(1)款的任何一種情況－第22(4)款規定的費用。
(2) If the applicant paid less than the fee declared by the Tribunal, the amount payable by the applicant is reduced by the amount paid.
(2) 如果申請人支付的費用少於仲裁庭宣布的費用，則申請人應支付的金額減去已支付的金額。
Note: For refunds of excess amounts, see item 2 of the table in subsection 32(1).
附註：有關超額退款，請參閱第 32(1) 款表中的第 2 項。
Consequence if fee not paid
未繳費用的後果
(3) The Tribunal is not required to deal with the application unless, and until, the fee is paid.
(3) 除非且直至費用已支付，仲裁庭無須處理該申請。
(4) For the purposes of section 98 of the Act, the time by which the fee must be paid is the end of the 6 weeks starting on the day the order is made.
(4) 就該法第 98 條而言，必須支付費用的時間為自下達命令之日起 6 週結束時。
Note: The Tribunal may dismiss the application under that section if the fee is not paid by that time.
注意：如果屆時未支付費用，仲裁庭可以駁回該條規定的申請。

title: 26 Consequences if the Tribunal considers that an applicant is not a small business entity
zh: 26 如果仲裁庭認為申請人不是小型企業實體的後果
path: Subdivision B — Applications to the Tribunal
text:
(1) If:
(1) 如果：
(a) an applicant paid the fee mentioned in subsection 22(2) on the basis that a decision related to a small business entity; and
(a) 申請人根據與小型企業實體相關的決定支付了第 22(2) 款中提到的費用；和

(b) 仲裁庭認為該決定與小型企業實體無關；
then the Tribunal may make an order declaring that the prescribed fee in respect of the application is:
則審裁處可作出命令，宣布與申請有關的訂明費用為：
(c) the fee prescribed by subsection 22(1); or
(c) 第 22(1) 款規定的費用；或
(d) if the Tribunal considers that subsection 22(3) applies in relation to the application—the fee prescribed by that subsection; or
(d) 若仲裁庭認為第 22(3) 條適用於該申請－該項規定的費用；或
(e) if any of the circumstances in subsection 29(1) exist—the fee prescribed by subsection 22(4).
(e) 若有第29(1)款的任何一種情況－第22(4)款規定的費用。
(2) If the applicant paid less than the fee declared by the Tribunal, the amount payable by the applicant is reduced by the amount paid.
(2) 如果申請人支付的費用少於仲裁庭宣布的費用，則申請人應支付的金額減去已支付的金額。
Note: For refunds of excess amounts, see item 2 of the table in subsection 32(1).
附註：有關超額退款，請參閱第 32(1) 款表中的第 2 項。
Consequence if fee not paid
未繳費用的後果
(3) The Tribunal is not required to deal with the application unless, and until, the fee is paid.
(3) 除非且直至費用已支付，仲裁庭無須處理該申請。
(4) For the purposes of section 98 of the Act, the time by which the fee must be paid is the end of the 6 weeks starting on the day the order is made.
(4) 就該法第 98 條而言，必須支付費用的時間為自下達命令之日起 6 週結束時。

注意：如果屆時未支付費用，仲裁庭可以駁回該條規定的申請。

title: Subdivision C — Applications to the President

path: Subdivision C — Applications to the President

title: 27 Fees for applications to the President

Standard application fee
標準申請費

優惠情況下的費用

title: 28 Consequence if application not accompanied by prescribed fee
zh: 28 申請未附上規定費用的後果
path: Subdivision C — Applications to the President
text:
(1) If an application is not accompanied by the prescribed fee, the President is not required to deal with the application unless, and until, the fee is paid.
(1) 若申請未附有規定的費用，則主席無需處理該申請，除非並直至繳納費用。

title: 29 Concessional circumstances
text:
(1) For the purposes of subsection 22(4), paragraphs 25(1)(e) and 26(1)(e) and subsection 27(2), the circumstances are the following:
(1) 就第 22(4) 款、第 25(1)(e) 款和第 26(1)(e) 款以及第 27(2) 款而言，情況如下：
(a) the applicant has been granted legal aid for the matter to which the fee relates under a legal aid scheme or service:
(a) 申請人已根據法律援助計劃或服務就與費用相關的事項獲得法律援助：
(i) established under a law of the Commonwealth or of a State or Territory; or
(i) 根據澳洲聯邦或州或領地的法律成立；或
(ii) approved by the Attorney ‑ General;
(ii) 經總檢察長批准；
(b) the applicant is the holder of any of the following cards issued by the Commonwealth:
(b) 申請人是聯邦發行的以下任何卡片的持有者：
(i) a health care card;
(i) 醫療保健卡；
(ii) a pensioner concession card;
(ii) 退休金領取者優惠卡；
(iii) a Commonwealth seniors health card;
(iii) 英聯邦老年人健康卡；
(iv) any other card that certifies the holder’s entitlement to Commonwealth health concessions;
(iv) 證明持有人有權享有聯邦健康優惠的任何其他卡片；
(c) the applicant is serving a sentence of imprisonment or is otherwise detained in a public institution, or is in immigration detention (within the meaning of the Migration Act 1958 );
(c) 申請人正在服刑或以其他方式被拘留在公共機構中，或處於移民拘留中（根據 1958 年移民法的含義）；
(d) the applicant is younger than 18;
(d) 申請人未滿 18 歲；
(e) the applicant is receiving youth allowance or Austudy payments under the Social Security Act 1991 or benefits under the ABSTUDY scheme;
(e) 申請人正在根據《1991 年社會安全法》領取青年津貼或 Austudy 付款，或根據 ABSTUDY 計劃領取福利；
(f) the Principal Registrar makes an order that, having regard to the applicant’s income, expenses, liabilities and assets, the Principal Registrar considers that the payment of an amount would cause, or has caused, financial hardship to the applicant.
(f) 主註冊官在考慮了申請人的收入、開支、負債和資產後，作出命令認為支付一筆款項將會或已經對申請人造成經濟困難。
(2) For the purposes of paragraph (1)(b), the holder of a card does not include a dependant of the person who is issued the card.
(2) 就第 (1)(b) 款而言，持卡人不包括持卡人的家屬。

title: 31 Multiple applications
text:
(1) The Principal Registrar may order that only one prescribed fee is payable in respect of 2 or more applications if:
(1) 在下列情況下，主註冊官可命令僅就 2 項或以上申請繳納一項規定費用：
(a) apart from this subsection, the same prescribed fee would be payable in respect of each of the applications; and
(a) 除本款外，每項申請均須繳納相同的規定費用；和
(b) the applications relate to:
(b) 申請涉及：
(i) the same applicant; or
(i) 同一申請人；或

(2) If the Principal Registrar makes a decision of that kind, the Principal Registrar must give to the person liable to pay the fee the following things in writing:
(2) 如果首席註冊官做出此類決定，則首席註冊官必須向負責支付費用的人提供以下書面資料：

title: Endnote 1—About the endnotes
text:
The endnotes provide information about this compilation and the compiled law.
尾註提供了有關本彙編和已彙編法律的資訊。
The following endnotes are included in every compilation:
每個彙編中都包含以下尾註：
Endnote 1—About the endnotes
尾註 1——關於尾註
Endnote 2—Abbreviation key
尾註 2——縮寫鍵
Endnote 3—Legislation history
尾註 3——立法歷史
Endnote 4—Amendment history
尾註 4——修改歷史
Abbreviation key—Endnote 2
縮寫鍵－尾註 2
The abbreviation key sets out abbreviations that may be used in the endnotes.
縮寫鍵列出了尾註中可能使用的縮寫。
Legislation history and amendment history—Endnotes 3 and 4
立法歷史和修訂歷史—尾註3和4
Amending laws are annotated in the legislation history and amendment history.
修改法律在立法史和修改史都有註釋。
The legislation history in endnote 3 provides information about each law that has amended (or will amend) the compiled law. The information includes commencement details for amending laws and details of any application, saving or transitional provisions that are not included in this compilation.
尾註 3 中的立法歷史提供了已修訂（或將修訂）法律彙編的每項法律的資訊。這些資訊包括修訂法律的開始細節以及本彙編中未包含的任何應用、保存或過渡條款的詳細資訊。
The amendment history in endnote 4 provides information about amendments at the provision (generally section or equivalent) level. It also includes information about any provision of the compiled law that has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law.
尾註 4 中的修訂歷史記錄提供了有關條款（通常是章節或同等級別）級別修訂的資訊。它還包括有關已根據法律條款廢除的已編纂法律的任何條款的資訊。
Editorial changes
編輯修改
The Legislation Act 2003 authorises First Parliamentary Counsel to make editorial and presentational changes to a compiled law in preparing a compilation of the law for registration. The changes must not change the effect of the law. Editorial changes take effect from the compilation registration date.
《2003 年立法法》授權第一議會律師在準備登記法律彙編時對已彙編的法律進行編輯和表述上的修改。變更不得改變法律的效力。編輯修改自編譯註冊之日起生效。
If the compilation includes editorial changes, the endnotes include a brief outline of the changes in general terms. Full details of any changes can be obtained from the Office of Parliamentary Counsel.
如果彙編包含編輯性更改，則尾註包括通用術語更改的簡要概述。任何變更的完整細節可以從議會法律顧問辦公室獲得。
Misdescribed amendments
錯誤描述的修正案
A misdescribed amendment is an amendment that does not accurately describe how an amendment is to be made. If, despite the misdescription, the amendment can be given effect as intended, then the misdescribed amendment can be incorporated through an editorial change made under section 15V of the Legislation Act 2003 .
錯誤描述的修正案是指沒有準確描述如何進行修正案的修正案。儘管有錯誤描述，如果修正案能夠如預期生效，那麼可以根據《2003 年立法法》第 15V 條進行編輯修改，將錯誤描述的修正案納入其中。
If a misdescribed amendment cannot be given effect as intended, the amendment is not incorporated and “(md not incorp)” is added to the amendment history.
如果錯誤描述的修正案無法如預期生效，則該修正案不會被納入，並且「（md not incorp）」將添加到修正案歷史中。
